544731|2026-09.headline: Rajputana Stainless Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR360 crore and PAT 79% to INR23.7 crore, with operating cash flow weak at INR4.5 crore in H1.
544731|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 33% YoY to INR360 crore, with operating EBITDA up 38% to INR33.4 crore (9.3% margin) and PAT up 79% to INR23.7 crore. H1 revenue was INR666 crore and H1 PAT INR43.9 crore, up 80%, and management said H1 PAT was about 88% of FY26 full-year PAT. The company is debt-free after IPO proceeds were used to repay debt, and capacity utilisation is reported at over 99%. Cash conversion weakened, with H1 operating cash flow of about INR4.5 crore, mainly absorbed by receivables as the company shifted from trader channels to direct end-user sales with 60-90 day terms.

financial_highlights.value: INR232-242 crore (figure quoted inconsistently in call)

financial_highlights.change: debtor days said to be up 3-4 days

financial_highlights.metric: Order book at start of H2
financial_highlights.value: about INR500 crore, including over INR80 crore aerospace and defence

segments.name: Aerospace and defence
segments.commentary: Over INR80 crore of the INR500 crore order book; company recently aerospace-certified and has begun supplying defence companies abroad. Management said quantities were broadly flat but higher-grade mix lifted revenue and profit, and does not track exact revenue share.

segments.name: Seamless pipes (new vertical)
segments.commentary: Planned entry into seamless pipe production with a B2B bar product to supply seamless pipe makers; the INR18.57 crore IPO-funded allocation is still unutilised. Management cited a seamless-pipe industry size of about 2.1 lakh tonnes/year growing about 15% a year, with plants at about 85% utilisation.

segments.name: Bright bar
segments.commentary: Bright bar capacity of 6,000 tonnes is about 60% utilised, per management.

segments.name: Melt and rolling
segments.commentary: Billet (melting) utilisation at 99% and rolled products at 99.45% in Q2; company describes itself as running at full capacity.

guidance_outlook: Melting capacity to rise from 48,000 tonnes to 60,000 tonnes, with commissioning expected in Q4 FY27 (calendar 2026-27 Q4 as stated).
Solar captive plants expected to start by end of calendar 2026, with power cost savings from 1 January 2027; windmill production targeted for end-March (2027).
Capacity expansion to be funded by internal accruals; management said no additional working capital is needed until about 60,000 tonnes, when some may be required.
Management expects free cash flow to be positive for the full year.
Long-term vision of about 2 lakh tonnes of capacity by 2031, described as 4-5 years away.
Management expects a positive EBITDA margin trend over the next three to four quarters.
Seamless pipe unit reported target of 80% utilisation in its first year; management said it has soft inquiries but no firm commitments were stated.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 48,000 tonnes melting, 36,000 tonnes rolling and 6,000 tonnes bright bar; over 80 grades and 5,000+ SKUs.
Expansion from 48,000 to 60,000 tonnes melting targeted for Q4 FY27, about a 25% increase, funded by internal accruals.
Seamless pipe vertical: INR18.57 crore of IPO proceeds still unused as of 30 September; delay attributed to sourcing the latest machinery intended to last 25-30 years.
Solar plants to cover captive power needs from 1 January 2027; windmill production targeted for end-March; power is about 80% of power cost covered by these projects.
Management said it is reconsidering the seamless machine order to a higher-end unit with greater output.
demand_pricing: Order-based (make-to-order) model with raw material hedged against each order; scrap sourcing about 39% imported, with management saying Indian buyers are favoured as the world exports scrap to India.
Consumables not hedged, estimated at about 10-12% of raw material cost; management said gross profit rose about 22% in Q2 despite higher other costs.
Management said prices are customer-specific and not standardised, supporting margins.
Demand drivers cited: AI-related machinery fasteners/components (mainly US demand), oil and gas repair work, and defence and aerospace.
Management said there is a large inquiry pipeline for seamless pipes from the Middle East, Europe and US, but did not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q2 production and capacity utilisation figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation was over 99% and continuous for two years: billets 99%, rolled products 99.45%, bright bar about 60%. Revenue growth was attributed to a richer specialty grade mix rather than volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 operating cash flow only about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash went into working capital, mainly receivables, as the company shifted from trader channels to direct end-users such as BHEL and L&T, who pay on 60-90 day terms. Debtor days were said to be up only 3-4 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and how much more working capital will growth need?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable cycle about 52 days; payables said to be under 10 days (not certain). Expansion to 60,000 tonnes to be funded by internal accruals, with working capital needs possible only beyond that level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and why is the IPO money for the seamless pipe plant still unspent?
qa_highlights.answer: Two verticals: capacity expansion to 60,000 tonnes and a consumer-facing seamless pipe entry. Management said INR18.57 crore is unused for the seamless plant because it is waiting for the latest machinery, and about INR4 crore of other IPO funds is also unused.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR34.5 crore loan and advance a related-party transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vishal Vijayvargiya said it is not a related-party loan but an inter-corporate deposit that carries interest.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY despite raw material hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only consumables (about 10-12% of raw material cost) cannot be hedged; other costs grew faster than sales, which kept EBITDA margin gains small (9.0% to 9.3%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the import share of scrap, and are there logistics issues?
qa_highlights.answer: About 39% of scrap is imported. Management said there have been delays, but ongoing contracts with dealers have avoided disruption, and transit costs have been absorbed by scrap sellers.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the seamless pipe market and what are the entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated industry size at about 2.1 lakh tonnes/year growing about 15% a year, with plants at about 85% utilisation. It said technical know-how and metallurgy are the main entry barriers, and that the company's scrap-to-finished-pipe integration is an advantage.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow of about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore; receivables rising with direct end-user sales on 60-90 day terms.
Commissioning risk on the 48,000 to 60,000 tonne expansion (Q4 FY27) and the solar and windmill projects (targeted end-2026 and end-March).
The INR18.57 crore seamless-pipe allocation is unspent and timing has slipped; the target of 80% utilisation in year one is unsupported by disclosed commitments.
Gross margin decline YoY despite hedging; cost growth above sales growth.
Management did not quantify aerospace and defence revenue share; figures for receivables were quoted inconsistently (INR232 crore vs INR242 crore).
544731|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, demand and the seamless pipe opportunity, with frequent use of superlatives. More cautious on cash conversion and capex timing, where answers were partial and some figures were corrected on the call.
key_quotes: So we are not in the race of producing more. We are in the race of producing the right product for the right customer at the right price.
We have taken the route of directly going to the end-user base, which has ensured that our receivable timings have increased

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Melting capacity rise from 48,000 t to 60,000 t (about 25%) is under construction with commissioning guided for Q4 FY27 and funded by internal accruals; solar captive plants are due from 1 Jan 2027.

rows.why: Utilisation is 99% on billets and rolled products, so volume can only grow with the 60,000 t expansion; management attributed Q2 revenue growth of 33% to richer grade mix rather than volume, and bright bar sits at about 60% utilisation.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation has run at 99% for two years and management is reconsidering the seamless machine order to a higher-output unit, with INR18.57 crore of IPO money still unspent for the seamless vertical.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric revenue guidance, but H1 PAT of INR43.9 crore is about 88% of FY26 full-year PAT and the order book is about INR500 crore at start of H2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was only about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore, receivable days are rising on 60-90 day direct terms, and commissioning of the Q4 FY27 expansion and solar projects could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Seamless pipe B2B bar entry is planned with INR18.57 crore unspent and machinery sourcing delayed, and the 80% year-one utilisation target is not backed by firm commitments.

rows.label: Solar and windmill captive power
rows.why: Solar plants to cover captive power from 1 Jan 2027 and windmills targeted end-March, together covering about 80% of power cost, which should lower power cost and support margins.

rows.label: Free cash flow turns positive for FY27
rows.why: Management says FCF will be positive for the full year, but H1 operating cash flow was only about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore and receivables are about INR232-242 crore, up from about INR132-137 crore.

rows.label: Seamless pipe export inquiries
rows.why: Management cites a large inquiry pipeline from the Middle East, Europe and US for seamless pipes but did not quantify it, and no firm commitments were stated.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, utilisation and the 60,000 t expansion, but cautious and partial on cash conversion, the unspent IPO money and gross margin, with some figures corrected on the call; analysts pressed on working capital, related-party loans and margin decline.

544733|2026-06.headline: GSP Crop Science Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR386 crore (from INR377 crore) and PAT grew about 16% to INR26.4 crore, helped by a one-off land sale gain.
544733|2026-06.overview: Revenue was broadly stable at INR386 crore versus INR377 crore in the prior-year quarter, with strong domestic momentum partly offset by raw material constraints in international business. Gross margin improved on a richer mix of specialty and patented products, and EBITDA was stated at around 11%. PAT rose almost 16% to INR26.4 crore, but management said about INR5.7 crore of other income came from a land sale, which is a one-off. ICRA upgraded the long-term rating from A to A+ stable, citing IPO-funded debt repayment and performance.

segments.name: Domestic B2C (branded)
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C sales; management aims to roughly double this over 3 years. Recent launches PCT 410 and Fighter are gaining volume.

segments.name: Domestic B2B
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Co-marketing of patented products with B2B partners showed good growth. Management targets B2B at 30-35% of revenue over the next 3 years.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: About 10% of Q1 revenue, seasonally weighted to H2 (Latin America, mainly Brazil). Q1 hit by raw material constraints, order slippage to China, and Brazil credit and liquidity concerns. Expected to be about 20% of mix over 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 15% growth rate, with EBITDA growing 13-14% over the next 2-3 years (earlier in the call, EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% was given).

Management expects the Q2 season to track anticipated growth; PAT in Q2 is expected to be a similar share of full-year PAT as last year (Q2 FY26 was about 60% of full-year PAT), with the absolute number higher.
Management expects Brazil demand to recover from September for H2 ahead of the October season.
Management targets a domestic market share rise from about 3-3.5% to 7-8%.

Management says patented product share of the portfolio will double in 2-3 years, with about 12 products launched in the last 3 years and two to three new patented formulations and one or two technicals a year.
capex_capacity: Technical capacity utilisation is about 70-75%, with room to grow and scope to swap high-value, low-volume products in multi-product plants.
Formulation plant utilisation is about 25-30%; management says formulations are sized for peak season and are not a bottleneck.
Backward-integration technical plant at Dahej and Saykha was capitalised after the prior quarter, raising depreciation.
Technical plant can run 12 months to supply H2 export demand from Latin America.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices were volatile in Q1 due to geopolitical events and petrochemical-linked inputs. Rupee depreciation of about 10-11% also raised input costs. Management said B2B prices can be passed on, while B2C has a lag covered by inventory.
Demand was held back by price volatility, with farmers, channel partners and formulators delaying purchases. Management cited El Nino forecasts and crude volatility.
Monsoon rains from July were good; cotton and soybean acreage is up and chillies are increasing. Management expects insecticide and fungicide demand to benefit.

Brazil demand is weak with customer liquidity and credit issues, and some orders moved to China on logistics. Management is cautious and is focusing on established B2B partners and second-tier distributors in Argentina and Uruguay.
Management says farmers are moving to specialty molecules and preventive spraying. It cited West Bengal as an example.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix between technicals, formulations and branded patented products?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel mix is about 45% B2C, 45% B2B and 10% export. Formulations are about 75% and technicals about 25%. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C, with a target to double over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of IPO fund utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The loan repayment object has been fully met during the quarter. A small residual amount remains pending bank settlement of brokerage, which may take 2-3 months, before the IPO account can be closed.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material costs affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion is mainly from product mix. Rupee depreciation of 10-11% and petrochemical-linked price volatility raised input costs. B2B passes costs through, and B2C is covered by inventory for now.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q1 export business faring and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Brazil orders were delayed by pricing volatility and some shifted to China. Management expects destocking, with demand returning from September for the October season. It is pursuing Argentina and Uruguay via second-tier distributors and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kharif progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: July rains were good and key kharif acreage is up. Management said South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) is still a wait-and-watch situation based on monsoon. No material shortage is seen currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical utilisation is about 70-75% with scope to add high-value products. Formulation utilisation is about 25-30%, which management says is by design for peak-season capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The company plans one or two new technicals a year, with data generation taking 4-5 years, and two to three new patented formulations a year, with a pipeline covering the next 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off nature of other income and the outlook for it?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR5.7 crore of the INR8.3 crore other income is the land-sale gain. No further other income is planned for the remaining quarters. Management said the land sale is a one-off.

risks_watch: Other income of about INR5.7 crore from a one-off land sale inflated Q1 PAT. Excluding it, management's PAT growth looks much lower, and the analyst cited roughly flat PBT.
Raw material volatility and rupee depreciation of 10-11% could compress B2C margins if pass-through lags.
Brazil credit and liquidity stress, plus loss of orders to China on logistics, puts export recovery at risk. Export is about 10% of Q1 revenue.
South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) depends on monsoon, and the El Nino forecast adds uncertainty.
Management guidance is inconsistent: EBITDA margin 12-13% in one answer, EBITDA growth 13-14% in another, and PAT growth expectations are not quantified. Monitor Q2 delivery against these.
544733|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on domestic patented product growth and the mix shift, but cautious on export, particularly Brazil. Management was less precise on margin and growth figures, sometimes giving different numbers across answers.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR377 crore in Q1 FY26 (as stated by management)
vs INR26 million last year; about INR5.7 crore is land-sale gain

financial_highlights.value: up about 240 bps (per analyst question, not disputed by management)
Domestic B2C about 45%, domestic B2B about 45%, export about 10%

key_quotes: Overall, the financial performance in Q1 FY27 was stable, especially considering the volatile operations environments.
So, from an EBITDA level what we see that we can expect it to grow around 13% to 14% in the upcoming 2 years to 3 years.

This is a one-off event which we don't expect in the remaining three quarters, but the remaining three quarters we see that as per the, you know, expectation we see that the business would grow based on the operational efficiencies that we see.
We expect the branded business to go to 45%-50% whereas remaining say 30%-35% will be then the B2B business.
Brazil, we are seeing we are a bit cautious also because we have seen liquidity issues in Brazil where is the credit is also a challenge.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin rose about 240 bps on a richer specialty and patented mix and management guides EBITDA margin at 12-13%, but Q1 EBITDA was about 11% and rupee depreciation of 10-11% plus petrochemical volatility could squeeze B2C margins if pass-through lags.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Technical utilisation is about 70-75% with room to grow via product swaps in multi-product plants, and formulation utilisation is only 25-30%, so no new plant or line is guided within the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Good July rains have lifted cotton and soybean acreage, management expects Q2 to track anticipated growth, and it targets domestic market share rising from about 3-3.5% to 7-8% over the medium term, although Q1 revenue grew only about 2.4%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Technical utilisation at 72.5% is below the 80%+ threshold that would force a capex call, and the Dahej and Saykha backward-integration plant was just capitalised, so a new capex announcement is only a conditional possibility if utilisation climbs.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management has only given a medium-term ~15% revenue growth goal, with no raised near-term numbers, and Q1 underlying growth was weak once the INR5.7 crore land-sale gain is excluded.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Brazil export (about 10% of Q1 revenue) faces credit and liquidity stress and order loss to China, Q1 revenue rose only about 2.4% (INR386 crore vs INR377 crore), and management's margin and growth guidance is inconsistent across answers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans two to three new patented formulations and one or two technicals a year, after about 12 products in the last 3 years, and recent PCT 410 and Fighter launches are gaining volume.

rows.label: Land-sale one-off inflates Q1 PAT
rows.why: About INR5.7 crore of the INR8.3 crore other income is a one-off land-sale gain with no further other income planned, so underlying PAT growth is far below the reported ~16%.

rows.label: Brazil export recovery from September
rows.why: Management expects Brazil demand to recover from September ahead of the October season, but export is only about 10% of revenue and customer credit and liquidity stress remain unresolved.

rows.label: IPO fund use and ICRA upgrade to A+
rows.why: The loan repayment objective is fully met and ICRA upgraded the long-term rating from A to A+ stable, though about INR small residual IPO funds await 2-3 months of bank settlement before the account closes.

tone.note: Management was confident on patented products, the domestic mix shift and the good monsoon, but cautious on Brazil export and vague on margin and growth figures, giving different EBITDA numbers across answers; analysts pushed on the one-off other income and underlying PAT growth.

544735|2026-03.headline: Novus Loyalty FY26 revenue rose about 22% to ~127 Cr, with PAT of ~9.28 Cr (7.29% margin) in its first results call after its 25 March 2026 listing.
544735|2026-03.overview: Novus Loyalty, a B2B2C loyalty and engagement technology company, reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) revenue of about 127 Cr, up roughly 22% YoY. EBITDA was about 12.33 Cr (9.68% margin) and PAT about 9.28 Cr (7.29% margin), with management citing PAT growth of about 150% and EBITDA growth of about 120%. Management attributed margin improvement to programs maturing (redemptions rising in years 2 to 3) and a shift toward technology and merchant-promotion revenue, which carry no direct procurement cost. Management guided to growth above 20% in FY27 and to international revenue at least doubling, but gave no formal numerical guidance, and the call was largely promotional with limited hard data.

financial_highlights.change: listed 25 March 2026; no proceeds utilised in FY26

segments.name: Technology
segments.commentary: Enterprise platform set-up fee and the first revenue line to open with a client; management says it carries no direct cost and is the main focus. Cited Central Bank order worth 88 Cr (via GeM) and Bank of Abyssinia technology revenue of about 4 Cr.

segments.name: Redemption
segments.commentary: Second revenue line, opening after technology in BFSI programs; carries a direct procurement cost. Management cited a client where redeeming customers rose from about 10,000 to 10 lakh within 10 months.

segments.name: Merchant promotions
segments.commentary: Merchants fund accelerated campaigns and pay affiliate commissions, which management said run at about 8-10% of tracked spend, of which part is passed to customers. Described as a higher-margin line with no direct cost.

segments.name: Digital vouchers
segments.commentary: Fourth line; vouchers sourced partly from vendors such as Gyftr. Carries direct procurement cost. Management said the voucher line is about 5% of Gyftr's business in its comparison.

guidance_outlook: Management said FY27 growth will be above 20%, but gave no revenue number.

International revenue to at least double from about 3.3 Cr in FY26, 'if not triple'. Management cited about 5 Cr for FY27 and more than 6 Cr in one answer, then 'close to 10' / 'more than 10' for FY27-28, which is internally inconsistent.
India growth expected at 15-20%.
Margins expected to rise from current levels as the mix shifts toward technology and merchant promotion.
IPO proceeds planned as about 11-12 Cr for sales and business development (about half in FY27), about 10-12 Cr for product development and AI, and about 12 Cr for small acquisitions.
Bank accounts onboarded recently, such as Central Bank, are expected to reach peak levels in FY27, which management said could increase numbers by 100%.
capex_capacity: Planned UAE wholly owned subsidiary, expected to be finalised in about a month; physical presence to serve MENA clients.
Two partners onboarded in Africa, with workshops started; Bank of Abyssinia (Ethiopia) order is the first such contract.

Planned acquisition of a small marketing agency or digital agency in the US and Australia, targeted this year or next, subject to finding the right candidate. Management also cited a PPI licence as a possible acquisition target.
Hiring additional sales staff in India for channel partner and corporate loyalty programs; management said BFSI needs no extra staff.
Platform scales from 10,000 to 100 million customers, with SaaS launch in about 2-3 weeks and on-premise deployment for banks.
demand_pricing: Over 100 enterprise customers and more than 4 crore end-customers on the platform; about 50 crore transactions processed per month; about 80 employees.
Clients include NPCI (since 2019), Central Bank, IDBI, Bank of Maharashtra, Equitas Bank, Sparkle Bank (Nigeria), PRYPCO (DAMAC) and NovaDisk (healthcare, 3 countries).
Contracts run 3-5 years with 3-5 year renewals (6-10 year total tenure). Programs typically mature in year 3, and management said margins rise over the program life.
Competition: management named Salesforce and other large loyalty players in the Bank of Abyssinia tender; said its platform processes transactions in 8 hours versus 24 hours for others.
Redemption rates in Indian bank programs are about 10%, against 45-50% in the US and Australia, which management cited as upside.
Management said seasonality has a 5-10% effect, mainly around September-October festive months.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth exceed 20% in FY27, and what revenue is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth would be 'more than' 20% and that IPO-funded sales and international expansion would grow the business faster than FY26, but gave no revenue figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~10% margins sustainable, or were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would increase from current levels as technology and merchant promotion revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: How will IPO proceeds be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately 11-12 Cr for business development and sales, about 10-12 Cr for product development and AI, and about 12 Cr for small acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Does Novus keep breakage on expired points, and what about gift points?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Novus is B2B2C and breakage goes to the bank client; it does not hold a PPI licence, so it cannot keep breakage. Management said Indian bank points expiry is about 7-10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international revenue mix and reseller economics?
qa_highlights.answer: International revenue was about 2.6% of FY26 revenue (about 3.3 Cr). Resellers take about 15-30% of the deal value depending on local support needs, and Novus retains IP ownership.

qa_highlights.question: How does Novus compare with Zaggle and Gyftr?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Zaggle focuses on spend management and employee rewards, which are about 5-10% of Novus's business. Gyftr is a voucher vendor to Novus, not a loyalty competitor.

risks_watch: Growth depends on the timing of program maturity and on contract wins, including government/GeM tenders that management said can be cancelled or uneven (Canara order cancelled).
International expansion relies on partners, resellers and a planned US/Australia acquisition, with reseller margins of 15-30% and a licence-dependent PPI plan that is not yet in place.
The FY27 international revenue guidance is internally inconsistent (about 5 Cr, then more than 6 Cr, then 10 Cr or more), so the number needs confirmation.
Concentration in BFSI and a few large bank and government clients; redemption-driven revenue carries direct procurement cost.
Use of IPO proceeds (about 60 Cr raised) has not yet been reported; watch quarterly deployment and the outcome of the planned acquisition.
Management did not give FY26 comparatives in detail; the EBITDA and PAT growth figures (120%, 150%) are management's approximations.

544735|2026-09.headline: Novus Loyalty H1 FY27 revenue rose to about ₹98 crore (vs ₹71 crore in H1 FY26), with ~35-40% growth; AutoPay 80.87% acquisition pending funding in June 2027.

544740|2026-03.headline: Tipco FY26 total income rose 9.5% to INR146 crore, with H2 income up 66% to INR95 crore and PAT up 65% to INR25.31 crore.
544740|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) as its first earnings call after the BSE SME listing on 1 April 2026. Total income was INR146 crore versus INR133 crore, and H2 income reached INR95 crore against INR57 crore in the corresponding period. EBITDA rose 62% to INR38.9 crore, with margin at 26.63% versus 17.95%, and PAT rose 65% to INR25.31 crore with a 17.32% margin. Management guided to Pune plant contributing toward INR180 crore total revenue in FY27, with 25% capacity in FY27, 75% in FY28, and full capacity in about two years. Debtor days rose sharply from 72 to 169, which management attributed to higher H2 sales.

544742|2026-09.headline: Sai Parenterals Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9% QoQ to INR196.1 crore, with gross margin up to 47.5% and EBITDA margin to 21.1%.
544742|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations rose 9% sequentially to INR196.1 crore, with H1 FY27 revenue of INR376 crore against a full-year target of INR750 crore. Gross margin improved from 40.9% to 47.5% as raw material cost fell about 3% on tighter inventory controls, lifting EBITDA 67% QoQ to INR41.4 crore (21.1% margin). Depreciation rose to INR25.1 crore from INR8.1 crore on Noumed and Sai Prathyak asset capitalisation, but PAT still grew 33% QoQ to INR10.5 crore. Management reclassified other income below EBITDA, restating Q1 EBITDA to INR24.7 crore (13.7%). Acquisitions of 60% in Saicriti Pharma and Sai Prathyak Laboratories closed, and the Adelaide and Unit III projects are moving towards operation.

Above 50% of INR750 crore FY27 target

segments.name: Branded generics
segments.commentary: About 27% of Q2 revenue (25% in H1 FY27). Domestic receivables ageing runs 120 to 150 days per management.

segments.name: Export mix
segments.commentary: Australia 76% of export revenue (83% in Q1), Philippines 16% (12% in Q1), South Africa 4%, other markets 3%.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: Private sector 80% of revenue, institutional 20%.

FY27 revenue expected to comfortably cross the INR750 crore target; H2 seasonally stronger.

Adelaide facility commissioning expected January 2027 (slightly behind earlier plan due to Iran-conflict logistics); TGA inspection expected Q2 2027; commercial supply after licence. Inventory at Noumed to fall from 9-10 months towards 5-6 months.

Debt expected to peak in FY26 per management wording and decline from FY28 and FY29; Saicriti project debt drawn at subsidiary level as construction progresses.
capex_capacity: Unit III Bhongir expansion almost complete; new block to start commencing December 2026. Capacity to rise from 85.5 million to 155 million units a month (+81%). Adds high-capacity ointment, high-speed capsule filling and liquid oral lines.

Saicriti Pharma new injectable facility at Gummadidala, targeted completion July 2027. Four process lines ordered (liquid and lyophilised, GLP pre-filled syringe, combi-filling, dry powder, ampoule). Total project cost INR215 crore; Sai contribution INR83.83 crore for 60%; promoters fund 40% of equity; project debt with 3-year moratorium and 7-year repayment. Injectable capacity to reach about 154.66 million units. Jeedimetla Units I and II to be discontinued after commissioning.
Adelaide (Noumed) facility: AUD46 million invested of AUD53 million planned; AUD20 million Modern Manufacturing Initiative grant supports the program.
H1 FY27 capex about INR70 crore, mainly Adelaide and Unit III. Total borrowing INR357 crore at 30 September 2026 vs about INR320 crore in March 2026; cash and equivalents INR129 crore.
Sai Prathyak has 36-molecule annual development capacity and 174 molecules and 285 SKUs in portfolio; 98 in-house dossiers, 45 commercialised and 76 under development targeted for FY28.
demand_pricing: Noumed renewed a 7.5-year exclusive OTC supply contract with EBOS Group (TerryWhite and Pharmacy Choice brands) from 1 July 2026, valued AUD202 million.

Wesfarmers (Priceline and Pharmacy Health) OTC contract renewed on 25 August 2026 for 3 years at AUD30 million (about INR204 crore). Combined contracted Australia OTC book: AUD232 million (about INR1,506 crore).

Philippines: 11 molecules and 22 SKUs added in Q2, mainly cardiovascular. Management said these fall under the existing USD14 million regular contract; the USD11 million anti-TB contract commercials start after January 2027.

Management targets Southeast Asia, Latin America and Middle East for injectables over the next two to three years; no US FDA launch planned for at least two to three years unless a CMO client brings a product.
Management plans to announce oncology mAbs and biosimilars plans (global focus) in about a month, subject to board approval.

qa_highlights.question: Heet (Axis Capital): Any quantitative guidance on sales growth or margins after the strong H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin was the key driver and will be kept above 45%. Unit III output from Q4 and Sai Prathyak revenue from Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28 should take revenue comfortably past INR750 crore and EBITDA margin above 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Amol Rao (Plutus Wealth): Why did receivables rise to about INR250 crore in H1, and what is the ageing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export and CDMO receivables age under 120 days, and domestic branded generics 120-150 days. The Q2 build reflected lower collections from two large export customers and sales bunched in the last 1-1.5 months. Domestic ageing to be below 120 days within two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Amol Rao: Is the 11-molecule Philippines addition part of the USD11 million contract, and what is Sai Prathyak's revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: The 11 molecules were added to the regular USD14 million contract; the USD11 million is a separate anti-TB contract. For Sai Prathyak, management has not yet modelled numbers and promised guidance on the next call.

qa_highlights.question: Murali (individual investor): Will the company pursue US FDA for injectables, and what is the multi-year growth CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: No US FDA launch for at least two to three years; US FDA is an option only for CMO client products. FY28 guidance to come on the next call; no three-year CAGR given.

qa_highlights.question: Gopal Bhatt (Baroda BNP Paribas AM): Why was H1 FY27 operating cash flow negative, and when does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a INR113.1 crore outflow in other financial liabilities for the IPO-linked OFS and about INR49 crore decline in trade payables and current liabilities. Management said H1 FY26 is not comparable because it was standalone only. The call did not reconcile the INR201 crore operating cash outflow figure that the analyst quoted to management's cash flow figures.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavika Singhvi (Niveshaay): How are CDMO partners and products selected, and what are the key challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the three-year plan is backward and forward integration across all dosage forms, with in-house development via Sai Prathyak. Challenges were integration of subsidiaries and capex execution; management is adding senior KMP and expects a further substantial increase in the next three to four months.

544744|2026-03.headline: Powerica FY26 revenue crossed INR3,012 crore (+13.5% YoY) and EBITDA margin was 12.8%; management targets double-digit FY27 top-line growth.
544744|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR801 crore (+10.9% YoY) with EBITDA of INR86 crore (10.8% margin) and PAT of INR45 crore (5.6% margin). Full-year FY26 PAT of INR277 crore (9.2% margin) was helped by a INR51 crore deferred tax credit from a tax regime change. Management said the IPO-related debt repayment of INR525 crore should cut finance costs from Q1 FY27, and cash including investments was about INR450 crore as of May 26. Management flagged geopolitical tensions, energy prices and supply-chain pressure as weighing on near-term demand, especially in Q1 FY27, and said margin pressure seen in Q4 is temporary.

segments.name: DG Sets (Cummins-powered)
segments.commentary: About 83% of FY26 revenue with 10.9% YoY growth and 9.1% EBITDA margin; Cummins-powered DG sets were about 66% of revenue. Data centers were about 12% of the Cummins business, and high-horsepower sets were over 50% of value.

segments.name: MSLG (medium-speed large generators)
segments.commentary: About 5% of FY26 revenue. Project-driven, with revenue tied to execution milestones and project cycles of 12 to 48 months, so management wants it judged over multiple quarters. The Australia project is 90-95% complete.

segments.name: Allied businesses
segments.commentary: EMI shelters, containers, defence applications, acoustic enclosures, Schneider Electric Prisma panels and project work; about 12.5% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Wind (IPP, EPC, O&M for BoP)
segments.commentary: INR512 crore in FY26 (16.9% of revenue), +28.6% YoY with 31.3% EBITDA margin. IPP is about 40% and EPC/O&M about 60% of wind revenue. Owns 12 Gujarat projects with 330.85 MW installed.

segments.name: Platino Automotive (associate)
segments.commentary: Retrofit emission control device (RECD) for pre-CPCB4+ DG sets of 125 kVA and above, cutting emissions by up to 92%; device cost INR3-30 lakh per installation. FY26 was a marketing-infrastructure build year; Q4 sales INR22 crore and PBT INR5.8 crore.

Secured 100 MW of GUVNL bids at Botad, with another 50 MW at advanced planning stage.
Khavda 2 GW RE project with GE Vernova JV is on hold pending land allotment from the Gujarat government.
FY26 capex was 51.3 MW for the business. MSLG needs no capex, as it is a service model.
Manufacturing in Bangalore, Silvassa and Khopoli; everything except the engine and alternator is made in-house.

EPC BoP order book is about 585 MW, including 175 MW in Gujarat (completion expected by Dec 2026) and 410 MW for Torrent Power in Maharashtra; orders run to about Dec 2027.
Wind IPP PPAs are 25-year, fixed-tariff contracts with GUVNL and SECI.
EPC installation work on data centers ranges from 25% to 75% of the supply order value.
Competitive pressure is rising in wind through ROW and land constraints, per management.
Management did not name data center competitors and said it could not quantify the data center share of hyperscaler capex.

qa_highlights.question: What were Platino's Q4 revenue and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Deferred to a later point in the call; Ritesh Agrawal then said Q4 FY26 Platino sales were INR22 crore with PBT of INR5.8 crore (PAT not given).

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins stay at about 10.5% in FY27 after the softer Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the Q3/Q4 dip temporary, citing geopolitical tensions, and expects FY27 to be in target range. It expects better margins from Q2 onward, helped by the 50 MW wind capacity and higher wind generation in the first two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are wind EPC/O&M inquiries facing land and connectivity delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradeep Gupta said the order book covers 585 MW to about Dec 2027, so there is enough work in hand. The 175 MW Gujarat project should complete by Dec 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Khavda 2 GW project timeline and the ROW situation?
qa_highlights.answer: The Khavda project is a long-term JV with GE Vernova and is still waiting for land from the Gujarat government. ROW issues are not improving, as competition and RE investment grow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IPP EBITDA margin and PLF?
qa_highlights.answer: The portfolio's EBITDA margin is about 60-62%. New machines run at 36.5% PLF and older ones at 23-24%, with an average of about 26% across the roughly 280 MW profile. New projects earn about 87-88% EBITDA in year one, stabilising at 82-83%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue split between EPC and IPP, and what growth drivers are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: IPP capacity will grow each year as projects are added, while EPC BoP work of about INR400 crore a year (250-300 MW) is steady. Growth drivers cited are data centers, manufacturing, realty, EV charging backup and rental. Over four to five years the revenue mix is expected at about 75:25 gensets to wind.

qa_highlights.question: How does Powerica view competition from fuel-cell technology such as Bloom Energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would deliver any new technology to market and that gensets stay as backup for 20-25 years. Jai Ram Oberoi said the company is a power solutions provider, not only a DG set maker.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DG set growth outlook, split between price and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic DG growth target is about 11-12% for FY27, with MSLG contributing on a milestone basis. Management did not split price from volume.

qa_highlights.question: Is Platino expected to grow faster than DG sets?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Jai Ram Oberoi said Platino is a small, high-growth business supported by state-level mandates, and FY26 was spent building marketing infrastructure.

Right-of-way and land constraints in wind are unlikely to ease and are raising competition for sites.

544744|2026-06.headline: Powerica Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26.7% YoY to INR780 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 13.6% on commodity inflation; DC order book hit INR900 crore (INR1,100 crore by Aug 7).

544785|2026-03.headline: Hexagon Nutrition FY26 revenue rose 17.8% to INR382.63 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 13.83% and PAT grew 56.1% to INR37.94 crores.

544793|2026-06.headline: Susan Electricals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 279% YoY to ₹95.36 Cr and PAT turned positive at ₹6.39 Cr, with blended operating margin ~11.9%.
544793|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 279% YoY to ₹95.36 Cr and operating profit rose 980% YoY to ₹11.04 Cr, with PAT of ₹6.39 Cr versus a ₹0.42 Cr loss a year earlier. Management attributed the improvement to higher scale, better product mix and higher EBITDA per unit. Management is shifting the mix toward HT/MVCC and LT cables and is adding 4,500 Km p.a. of capacity (+60%) with commercial operations targeted from Feb 2027. Management declined to give a FY27 revenue number, and several answers on margins and product mix were inconsistent between the prepared remarks and the Q&A.

segments.commentary: Management cited ~6.5% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27. Company said winding wires and LT/conductors typically earn 10-15% per unit.

segments.commentary: Management cited ~7% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27. HT/MVCC currently make up ~5-10% of revenue (another answer said 10-15%).

segments.name: Winding wires
segments.commentary: Management cited ~24.39% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27, the highest of the three segments cited.

segments.name: MVCC cables
segments.commentary: Grouped with HT cables by management; no separate margin disclosed. Management targets HT/MVCC potential of ~20% per-unit margin.

guidance_outlook: HT and MVCC share of revenue targeted to rise from ~5-10% toward ~15% by year-end, with 'higher thereafter'. A later answer said ~50% by year-end; this is inconsistent and needs verification.
Expected FY27 revenue mix of roughly 30-35% each across HT/MVCC, LT/conductors and winding wires.
Management expects blended operating margin to be maintained or improved with mix shift and operating leverage.
No absolute FY27 revenue guidance; management said growth momentum will continue and pointed to the last 2-3 years' trajectory.
Capacity expansion on track for commercial operations from Feb 2027, taking capacity from 7,500 Km p.a. to 12,000 Km p.a.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of approximately ₹15-20 Cr, mainly machinery and factory expansion.
Capacity adds 4,500 Km p.a., taking total from 7,500 Km to 12,000 Km p.a. (+60%); commercial operations from Feb 2027.
Management referenced a 'peak capex reference potential' of ~₹700-800 Cr in revenue, which is not clearly defined in the call.
Longer-term plan of aggressive capacity build-out to reach much larger scale in 2-3 years.
demand_pricing: Order book ₹142.39 Cr as of 30 June 2026, with an active pipeline of ₹150 Cr and total visibility of ₹292 Cr.

Bidding ₹800-1,200 Cr of tenders with expected conversion of ~15-20%; several pipeline items are L1/L2 awaiting LOI.
Exploring railways and defence; working on empanelment with power sector companies.
Raw material (aluminium rod) price volatility is handled through 'appropriate pricing mechanisms', with no specifics given.

qa_highlights.answer: LT cables and conductors ~6.5%, HT cables ~7%, winding wires ~24.39% in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said current margins reflect early-stage revenue and that operating leverage will help as volumes scale. HT and MVCC have potential of ~20% net margin at product level, depending on scale and mix.

qa_highlights.answer: About ₹15-20 Cr, mainly machinery and expansion, with factory expansion commissioning in February.

qa_highlights.answer: No absolute number. Management said growth momentum should continue on power-sector demand and pointed to the last 2-3 years' trajectory.

qa_highlights.answer: Overall company EBITDA margin was ~12% in Q1 FY27. Management said product-level margins vary by mix and scale, and a participant's request for more detailed product margin disclosure was acknowledged.

qa_highlights.question: How are aluminium rod price swings managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices are monitored and handled through pricing mechanisms and operational measures, with no quantification.

qa_highlights.answer: No specific plan. Management said it would evaluate funding needs based on growth and expansion.

544793|2026-09.headline: Susan Electricals H1 FY27 revenue rose 190% to ₹202 crore and PAT rose 191% to ₹13.15 crore, while H1 EBITDA margin fell to 11.77% from 13.13%.
544793|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 revenue of ₹202 crore (up 190% YoY from ₹69 crore) and PAT of ₹13.15 crore (up 191% from ₹4.53 crore), with EBITDA up 160% to ₹23.78 crore. The company is shifting its mix toward HT and CCV-based products, with HT share of the Q2 mix reaching about 30% from 0.75% in H1 FY26. Order book stood at ₹147 crore plus ₹200 crore of L1/L2/L3/L4 pipeline. Margins were lower YoY, which management attributed to one-time metal-price gains in H1 FY26 and an expected sustainable 11.5%–12% range. Management flagged a land acquisition and a new plant, with a CCV line commissioning as the key near-term milestone.

segments.name: HT (high tension) cables/conductors
segments.commentary: Share of revenue rose from 0.75% in H1 FY26 to about 30% in Q2 FY27; HT is 54 crore of the 147 crore order book. Q2 EBITDA margin was 13.13%, and management guided HT EBITDA margin at 12%–14%.

segments.name: MV (medium voltage) products
segments.commentary: Management cited 69 crore of order book, the largest component (almost half), and an EBITDA margin of 10%–13%. Q2 EBITDA margin was 11.82%.

segments.name: LT (low tension) cables
segments.commentary: LT share fell from 46% in H1 FY26 to about 31% in Q2 FY27; LT order book is 24 crore; LT EBITDA margin of 9%–11.5%, Q2 at 11%. Company is deliberately reducing LT exposure given competition.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1, citing seasonality (government and EPC targets, with February and March typically stronger) and a healthy pipeline.
Blended EBITDA margin expected in the 11.5%–12% range going forward; management called Q2's 18.18% not sustainable.
Target product mix of 33%-33%-33% across HT, MV and LT, with HT and MV reaching 40%–45% each and LT at 10%–20% over time.
Installed capacity targeted to rise from 7,500 tons to 20,000 tons after the new plant, with the new location expected to be operational around end-FY28 and construction underway.
Management is not giving a specific revenue number for the 347 crore visibility; it said about 90% is scheduled to be executed by March 31, 2027.
capex_capacity: CCV (continuous curing vulcanisation) line has arrived at the factory and is in installation; commissioning is expected in the next few months. CCV is mandatory for HT projects in most states.
Winding-wire capacity is planned to rise from 4,200 tons to 5,500 tons; total manufacturing capacity is targeted at 7,500 tons, with the new plant to take it to 20,000 tons.

A land parcel is being acquired (price about ₹10,000 per sq yard versus ~₹1 lakh per sq yard for UPSIDC area), with plans to shift 1–2 factories there; the funding mix is internal accruals and bank loans.

Current borrowings are backed by ₹48 crore of FDs (including ₹5.62 crore pledged mutual funds) as collateral for cash-credit limits; management expects these to be released once the new land is acquired.
Management said the new facility can be built within 1.5–2 years, with a shift in FY27-28 and FY28-29 ramp-up; sheds are used to speed construction.
Management said CTC (continuously transposed conductor) R&D is underway, with no supply to date; the company will announce when it starts.
demand_pricing: Order book: ₹147 crore as of September 30, 2026, of which HT is ₹54 crore and MV is ₹69 crore, and LT is ₹24 crore. An additional ₹200 crore of L1–L4 bids in progress gives combined visibility of ₹347 crore.
Q2 FY27 executed ₹107 crore against ₹111 crore of new orders won.
Management says it bids for HT tenders now that the CCV line is arriving, and it accepts many L2–L4 bids at its discretion.
Competition in LT has intensified, so management is cutting LT bids; it sees more attractive economics in HT and MV.
Private customers often buy at a base rate with metal-price variation included, while EPC customers are about 90% variation-inclusive. Government payments are 90–95% of receivables.
Customers include transformer manufacturers such as CG, CMI and Hitachi Energy (non-contractual). The company also supplies railways (RVNL, Coalfields).

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from 13.7% to 11.5%, and is 11.5%–12% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY26 included one-time metal-price gains. Adjusting for them, H1 FY27 margin is 11.77% against 13.13% in H1 FY26. FY26 full-year margin was 11.91%, and management expects 11.5%–12% with HT and MV mix gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected HT and MV contribution in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: HT was 30% of Q2 volume, MV 33%, and LT 31%. Management targets HT and MV at 40%–45% each and LT at 10%–20%.

qa_highlights.question: How will the land acquisition and expansion be funded, and will it stress working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding combines internal accruals, bank cash-credit and loans; collateral is ₹48 crore of FDs. Management said there is no stress and the company is cash-flow positive.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash flow positive, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flow turned positive. Of ₹95 crore receivables, ₹25 crore is from September and not yet due, ₹44 crore was collected in October, and about 5% exceeds 180 days.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 seasonally stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said EPC and government targets push activity into October–March, with H2 typically 25%–40% stronger, particularly in February and March.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue exports or new product lines (capacitors, insulators)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no export plans for now; it is focused on HT, MV and LT cables and holds 12 BIS certifications.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the HT certification to 33 kV, CTC and defence?
qa_highlights.answer: HT is up to 33 kV, and the company plans to move to higher voltage levels once the BIS certification is obtained, which takes 2–3 months. CTC production is not yet supplied. The company is not yet a defence supplier.

risks_watch: Margin dilution: Q2 margin was 18.18% with metal-price gains, so H2 margin could be lower if metal prices fall or as LT mix changes.
Working capital: receivables at ₹95 crore and rising; collections and conversion to cash flow remain a management priority.
Execution: CCV line commissioning, HT tender wins and the new plant timeline (FY27-28/FY28-29) are key to the 20,000-ton target.
Funding and collateral: ₹48 crore of FDs backing CC limits; the land deal depends on bank release of collateral and a revaluation.
Disclosure: management corrected Q1 segment margin figures and declined to give specific forward numbers; monthly or quarterly realisation disclosure was requested but not committed.
Dependency on government and EPC payment cycles; MSME bill discounting via TReDS was classified in financing flows and may recur.

544799|2026-06.headline: Turtlemint's first post-listing call: FY26 revenue up 57% to INR 1,098 crores, Q4 first adjusted-EBITDA breakeven quarter (INR 60 crores service EBITDA).
544799|2026-06.overview: Management reported FY26 platform premium of INR 3,868 crores (up 31% YoY) and operating revenue of INR 1,098 crores (up 57%). Service EBITDA rose 70% to INR 142 crores (about 13% of revenue), and Q4 revenue of INR 357 crores (up 42%) delivered the company's first breakeven quarter at adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated basis. Corporate overheads fell to 23% of revenue in FY26 from 38% in FY25, and PAT before exceptional items was INR 129 crores. Management declined formal guidance but said FY27 should be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis and that losses or profitability gaps would improve by more than 40%.

segments.name: Insurance distribution (PoSP / Turtlemint Insurance Broking)
segments.commentary: About 97% of FY26 revenue is commission from the broking subsidiary; PoSP premium grew more than 40% in FY26. General insurance is more than 90% of platform premium (revenue split is 90% GI, 10% non-GI per management); health grew more than 60%.

segments.name: Turtlefin (enterprise)
segments.commentary: Enterprise partners (banks, NBFCs, fintechs) contribute about 20% of platform premium, roughly INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic. Take rate is low, transaction-based, and management called it high margin with no direct variable cost.

segments.name: Adjacencies (mutual funds, loans)
segments.commentary: Mutual fund AUM about INR 1,400 crores through the subsidiary; loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised, recently launched. Non-insurance businesses are about 3% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; board decided not to give future guidance, but management gave directional color.
FY27: management expects to reduce losses or improve profitability by more than 40% and to be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis; each quarter expected to exceed the prior one.
FY27 corporate overheads expected to grow with inflation rather than volumes; no exceptional items expected in FY27.

Medium term (about five years / FY30): service EBITDA expected to rise from 13-14% to about 24-25% of revenue, corporate overheads to fall to sub 5-6% of revenue, giving EBITDA/PBT/PAT of about 18-20% of revenue.
Long-run growth framed as continuing the historical 40%-plus CAGR in revenue and key KPIs; dividend policy possible after one to two years of sustained profitability.
capex_capacity: Balance sheet has few fixed assets (IT equipment, offices); no costs are capitalised, all expensed.
Digital partner base: 93,000+ P3M active at 31 March 2026 (51% CAGR over seven years); about 6.5 lakh verified DPs; 46 insurers (45+ partners per Q&A); coverage across 19,000+ PIN codes.
Turtlemint Academy averages 52,000+ monthly active users and 6,500+ training hours per month; certifies over 5,000 new sellers per month.
Insurance Hub gives paperless policy issuance across 40+ insurers; 8 lakh+ quotes generated daily.
Agentic AI and LLM automation under development for support tickets, renewal calling, claims and activation; more updates promised.
demand_pricing: Growth drivers: recruitment of new DPs (about 80% non-insurance background, mostly under 35) plus productivity gains in existing cohorts (frontline premium productivity up 20%+ YoY).

Health insurance growth above 60-75% helped by affordability tailwinds and GST cuts; commissions were cut in Oct-Dec quarter and management says the platform passed these through without slowing volume.
Renewal rates in Q4 were significantly higher than in the same quarter of the prior year; management says renewal rates are above industry averages.
Insurer concentration is low: top 3 insurers about 22% of business; top 100 DPs generated 4.62% of platform premium.
Claims desk settled over INR 85 crores of delayed or rejected claims in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FY26 premium and revenue growth, and is it sustainable given the high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited DP recruitment and productivity, the renewal book, and health tailwinds; H1 growth was flattered by base effects, Q4 growth (about 42%) is closer to steady state, and management expects historical 40%-plus growth to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How would commission regulation changes affect the business, and how are PoSPs classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the asset-light model incurs costs only after a transaction, so commission changes are passed down, as shown in the Oct-Dec GST period. It could not say how the regulator will classify PoSPs as agents or brokers.

qa_highlights.question: How does Turtlemint recruit DPs amid competition, and what is the TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of DPs come from non-insurance backgrounds with 60-65 profiles; onboarding is digital plus a pan-India branch network. Management did not quantify TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of the enterprise (Turtlefin) business and its take rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Enterprise premium is about 20% of platform premium (about INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic). The take rate is low but volume-based and high margin, since tech is already built and licensed; enterprise growth should accelerate as new accounts go live.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal vs new service EBITDA margin, and renewal share?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal service EBITDA margin is about 2.5-3x the new business margin. Renewal revenue is INR 225 crores; management declined to disclose renewal premium.

qa_highlights.question: Non-insurance revenue share and the other financial products?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-insurance is about 3% of FY26 revenue. Mutual fund AUM is about INR 1,400 crores and loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised; the incremental revenue drops straight to service EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to the 18-20% long-term EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Service EBITDA is 13-14% today and is expected to reach 24-25% in a few years, with corporate overheads held at sub 5-6% of revenue for FY30.

risks_watch: Commission regulation: a forthcoming discussion paper could change commission structures and PoSP classification, which the company has not yet seen.
Base effects: FY27 H2 faces a high base after the strong FY26 growth; Q4 seasonality means profitability is concentrated in the March quarter.
Reliance on the PoSP network: DP productivity, retention and recruitment must keep rising for premium growth.
Disclosure limits: no segment split of GI motor vs health, no renewal premium, no new vs renewal margins; management asked for more time.
Exceptional item of INR 55 crores (non-cash, preference share conversion) recorded in the nine months to December 2025; ESOP cost of INR 25 crores (2.3% of revenue) is expected to fall by FY28.

The platform has the ability to absorb any volatility, and it is able to pass down any cost structure, any commercial structure changes.
Service EBITDA is our measure of profitability after accounting for all the variable cost of our business.

544801|2026-09.headline: GSPL Transmission Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR 290 crore; EBITDA flat at INR 169 crore and company remains debt-free.
544801|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was INR 290 crore, up 8% YoY and 4.5% QoQ, while H1 FY27 revenue was INR 567 crore, up 4.5%. EBITDA (excluding non-operating income) was about INR 169 crore against INR 168 crore a year earlier, with a 58.4% margin; PAT rose about 2% to INR 120 crore. Management reframed volume reporting from physical throughput to contractual volumes, and said it has about INR 3,500 crore of expansion capex (about 700 km, taking the Gujarat network to about 3,600 km) with about INR 300 crore spent in H1. The call was dominated by questions on the capex funding model, tariff review timing, PNGRB appeal, loss-making subsidiaries GIGL and GITL, and capital allocation versus buyback.

segments.commentary: Volumes rose 30% YoY in Q2 FY27, the fastest-growing grid mentioned.

segments.commentary: Volumes rose 16% YoY in Q2 FY27.

segments.commentary: Operates about 1,439 km across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab; combined GIGL and GITL capacity about 44-45 MMSCMD, with utilisation described as low double-digit and breakeven expected in about a couple of years.

segments.name: GITL (JV)
segments.commentary: Operates about 365 km connecting Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; management said it is profitable on a standalone basis, but it is loss-making at the group level per the analyst's framing, and major investment has been held back due to KG Basin sourcing issues.

guidance_outlook: About INR 3,500 crore expansion capex over 2 to 2.5 years; about INR 3,000 crore targeted by March 2028, with the balance spilling into April to June 2028.
Network to expand from about 2,900 km to about 3,600 km; capacity to rise from about 36.5 MMSCMD by about 8-9 MMSCMD.
Next tariff revision expected around 2028 (last revision April 2024); management will not speculate on tariff level and says the revision will not reduce tariffs.
Maintenance capex expected at INR 60-100 crore per year over the next couple of years.
Dividend payout expected to be maintained at current levels, subject to Board discretion; no guarantee on amount.
Interest income on deposits expected to fall toward zero as cash is deployed into capex, which will weigh on PAT.
capex_capacity: Expansion capex about INR 3,500 crore across more than 10 pipeline and connectivity projects totalling about 700 km; all projects board-approved and mostly in execution stage.
EPC contracts worth INR 1,800 crore awarded in July 2026 for Anjar-Palanpur pipeline, which is the major project stretching to March 2028; approvals said to be almost fully in place.

Other projects under implementation include Jamnagar-Dwarka, Vapi-Tarapur, Dahej-Bhadbhut and spur lines; Jamnagar-Dwarka linked to a Sun Petro-operated offshore Dwarka field with minimum 2.5 MMSCMD expected.
GIGL has a remaining capex of about INR 100-110 crore under execution and no major capex needs seen near term.
GITL: major investment deferred because of KG Basin sourcing issues; management says no PNGRB penalties incurred so far.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of 12% YoY to 45 MMSCMD in Q2 FY27; management says volumes are now contractual rather than physical throughput, which is the basis for revenue.
Tariff regime: 12% post-tax RoCE on regulated assets; management said the 2024 revision was based on a 2023 filing; the next revision is expected in 2028.
Pending PNGRB appellate tribunal matter on prior claims; any favourable outcome would be credited prospectively via true-up, not retrospectively.
Revenue for GIGL and GITL is partly take-or-pay, which management said explains the gap between volume growth and revenue growth.
Other expenses rose in Q2 due to longer compressor operation to send more gas north; management says these are pass-through costs recoverable in the next tariff revision.

qa_highlights.question: Debt-to-equity plan for INR 3,500 crore expansion and whether board approval for debt is in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expansion will be funded mainly from internal accruals and cash, with limited financing if required; financing approvals are already in place and all projects are board-approved, with no further approvals needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volume reporting change from physical to contractual, and how do tariffs reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier figures were physical volumes and the new figures are contractual, which align with revenue; some variation vs. tariff back-calculation is due to gross calorific value differences.

qa_highlights.question: Useful life of the 2,900 km network and next tariff revision timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial useful life is 30 years, extendable with recertification (PNGRB allows up to 10 years per tranche); next revision expected around 2028 and management does not expect tariffs to fall.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the PNGRB challenge and how true-up works?
qa_highlights.answer: The matter is still before the PNGRB appellate tribunal; any credit would be prospective only through subsequent transportation, and no prior claims have been adjudicated by PNGRB.

qa_highlights.question: How much of GIGL and GITL capacity is contracted and when will they break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are a few key customers but contracts are not yet enough for breakeven; it expects breakeven in about a couple of years and would revert with contract details later.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company consider a buyback or higher dividend, given cash and net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback is not top of the agenda and dividend is a Board decision; it intends to maintain the dividend at least at current rates but cannot guarantee amounts.

risks_watch: Anjar-Palanpur delivery by March 2028 is the critical path; the EPC contracts were awarded only in July 2026.
Land acquisition and right-of-way delays raised by an analyst; management said costs are capitalised and treated as pass-through, but no quantification given.
Subsidiary losses at GIGL and GITL: volumes remain well below capacity and breakeven is 'a couple of years' away; GITL capex deferred due to KG Basin sourcing issues.
PAT decline risk as cash is deployed and interest income on deposits falls toward zero.
Tariff outcome at the 2028 revision is not guided; the PNGRB appeal outcome is unknown and would be prospective only.
Capital allocation questions: investors pressed on buyback versus new pipeline investment at about 12% regulated return; management gave no buyback commitment.

544802|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 net profit Rs.22.77 Crores (~12% margin) on 105% load factor, with fuel costs the main EBITDA drag.
544802|2026-06.overview: Management attributed the quarter to a Middle East-driven spike in fuel prices, which took roughly Rs.14 crores out of EBITDA, while load factor rose to 105% and average ticket price rose about 4.3% year on year. Guests served exceeded 55,700 and staterooms booked reached 24,245, up about 10%. Management expects fuel surcharges on new bookings to show up from end-Q2/early-Q3, and says the second ship (Cordelia Sky) brings a much higher suite count. Finance cost roughly doubled to about Rs.4 crores on a bank loan taken to support rating and FD-backed arrangements.

segments.name: Empress (existing ship)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth for June 2026 vs June 2025 estimated at about 8-9% by management; expected to move to 10-12% going forward. Empress has about 69 suite and balcony cabins and about 800 total cabins.

segments.name: Cordelia Sky (new ship)
segments.commentary: Expected to have about 269 suite and balcony cabins and about 1,000 total cabins, with nine restaurants versus three on Empress. Management says revenue potential per ship is almost 100% higher than the current vessel.

Fuel surcharges on new bookings expected to recover most of the extra fuel cost, with impact visible from end-Q2 / beginning of Q3.
Management is hopeful that the extra fuel cost will be offset by year-end through additional savings, as fuel prices move toward forecast levels.
Management says it is planning on an annual-average basis rather than quarterly, and Q2 is being used as a lower-capacity test period for new itineraries without affecting annual results.
Cost sharing across three ships (fixed shore-side marketing and management fees) expected to lower per-ship cost once the fleet is fully operational.

Management says ticket prices do not change much; revenue growth is driven by cabin mix, not pricing.
Fuel price: VLSFO average was $580 per metric tonne over last year, peaked at $1,228 when tensions started, and is about $800 currently per management.
Port charges abroad said to be lower than in India due to GST on domestic port charges; more sea days on international cruises reduce port cost impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why has EBITDA margin declined over the last two quarters, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main driver is fuel, worth about Rs.14 crores; crew wage increases of about Rs.2 crores (about 16% in percentage terms) and food costs of about Rs.1 crore were smaller items.

qa_highlights.question: How will higher fuel costs be passed on to customers given advance bookings?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel surcharges apply to new bookings only, not already-sold Q1 cruises, so recovery shows from end-Q2/beginning-Q3. Fuel was pre-ordered and bought at prices that management says have fallen from the peak.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 revenue growth from occupancy or ticket price?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: load factor rose from 99.9% to 105% and average ticket price rose about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost roughly double?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a loan was taken from IDFC First Bank, backed by FDs, to support rating requirements; it carries a 1% prepayment cost and is being carried over, with the company citing zero net debt given matching FD assets.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Q2 top-line run rate versus about Rs.190 crores in Q1, and like-for-like Empress growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a numeric Q2 run rate, pointing to cabin mix. Empress growth was about 8-9% in the quarter, expected to reach 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy to expand margins beyond fuel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed shore-side marketing, management fees and other costs will be spread across three ships as the fleet grows, with better purchasing power.

544802|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to Rs 1,329 million, with EBITDA of Rs 777 million (58.45% margin) and Cordelia Sky delivered early.
544802|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 1,329 million, up 31% YoY, with PAT of Rs 585 million. H1 FY27 revenue was stated as Rs 3,230 billion (likely Rs 3,230 million, a transcript inconsistency), up 16% YoY, with H1 PAT of Rs 813 million. Cordelia Sky arrived in Mumbai on schedule, about a month early, with sailing set to start 23 October 2026, adding roughly 126% to capacity. Fuel cost per APCD roughly rose 72% in Q2 YoY (Rs 2,471 vs Rs 1,434), which management said cost about Rs 28 crore in H1 that was partly offset by fuel surcharges and cost savings.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 3,230 billion as stated (appears to be Rs 3,230 million)

segments.name: Cruise operations (Empress, Sky, SUN)
segments.commentary: Empress is the operating vessel with 796 rooms and 2,005 beds. Sky (2,400 guests, 1,002 staterooms) arrived early and starts sailing 23 October 2026. SUN, a sister ship slightly larger, is due in about 11 months.

guidance_outlook: Sky revenue to begin contributing from H2 FY27, with larger benefits as utilisation ramps up.

Management hopes fuel costs ease in Q3 and Q4, and expects fuel cost impact to be neutralised by Q4 if prices return toward original forecast. Management said it could not fully absorb the fuel increase.
Management said Q3 and Q4 are the strong quarters (wedding season, Diwali, Christmas, New Year), but declined to give forward booking numbers.
Management said it expects cruise operating margins of about 35% or higher, versus a global range of 35% to 40%.
Fuel cost impact of about Rs 12 crore is expected to remain in the current period after surcharges, per the CFO's answer on Q1 and Q2 impact.
SUN delivery remains on schedule for about 11 months from the call.
capex_capacity: Cordelia Sky (2,400 guests, 1,002 staterooms) delivered early and arrived in Mumbai on the call date; sailing starts 23 October 2026. Capacity rises about 126%.
SUN, a sister ship of Sky, is due in about 11 months, on schedule.
Advance of Rs 4,290 million toward acquisition of new vessels, interest-bearing, held through a subsidiary and an intermediary; not yet used as of the call.

Management is exploring fleet expansion beyond SUN and is at an initial discussion stage. Financing options: lease structure (fixed lease over 10 years, dollar buyout at year 10), internal accruals, or outright purchase with debt.
Sky lease cost is about USD 16 million per year, treated as an operating cost in management's numbers under Ind AS.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per passenger rose to Rs 13,645 in Q2 FY27 from Rs 10,349, driven by higher ticket price and onboard revenue.
Company started charging a fuel surcharge of USD 15-20 per person per day to offset part of the fuel cost increase.
Sky's per-guest pricing is said to be about 100% higher than Empress, and SUN's about 150% higher, driven by cabin mix (suites: 60/69 on Empress, 260 on Sky, 600 on SUN).

Management said the Indian overnight ocean and coastal cruise market was about Rs 8,301 million in FY25 and is expected to grow 20-25% CAGR over FY26-FY31. India had about 4.8 lakh cruise passenger movements in CY2025, about 89% domestic.
Management cited about 95 wedding dates in FY28 versus a typical 65-70, and plans to grow weddings and celebrations as a revenue stream.
Loyalty programme 'Chairman's Club' is being rolled out.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion from operating leverage, and how will fuel, crew and port costs be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cruise margins globally are 35-40% and the company expects to match or beat that. Shared corporate costs across more ships are expected to lower per-ship operating cost. Fuel is expected to ease, and the company plans to offset it with surcharges, itinerary changes and cost savings.

qa_highlights.question: How will the next fleet addition be financed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the lease structure used for Empress, Sky and SUN (fixed lease over 10 years, then a nominal buyout). It also cited internal accruals (about Rs 220 crore used for Sky and SUN pre-IPO) and possible debt funding for an outright purchase.

qa_highlights.question: Why did short-term borrowings rise by about Rs 344 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the funds were advanced to a subsidiary, which passed them to an intermediary to hold ready for an identified vessel deal. The money is interest-bearing and not yet used.

qa_highlights.question: How much fuel cost is unrecovered and what price increase would neutralise it?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said about Rs 12 crore of fuel cost impact remains after surcharges and savings. Management said full absorption is unlikely and it hopes to return to original forecast by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How does lease cost for Sky and SUN affect earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Sky lease is about USD 16 million per year. Management said it is included in operating costs and pricing, and below EBITDA under Ind AS it is absorbed at PBT and PAT levels.

qa_highlights.question: What are the bookings for H2, including Empress and Sky?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers, citing restrictions on forward-looking statements. It said demand was strong and that near-term bookings were hard to get.

544803|2026-03.headline: Advit Jewels FY26 revenue rose 33.68% to INR 167.03 crore and net profit 35.56% to INR 34.39 crore, but Q4 was softer at INR 43.23 crore income.
544803|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the company's strongest year: total income grew 33.68% to INR 1,67,02,56,000, EBITDA rose 32.52% to INR 49,23,80,000 at a 29.48% margin, and net profit grew 35.56% to INR 34,38,79,000. 544812|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 77.5% YoY to INR36.69 crores, while EBITDA margin fell to 20.3% on a raw-material pass-through lag.
544812|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR36.69 crores versus INR20.67 crores in H1 FY26 (up 77.5% YoY, up 8.8% HoH). EBITDA rose to INR7.45 crores from INR3.88 crores in H2 FY26, with margin at 20.3% against 11.5% in H2 FY26 and 20.7% for full-year FY26. PAT rose to INR4.38 crores from INR1.75 crores. Management attributed the lower margin versus H1 FY26 to a one-month lag in customer raw-material pass-through as polymer prices spiked in September. Net worth rose to INR46.06 crores post-IPO and borrowings fell 53%, leaving debt-to-equity at 0.1x.

qa_highlights.question: Is there additional billing for already-shipped material to recover the margin hit, or will recovery come only in subsequent orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the crude rise of about 20% lifted polymer about 22%; pass-through contracts reset with a one-month lag. About INR1.45 crores of higher prices was billed in October, and adjustments are expected to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak capacity utilisation and when will expansion be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Target operating efficiency is 88%, with no hurdles scaling from 67% to 88%. Management expects to reach 88% around FY28 and then add machines one at a time, with investment in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Will customers add other suppliers as new OEMs enter India, and how fast can capacity scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are unlikely to add suppliers because the company works from design stage. Machine additions take 45 to 60 days, with generic machines installed in about 15 days; scaling is limited by product qualification and forecasts, not buildings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 FY26 margins fall so sharply versus H1 FY26, and will margins be lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to mix: home appliances were about 30% of H2 FY26 revenue, while H1 had high-margin engineering services billings (about 22%). Management expects a more stable full-year profile with a stronger H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the engineering revenue contribution target and what are the other engineering markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineering is guided at 22% to 25% of FY27 revenue. Co-design work includes the drip irrigation project, which may later be separated as its own vertical with higher margins.
