544814|2026-06.headline: Knack Packaging Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 40.5% YoY to INR2,647.7 million, with EBITDA up 53.1% and margin at 22.35%.
544814|2026-06.overview: Knack Packaging reported Q1 FY27 as its first earnings call after listing on NSE and BSE. Consolidated revenue grew 40.5% YoY on 20.9% higher volume (10,940 MT), with EBITDA up 53.1% and PAT up 47.96%. Management attributed margin gains to operating leverage, cost discipline, solar power and a rising share of pinch-bottom bags. Capacity utilisation is about 91%, with a rented plant added to bridge until the IPO-funded plant, targeted for October 2027, takes installed capacity to about 70,000 MT.

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Management said about 55-56% of sales are export and about 45% domestic; export margins are about 5-6% gross profit higher than domestic. Operations span 74 countries, up from 71 in FY26.

segments.name: PLWPP and pinch-bottom bags
segments.commentary: Pinch-bottom share of sales rose from 19-20% in prior-year quarters to a current 22.5-23%. Management says about 70% of sales are PLWPP bags. Two pinch-bottom machines (about INR20 crore each) were installed in the last quarter of FY26.

guidance_outlook: New IPO-funded plant targeted for commissioning in October 2027, taking installed capacity to about 70,000 MT from about 43,300 MT at listing.
Management expects Q1 FY27 sales levels to be maintained until the new plant starts, using the rented facilities.
Another rented plant of about 5,040 MT annual capacity was added about a month before the call; trials are under way.
Main construction of the new plant is expected to pick up after the monsoon; machinery finalisation is ongoing.
No explicit FY27 volume or EBITDA per kg guidance was given.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 43,300 MT at listing; operating above 48,000 MT including rented facilities, at about 91% utilisation.
Target installed capacity about 70,000 MT once the new plant is commissioned (October 2027).
Management said it is running at 90-92% utilisation and has no spare space to expand existing sites.
11 MW solar farm at Khedbrahma started in the last quarter; electricity cost fell about 1.1% of revenue YoY from solar.
Gross block rose to INR416 crore, with INR141 crore added over the year; the IPO proceeds are about INR320 crore.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR130 crore cited by management.
Customer retention is about 90%; more than 2,000 customers and over 13,000 SKUs.
Cargill is about 12-17% of revenue (figures varied on the call), with about 600 SKUs and a contract of 2 years plus a 1-year extension, priced as polymer cost plus conversion.
About 45-50% of customers are on fixed conversion-cost pricing with raw material pass-through; the rest are small buyers with pass-through pricing on the day of change.
Management said it passes polymer price changes through to customers on the same day, and that about 50% of input cost changes are passed on, with about 60% retained in some cases.

Management claims about 10% market share in the Indian bag segment (per a Technopack report), and says it is the leader in pinch-bottom bags in India. Management named Polytex (USA) as its only direct listed peer.

qa_highlights.question: Why are ROCE and asset turnover so high versus peers, and how is margin sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset turn is 2.53x on gross block and 4.12x on net block as of 30 June 2026, versus peer averages of about 1.5-2x. It attributed this to specialised machinery and a shift to higher-margin pinch-bottom bags. ROCE is supported by ongoing profits and IPO proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: How is the polymer price rise being managed, and how fast is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a SAP S/4HANA forecasting system, buys in cash and in bulk, and passes price changes to customers the same day. It said conversion-cost contracts cover 45-50% of customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Cargill relationship and the FX gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Cargill (USA) business grew from INR4 crore in 2020 to about INR140 crore; it is on a 2+1-year contract and buys finished bags. Management cited the cost of packaging below 1% of product value. FX gain in Q1 FY27 was INR1.6 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How does EBITDA per kg look, and how fast will pinch-bottom volumes move?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited EBITDA per kg of about INR54 in Q1 and INR45 in FY26. Pinch-bottom share is 22.5-23% and is rising; the call did not give a 70,000 MT utilisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth be sustained in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q1 sales levels to hold as the rented plants run until the new plant starts in October 2027. It said the onboarding process for new products is long, so marketing is being increased through rented capacity.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude volatility; management said the situation is fully volatile, and pass-through on fixed-conversion contracts shifts cost to the company.
Commissioning timing of the October 2027 plant; construction main phase is after the monsoon.
Dependence on rented plants for interim capacity and on rented facilities until the new plant starts.

Export share of about 55% and FX exposure; the company reported only INR1.6 crore FX gain in the quarter.
Gross block growth to INR416 crore; management did not commit to maintaining asset turn of 2.5x+ on INR380 crore expansion.

544814|2026-09.headline: Knack Packaging Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 52.5% to INR294.76 crores, but EBITDA margin fell 285 bps to 16.35% on polymer cost pass-through lag.
544814|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached a record INR294.76 crores in Q2 FY27 (up 52.5% YoY), with EBITDA up 29.9% to INR49.77 crores but margin down 285 bps to 16.35%. Management attributed the margin squeeze to polypropylene prices rising over 50% within weeks after the West Asia conflict, plus higher Red Sea freight costs, with price pass-through lagging by one to two quarters. PAT rose 21.2% to INR25.02 crores, though it absorbed a INR2.62 crores share of loss from the Sayem Knack JV in Mexico. Management expects margin recovery from Q3 FY27 as price revisions flow through, subject to market stabilisation.

financial_highlights.change: Moderation attributed to post-IPO capital base
Down from INR39 crores (as stated by analyst)

segments.name: Packaging (bags, PLWPP and pinch-bottom)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume was 11,252 metric tons, up 3% QoQ from 10,940 MT and up about 13-14% YoY from 9,927 MT. Pinch-bottom bags contribute about 21% of revenue, and PLWPP is about 71-72% of volume.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Sold to 75 countries across 6 continents as of September 2026, up from 74 at end Q1 FY27 and 71 in FY26. Export receivable cycles are longer than domestic, adding to working capital.

segments.name: Sayem Knack JV (Mexico)
segments.commentary: Greenfield plant with 400 MT installed capacity; selling about 80 MT/month last quarter, targeting 100-120 MT in Q3. Breakeven estimated at about 120 MT/month; JV loss was INR6.06 crores in H1 and INR2.62 crores in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Margin expected to recover from Q3 FY27 as price revisions flow through, subject to market stabilisation; management said full loss recovery in one quarter is difficult.
Volume expected to be better in Q3 than Q2, with new capacity (5,040 MT added in August 2026) ramping to about 50% utilisation (about 2,500 MT).
Mexico JV expected to reach breakeven in Q3 FY27, with Q4 as the committed-target fallback.
Management said full-year targets are on track, though Q2 is significantly down.
Expansion targeted for October 2027, taking installed capacity to about 69,000-72,000 MT from about 42,000 MT.
Pinch-bottom output targeted at 25,000-30,000 MT, with 2 new pinch machines due around October 2027 and full benefit by 2028.

5,040 MT of new capacity added in August 2026, ramping up; a rented plant added about two months before the call is expected to add capacity in one to two months.

Expansion (new Gujarat plant) targeted for October 2027 and cited as a key milestone through 2027.
Mexico JV: 400 MT installed capacity, utilised at about 80-90 MT/month.
demand_pricing: Polypropylene prices rose more than 50% within weeks of the West Asia conflict and stayed elevated through Q2; management cited polymer moving from about INR92 pre-war to INR160 at peak.

About 45-50% of customers are on conversion-cost contracts where bag prices move with polymer; the rest are order-by-order. Management said price hikes of 25-30% were applied immediately, with realisation lag of 1-2 quarters.
Management said gross margin impact was about 7% from the price lag; raw material rose about 26% in the quarter.
EBITDA per kg fell to about INR45 in Q2 from about INR54-55 in Q1 (per management; analyst cited INR36 vs INR51-52, which management confirmed as directionally correct).
New INR150 crore per year, 3-year contract renewal with a large US-based pet food and animal nutrition packaging customer, announced 2 October 2026; minimum INR150 crores per year.
Demand drivers cited: pet food (double-digit growth in India), rice (pinch-bottom season starting), and migration from jute, paper and POPP bags to PLWPP and pinch-bottom.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth was achieved in Q2, and what is plant utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was 11,252 MT, up 3% QoQ and about 13-14% YoY; plant utilisation is about 90-91%, with 5,040 MT of capacity added in August.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken in Q2 and what is planned for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material rose about 26%, gross margin impact was about 7%, and the remaining increase was passed on with the bulk expected to reflect in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin on track to recover in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q3 and Q4 to be better in volume and margin, but said full recovery depends on the market and crude prices; 99% of the cost increase is expected to be covered.

qa_highlights.question: How scalable is the INR150 crore international order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a minimum INR150 crore per year contract for 3 years from an existing US customer, with scope to add products, with the customer currently serving 8-9 countries against more than 100 for the customer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow fall in H1 and is it seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said inventory rose by about INR26.9 crores due to scale-up, and export receivables added about INR55 crores; tax was higher with effective rate about 25%, plus deferred tax and IPO-related items.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Mexico JV break even and what is its capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is 400 MT/month; sales were about 80 MT last quarter, targeted at 100-120 MT in Q3, with breakeven around 120 MT/month and Q3 expected to be near breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: Will the lost margin be recovered, and should pinch-bottom margins be higher YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full recovery in one quarter is difficult; Q3 is expected to recover a small part. Management agreed that with five pinch machines vs three last year, pinch-bottom margins should be higher YoY.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude price volatility: management said the 1% of residual risk depends on the market, and the price lag of 1-2 quarters could hurt margins again.
Mexico JV losses weigh on consolidated PAT until breakeven; Q1 and Q2 losses were INR6.06 crores in H1 and INR2.62 crores in Q2.
Working-capital build from exports (longer receivable cycles) and inventory; H1 operating cash flow fell to INR22 crores from INR39 crores.
Pinch-bottom market size and ability to convert PLWPP customers; pinch-bottom utilisation only about 60-70% after new machines.
Expansion timeline: October 2027 is the deadline for the new Gujarat expansion, and any slippage would limit volume growth.
Concentration: the INR150 crore contract is a large single-customer renewal; the 45-50% contracted book is also seasonal.

544821|2026-06.headline: Kusumgar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 102% YoY to INR247.2 crore and EBITDA margin hit 31%, but management gives no formal guidance.

EBITDA was INR75.9 crore at about 31% margin, up roughly 900bps YoY from 22% and down from 41% in Q4. PAT was INR42.6 crore (about 17% margin) versus INR6.6 crore a year ago. This was the company's first earnings call after its July 15, 2026 listing, and management declined to give formal forward guidance, citing unpredictable approval timing, government tenders and tariff exposure.

544822|2026-06.headline: Laser Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR5,215 million and EBITDA 26% to INR659 million, with EPC revenue up 129%.
544822|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 15% YoY to INR5,215 million, with EBITDA up 26% to INR659 million and margin expanding to 12.6% from 11.5%. Growth came mainly from EPC (revenue up 129% to INR1,391 million), while manufacturing revenue fell slightly to INR3,824 million from INR3,932 million. Finance cost of INR362 million absorbed about 55% of EBITDA, and PAT was INR211 million. Management said the IPO-funded debt repayment of about INR4,900 million, completed in Q2 FY27, will lower finance cost from later quarters; the company did not give numerical guidance for FY27.

544823|2026-09.headline: Devson H1 FY27 revenue rose just 1.14% to INR31.69 crore, but EBITDA margin expanded 250 bps to 31.80% as catalysts offset weak exports.
544823|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations was INR31.69 crore in H1 FY27, up 1.14% YoY, while EBITDA grew 9.84% to INR10.25 crore and PAT rose 13.12% to INR7.5 crore. Export share fell to 6.72% from 42.95% because Strait of Hormuz disruption hit Middle East shipments, and domestic sales carried the half. Catalyst sales rose to INR25.31 crore from INR13.26 crore, while ceramic ball sales fell to INR3.81 crore from INR13.45 crore. The company listed on BSE SME in July 2026 raising INR39.39 crore, and a 5,088 MTPA capacity addition is targeted for Q1 FY28.

Product revenue was lower YoY on customer delivery timing and supply chain factors. EBITDA margin was 36.1% in Q2 and 35.7% in H1, down YoY on mix and people costs but up sequentially. Order inflows were strong (H1 ₹330 crores, up 95% YoY), and capex is largely complete, with growth to be funded mainly from internal accruals.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up ~41% YoY and H1 up 29%, contributing 27% of H1 revenue. Management is building export aftermarket via hiring and agent partnerships; aftermarket orders deliver in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Defence and Marine
segments.commentary: Defence revenue scaled meaningfully from a low base (analyst cited 3.3x YoY in Q2 and 4.7x in H1; company did not give absolute figures). Of the ₹626 crores order book, ₹81 crores is for FY27 from Defence; defence orders are lumpy with 12-month or longer cycles.

Some H2 book-and-bill is needed to meet internal targets; management says it is secured. Orders pushed from Q2 to Q3 FY27; Q3 and Q4 outlook described as 'extremely encouraging'.
Further capex expected to be balancing, routine and small capacity enhancements, not substantial; next capex trigger at about 80-85% capacity utilisation.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex ₹41 crores; the ₹340 crores capex programme (split evenly between gears and defence) is almost fully complete.

demand_pricing: Middle East and African orders were significant in Q2; delayed STG pump and Middle East orders expected to finalise, timing shifting quarter to quarter. Management cited ADNOC pump and compressor orders via OEMs.

544829|2026-06.headline: SBI Funds Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 15% YoY to ₹1,149 crore and PAT reached ₹873 crore, up 37% QoQ.
544829|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first earnings call after the company's IPO listing. Mutual fund QAAUM reached ₹12.6 trillion (up 11% YoY) with a 15.1% overall market share, while operating revenue of ₹1,149 crore and operating profit of ₹907 crore grew 15% and 17% YoY. Management attributed margin gains mainly to asset-mix shift from passive funds toward equity, hybrid, arbitrage and gold/silver ETFs, and said the TER cut was passed on to distributors with a net neutral-to-positive effect. Management declined to give guidance, citing the silent period.

segments.commentary: Together about 8% of operating revenue. Management said AIF and PMS are more attractive than equity on margin, and the company plans one more AIF product this quarter.

segments.name: Passive
segments.commentary: Passive QAAUM ₹4 trillion, up 12% YoY; management said low-yield passive concentration has declined, adding about 2 bps to overall margin.

Alternate business hiring underway; one more AIF product to be launched this quarter.

544838|2026-09.headline: Xtranet Q2 FY27 revenue rose 63% YoY to about Rs 110 crore, with PAT up 111% to about Rs 14 crore and EBITDA margin at 20.42%.
544838|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of about Rs 110 crore (+63% YoY) and H1 revenue of about Rs 160 crore (+42%), with H1 operational EBITDA of about Rs 33 crore at 20.49% margin. Government and PSU share of business has fallen to about 30-35% from roughly 75-80% earlier, per the CFO. A new data center subsidiary was formed, with an initial 2 MW build at an estimated Rs 130-140 crore. Management said working capital rose during H1 and operating cash flow was negative, and it reiterated FY27 revenue ambition above original guidance of Rs 500 crore. Several analyst questions on cash flow, receivables and IPO capex were answered only partially on the call.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 24.38 crore (per analyst, not disputed by management)

segments.name: Data center infrastructure and IT operations
segments.commentary: Largest vertical and key growth driver; management says over 50% of the pipeline sits here. Company has over 1 MW hosted capacity and about 2 MW internal demand, currently served from third-party data centers.

segments.name: Enterprise applications (ERP)
segments.commentary: Lower-margin vertical, per CFO at about 25-26% margin versus 34-35% earlier. XERP is being pitched to small and mid-market firms; management cited XtraBanks deployed in 60+ banks.

segments.name: Digital transformation services
segments.commentary: Higher-margin, growing vertical; management cites AI-led projects and services growth as reducing dependence on supply chain. No separate revenue figure given.

segments.name: Proprietary platforms (XtraTrust and Synergy)
segments.commentary: Together contribute 14% of revenue per management. XtraTrust is a MeitY-approved certifying authority; about 1 million B2C subscribers and 80+ B2B clients; 100+ government portals accept its digital signatures. Individual revenue, EBITDA and recurring split not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management ambition is to surpass original FY27 revenue guidance while sustaining strong EBITDA and PAT margins; an analyst cited Rs 500 crore FY27 guidance from the prior call, and management said it is hopeful of achieving it with Q3 and Q4 heavily loaded.
EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at about 17.5-18% going forward, per CFO.
Working capital cycle expected to improve by about 15-20 days by year-end FY27 versus FY26.
International revenue expected to start from Q4 FY27; six-country proposals in Middle East and Africa under negotiation, with 10-15 year contract tenors.
Data center: initial 2 MW build at Rs 130-140 crore funded by internal accruals and debt; scale-up to 10 MW under an asset-light model still being worked out, with figures to follow.
capex_capacity: Data center subsidiary formed in Q2 for hosting, cloud and managed services; initial 2 MW build at about Rs 130-140 crore, with expansion to about 10 MW planned.

Rs 8.48 crore IPO capex allocation not yet utilised; management said it is for equipment for the IT park, with the first 42,000 sq ft block aligned and deployment expected to be allocated in the current quarter.
Procurement and supply chain strengthened in H1 to secure hardware and software; management says OEM supply has improved, though Q1 was weak.
demand_pricing: Fresh orders of about Rs 90 crore in Q2 FY27; order book about Rs 390 crore at 30 Sep 2026, with 50-55% expected to bill in FY27.
Bid pipeline above Rs 2,000 crore; 25-30% of pipeline typically converts into firm orders.
Order book walk per management: about Rs 350 crore at start of year, about Rs 200 crore of new orders in the year (25% existing customers, 75% new logos), about Rs 160 crore executed.
Government and PSU share down to about 30-35% of business from about 47% of FY26 revenue as cited in the opening remarks; CFO said 50-50 government/enterprise at FY26 close.
Competitive positioning: XERP targeted at small and mid-market (about 100,000 MSMEs) where Oracle and SAP are seen as too costly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the proposed investment, timeline and funding for the new data center subsidiary, and what capacity and revenue are envisaged?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial 2 MW build needs about Rs 130-140 crore, funded partly by internal accruals and partly by debt; expansion to 10 MW is on a different, asset-light financial model still being worked out. Specific numbers to follow.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company differentiate its data center and cloud offering from established operators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited over 1 MW hosted capacity and about 2 MW internal demand from its own SaaS applications, to be hosted on its own platform and later offered as public cloud.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin expansion and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to mix shift: lower-margin enterprise business (about 25-26% margin, down from 34-35%) is shrinking while digital services, proprietary platforms and data center grow. Sustainable margin guided at about 17.5-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days rise, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the government share fell from about 75-80% to 30-35%, and the working capital cycle is expected to improve by 15-20 days by year-end versus FY26. The analyst's day-count figures were partly garbled on the line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book split between fresh and repeat business, and which verticals drive inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Of about Rs 200 crore new orders, 25% from existing customers and 75% from new logos; data center and IT operations and digital/AI projects plus proprietary platforms are the focus areas.

qa_highlights.question: How consistent has order-to-revenue conversion been, and what are typical execution timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was low due to supply chain issues; management says supply has since streamlined. Infrastructure deployments take 90 days to 18 months followed by 5-10 years of O&M; enterprise application deployments take 4-6 months plus 5-6 years of support; B2B PKI deployments take 30-90 days; B2C is subscription-based (1-3 years).

qa_highlights.question: What progress has been made internationally, and are there signed contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Proposals submitted in six countries across the Middle East and Africa, under negotiation; none signed yet. Contracts are expected to run 10-15 years, with revenue starting around Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive standing in the DSC market and XERP versus Oracle?
qa_highlights.answer: XtraTrust cited 24x7 online issuance within 15-30 minutes, integrations with PAN, Aadhaar, GST and banks, and availability on web, Android and iOS. XERP is positioned for small and mid-market firms, with banking solutions deployed in 60+ banks.

qa_highlights.question: Why was operating cash flow negative despite strong PAT, what is the collection timeline for the Rs 24.38 crore receivables increase, and what are the revenue, EBITDA and recurring split for XtraTrust and Synergy?
qa_highlights.answer: Not answered directly. Management said the receivables rise reflects invoices raised in late September for recently delivered projects, expected to be collected in October and within Q2 FY27. Management said the XtraTrust and Synergy breakdown was in the uploaded presentation and offered to answer in writing; the cash flow reason was not explained. The IPO capex question was answered (see capex section).

qa_highlights.question: How confident are you of the Rs 500 crore FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 execution will be heavily loaded in Q3 and Q4, as in prior years, and it is hopeful of hitting the target.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow in H1 despite PAT of about Rs 20 crore; receivables up Rs 24.38 crore and working capital build for procurement. Watch Q3 OCF and receivable days.
Revenue back-loaded into Q3 and Q4 to reach guidance; H1 revenue of about Rs 160 crore would need a steep H2 ramp versus a Rs 500 crore FY27 target.
Order book of Rs 390 crore is well below the target path; conversion of Rs 2,000 crore+ pipeline (25-30% historical conversion) is the key swing factor.
Supply chain dependence for OEM hardware in data center projects; Q1 execution was weak.
Data center plan is asset-heavy (Rs 130-140 crore for 2 MW) despite the stated asset-light model for scale-up; funding mix and returns not specified.
Disclosure gaps: no split for XtraTrust and Synergy revenue, EBITDA or recurring revenue; no order-book-to-revenue numbers beyond H1; several analyst questions were deferred to written responses.
Q2 Rs 24.38 crore receivable collections in October not yet verified.
544838|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and pipeline, but evasive on cash flow and receivables: the operating cash flow question was not answered and several numeric questions were deferred to the presentation or to written replies.
key_quotes: We delivered a successful quarter with exceptional growth and robust execution momentum across all our business verticals.
While this has temporarily increased our working capital requirements, we believe these investments will support stronger execution, revenue growth, and profitability during H2 FY'27.
The momentum achieved during H1 gives us confidence in our full-year performance, and our ambition is to surpass our original revenue guidance while sustaining strong EBITDA and PAT margins.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin sustained at about 17.5-18% versus H1 operational EBITDA margin of 20.49%, so the guide sits below current levels; mix shift away from 25-26% margin enterprise business is the driver, but the guide implies some give-back from H1.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Initial 2 MW data center build at Rs 130-140 crore is approved with no live date, and the IPO-funded IT park equipment (Rs 8.48 crore, first 42,000 sq ft block) is expected to be allocated in the current quarter; 10 MW scale-up figures are still to follow.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 fresh orders about Rs 90 crore, order book about Rs 390 crore with 50-55% expected to bill in FY27, and H1 revenue up 42% YoY to about Rs 160 crore, though H2 must ramp steeply to reach Rs 500 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The 10 MW scale-up is planned but its funding and figures are still being worked out, and the 2 MW build is already committed at Rs 130-140 crore, so further data center capex disclosure is likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is only hopeful of hitting the Rs 500 crore FY27 target with Q3 and Q4 heavily loaded, and the Rs 390 crore order book is well short of the target path, so an upgrade is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rs 500 crore FY27 target requires a steep H2 ramp from H1 revenue of about Rs 160 crore, Q1 was weak on supply chain, and H1 operating cash flow was negative with receivables up Rs 24.38 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: International revenue is expected to start in Q4 FY27 from six-country Middle East and Africa proposals under negotiation with none signed, and XERP is being pitched to about 100,000 MSMEs, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: International revenue from Middle East and Africa
rows.why: Proposals submitted in six countries, none signed yet, with 10-15 year contract tenors and revenue expected to start around Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Working capital cycle improvement of 15-20 days
rows.why: CFO guided a 15-20 day improvement versus FY26 by year-end, but H1 operating cash flow was negative and receivables rose Rs 24.38 crore, so the path is unproven.

rows.label: Bid pipeline conversion
rows.why: Bid pipeline is above Rs 2,000 crore and 25-30% typically converts, implying roughly Rs 500-600 crore of potential orders, but conversion depends on bids being won.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, margin sustainability and the Rs 2,000 crore+ pipeline, but cautious and evasive on operating cash flow, receivables and the XtraTrust/Synergy split; analysts pushed on cash flow, working capital days and how the Rs 500 crore FY27 target can be reached.

544839|2026-06.headline: Lohia Corp Q1 FY27 revenue rose 60% YoY to INR503 crore, EBITDA margin 19.9% and order book about INR1,778 crore.
544839|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR503 crore versus INR315 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR100 crore (19.9% margin vs 11.5%) and PAT of INR66 crore (13% margin). Management attributed margin expansion to higher volumes, operating leverage and efficiencies, and said it targets about 20% EBITDA margin internally without formal guidance. The order book reached about INR1,778-1,780 crore, up 30% since March 2026 and 195% since June 2025, with about 20% backed by customer advances. Domestic demand now drives the order book, while management expects exports to recover to around 50% of revenue. This was the company's first earnings call after listing.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR17 crore in Q1 FY26; PAT margin 13%

segments.name: Machinery (woven plastic / technical textiles)
segments.commentary: Core business, estimated at 80-85% of revenue. Order book is about INR1,780 crore with about 20% customer advances, and execution quoted at 6-9 months.

segments.name: Spare parts
segments.commentary: Approx. 10-12% of revenue. Management said spare-parts gross margins run 2-3 percentage points above machinery.

segments.name: New initiatives (recycling, monofilament)
segments.commentary: Approx. 5-6% of revenue. Polyolefin recycling only; no polyester recycling yet. Shredding and granulating adjacencies under evaluation.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Domestic approx. 59% and exports approx. 41% of Q1 revenue. Export prices are said to be 10-15% above domestic, net of CIF freight and agency costs.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth of 20-25% (no EBITDA guidance given).
Internal EBITDA margin target is about 20%, described as the new normal; management said it will not formally guide on EBITDA.
Capacity is adequate for about INR2,400-2,500 crore turnover. Beyond that, roughly INR80-100 crore capex per INR500 crore of incremental turnover is needed.
Exports are expected to stabilise at around 50% of revenue and order book over time.
R&D spend is expected to average about 3% of revenue going forward.
capex_capacity: Current utilisation stated at about 70-75%; management said peak achievable is about 80-85% across tape extrusion, circular looms and winders.
Maintenance capex and machine balancing continue each year; major capex not yet planned.
Asset turnover of 3-4x; new capacity could go live in 5-6 months, since land is available adjacent to the Kanpur plant.
New products launched: CoEx 1600 multi-layer coating line, Nova 6 Plus six-shuttle circular loom (up to 1,150 picks/min), FIBC cutting and back-cutting machines.
Virtual remote assistance centre set up at Kanpur; TTRC launched a 3-month certification programme for block bottom bag machines.
demand_pricing: Order book is driven mainly by domestic investment; management expects exports to recover to about 50% of revenue and order book.
Conversion of inquiries to executable orders is about 10-15%, over 2-3 years, per management. The current pipeline figure was not disclosed.
Management said Lohia commands 15-20% price premium over Chinese competitors; export competition in Southeast Asia is mainly from Chinese players, and in developed markets mainly from Starlinger.
Margin defence rests on three levers: repricing new orders to current input costs, short- and medium-term supplier contracts, and discount structure tweaks.
Replacement demand is about 3-5% of the order book today and is expected to rise, given 20-25 year machine life.
Management said the tariff does not affect the company directly, as machinery goes mainly to developing countries; customers export fabric to the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book rise so steeply from FY24 to about INR1,800 crore, and is this a peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to post-COVID capex recovery, growing non-packaging applications, and single-use plastic bans driving new uses. It said the peak has not yet been reached.

qa_highlights.question: Will exports recover to 40-50% of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export share ranged 45-55% of revenue historically and expects it to stabilise around 50%, though domestic currently leads the order book.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 20% EBITDA margin be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pre-COVID margins were 15-20%, Q1 and Q4 FY26 reached about 20%, and 20% is the new normal internally. It gave no formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is implied for FY27 from the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: An analyst suggested INR2,150-2,200 crore; Raj Kumar Lohia said 'should be like that', without confirming the figure.

qa_highlights.question: How much did service and spares contribute, and at what margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Spares are about 10-12% of revenue, with gross margins 2-3 points above machinery. Consumable parts run about 2-3% of installed plant value each year, perpetually.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution cycle for new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 6-9 months, depending on product complexity. Legacy products can be delivered faster and newer, more complex products take longer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D plan and are there hero products?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 3% of revenue and expected to stay around 3%. Confidential automation and IoT technologies are in development, but no launch dates were given.

qa_highlights.question: Are any regulations benefiting Lohia against Chinese competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only customs duty on Chinese and European equipment helps. No BIS or other regulatory benefit was identified.

risks_watch: Raw material and component cost volatility; management said it does not hedge purchases through long-term fixed-price contracts with large steel suppliers.
Margin dilution as domestic mix rises during FY27, since export pricing is 10-15% higher; management says margins will be protected.
Chinese competition, particularly in Southeast Asia, where rupee depreciation has been used to offer higher discounts.
Inquiry-to-order conversion of 10-15% and the lack of a disclosed current pipeline figure.
Management did not confirm the FY27 revenue estimate of INR2,150-2,200 crore; watch the Q2 run-rate and order book conversion.
Capacity utilisation figures given in the call were inconsistent (50%, 70-72%, 75%), so the true utilisation level needs confirming.
544839|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and margins, with a clear focus on the 20% EBITDA target. Evasive or unprepared on the order pipeline figures, capacity utilisation and export share, which the chairman deferred to later email. The call had audio issues and several figures were corrected mid-call.
key_quotes: For the quarter, we reported revenue from operations of INR503 crores compared with INR315 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, represe nting a growth of around 60%.
So we believe that this is going to be the new normal for us.
So we expect to grow in the range of 20% to 25%.
But we do not give any guidance on the EBITDA number going forward.
We currently are maintaining that we internally target 20% as our EBITDA number.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin reached 19.9% vs 11.5% a year ago and management calls ~20% the new normal internally, though export mix (10-15% higher pricing) will dilute as domestic share rises.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Current capacity supports about INR2,400-2,500 crore turnover versus FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% on a ~INR503 crore quarter, and land is available next to Kanpur, but no size, capex or date was given and utilisation is only about 70-75%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 20-25%, backed by an order book of about INR1,780 crore (up 195% since June 2025, up 30% since March 2026) with 6-9 month execution.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 70-75% (peak 80-85%), below the 80%+ threshold, and management said major capex is not yet planned, though the order book is rising fast and the adjacent land is available.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book is up 195% in a year and an analyst's INR2,150-2,200 crore FY27 view implies growth above the 20-25% guide, but management did not confirm that figure and gives no EBITDA guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw materials are not hedged through fixed-price steel contracts, export mix is set to fall toward 50% (lower price), and inquiry-to-order conversion is only 10-15% with no disclosed pipeline.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CoEx 1600, Nova 6 Plus and FIBC machines were just launched, and confidential automation and IoT products are in development, though no dates were given.

rows.label: Order book of about INR1,780 crore converting to revenue
rows.why: Order book is about INR1,780 crore with 6-9 month execution and about 20% customer advances, supporting the 20-25% FY27 revenue guide.

rows.label: Export recovery to about 50% of revenue
rows.why: Exports were 41% of Q1 revenue and management expects them to stabilise near 50%, though domestic demand currently leads the order book and exports face Chinese competition in Southeast Asia.

rows.label: Net working capital cycle easing
rows.why: NWC cycle is about 81 days excluding advances, down from 84 days at FY26 end.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the INR1,780 crore order book and the ~20% margin, but deferred on capacity utilisation (figures varied from 50% to 75%), export share and pipeline size. Analysts pushed on the FY27 revenue estimate of INR2,150-2,200 crore, which management did not confirm.

544839|2026-09.headline: Lohia Corp Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR594 crores, with order book near INR2,000 crores (up 93% YoY) and EBITDA margin at 19.4%.
544839|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations grew 42% YoY to INR594 crores and 18% QoQ, with H1 revenue up 50% to INR1,097 crores. EBITDA rose 33% YoY to INR116 crores, but margin eased to 19.4% from 20.7% a year earlier, which management attributed to higher commodity prices. PAT rose 48% YoY to INR77 crores, and the company reported a net cash position of INR123 crores. Order book reached about INR2,000 crores, with a record export order book, and management guided FY27 revenue growth of roughly 30-35%.

financial_highlights.change: +33% YoY from INR87 crores; margin vs 20.7% in Q2 FY26 and 19.9% in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: ~INR2,000 crores (INR1,994 crores per analyst read-back, not disputed)
INR115 crores / INR238 crores; net cash INR123 crores
financial_highlights.change: Net debt to equity -0.18x; net debt to EBITDA -0.57x

segments.name: Machinery
segments.commentary: Machinery revenue was INR480 crores in Q2, about 81% of quarterly revenue.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Aftermarket (spares and services) revenue was INR50 crores in Q2; management expects spares growth to support FY28.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.commentary: Other revenue was INR59 crores in Q2. Recycling machinery is still small, at an expected INR30-35 crores for FY27, with management targeting roughly a doubling in FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at roughly 30-35% YoY; H1:H2 split expected at about 45:55, implying H2 revenue of INR1,200-1,300 crores.
Order book expected to stay in the INR2,000-2,200 crores range by March 2027.
FY28 revenue growth guided at 10-15%, implying roughly INR2,500-2,600 crores, with possible spillover of orders from FY27.
Sustainable EBITDA margin range of 19-21%; internal planning figure of 20%.
Current capacity seen as supporting revenue of about INR2,500 crores; FY27 capex around INR75 crores, with a new shed planned for assembly capacity and Kanpur land available.
Recycling machinery revenue expected to roughly double in FY28.
capex_capacity: Current capacity supports revenue of about INR2,500 crores, which may need balancing equipment in one or two plants.
FY27 capex of about INR75 crores covering maintenance, balancing, and new machine capacity for conversion, recycling, and coating machinery.
Plans to build a new shed for additional assembly capacity; Kanpur premises have land available for further expansion.
Vendor base in Kanpur, Faridabad, and Bangalore is being expanded; three dedicated ancillaries in Kanpur have added capacity.
Management said utilisation cannot be measured precisely because capacity is fungible between in-house and vendor capacity across heterogeneous products.
demand_pricing: Export order book at an all-time high, about INR500 crores plus; the company exports to over 100 countries, with a customer base mainly in the developing world.
Domestic demand traction described as heavy after two to three years of low investment, with inquiries rising from mid-2025 and expected to continue for at least five to six months.
List prices were raised in February 2026 and July 2026; orders booked after a revision are priced at new rates. Contracts with 6-9 month delivery do not get price increases in the interim.
Overall inquiry pipeline about INR13,000 crores, with historical conversion of 15-20% into firm orders.

Domestic growth drivers cited: cement bags, block-bottom bags replacing pillow bags, BOPP bags, wrapping and specialty fabric. Management expects a slight slowdown in FY28 orders as industry capacity is added and fabric conversion rates cool from peak.
Gross margin fell about 3% QoQ, mainly due to input cost inflation (commodity prices, geopolitics) and some geography mix; management said gross margin is at around 41%.
Recycling: 1-2 machines executed per month; a first ReclaMax 120 (500 kg/hr) was supplied to a domestic customer; washing lines and mother-baby recycling launched.

qa_highlights.question: Does a customer buy the full project or individual machines?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers mostly buy complete projects (tape extrusion, looms, downstream equipment); partial and balancing orders for solo looms are smaller, typically 2 to 12 machines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 19-21%, with an internal 20% planning figure, subject to commodity trends.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book capacity and inquiry pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity supports about INR2,500 crores of revenue; inquiry pipeline is about INR13,000 crores with 15-20% conversion.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is recycling and spares?
qa_highlights.answer: Machinery order book of about INR2,000 crores includes INR30-35 crores of recycling machines; spares (about INR30-35 crores of annual revenue) are excluded from the order book.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY28 growth expected to slow to 10-15%, and what drove domestic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic growth came from new conversion segments such as block-bottom bags plus fabric and cement bags; management expects slower order growth as industry capacity is added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market share in converting machines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates a 25-35% share in converting machines, depending on the machine type.

risks_watch: Commodity (raw metal) price inflation and geopolitics: contracts lock prices for 6-9 months, so margin pressure can persist; EBITDA margin fell YoY to 19.4% in Q2.
Execution timing: customer site readiness, bank finance, and LC delays in exports can push dispatches beyond 6-9 months, and orders may spill into FY28.
Capacity ceiling near INR2,500 crores revenue; vendor capacity and balancing equipment needed to exceed it.
Expected FY28 deceleration to 10-15% growth after a 30-35% FY27 year, with domestic fabric-conversion demand cooling.
Recycling is an early-stage segment (about INR30-35 crores), with PET not a current focus and rigid recycling order book not yet established.
Balance-sheet disclosure: other current liabilities of INR478 crores, mainly customer advances (about 20% of order value). Management said it will consider reporting in crores for consistency.

Management was cautious on FY28 growth and margins, using ranges and caveats, and was evasive on order-level price versus volume splits and market share, which it said it could not provide.

So, as far as the EBITDA margins are concerned, we should look at somewhere in the range of 19% to 21%.
We definitely would be growing between 10% to 15% next year, because of our new offerings, because of the demand of the output that gets developed, generated from our machines.
So, currently, it is very, I mean, minuscule. This year we expect that the total revenue from the recycling piece of machinery would be around in the range of INR30 crores to INR35 crores.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: List prices were raised in February 2026 and July 2026, and orders booked after revisions are priced at new rates, though 6-9 month contracts carry no interim increase.

544844|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 68% YoY to INR210 crores and PAT 88% to INR25 crores, with an INR1,180 crore order book backing a 50% FY27 growth target.
544844|2026-09.overview: Poojaa Precision Engineering reported its maiden earnings call for H1 FY27 (half year ended September 30, 2026). Revenue from operations reached INR210 crores versus INR125 crores in H1 FY26, with EBITDA of INR40 crores (19% margin) and PAT of INR25 crores (12% margin). Non-automotive revenue grew 194% YoY to INR53 crores, lifting its share to 25% of sales from 15%. Management reiterated a target of about 50% growth in FY27, 30-35% CAGR thereafter, and INR1,000 crores of turnover by FY30, while capacity is being nearly doubled by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +68% YoY vs INR125 crores in H1 FY26
FY24 INR174 crores; FY25 INR222 crores; 30% CAGR
Last month sales INR42 crores; die stock INR20 crores

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Serves two-wheeler, three-wheeler, passenger and commercial vehicle components (intake manifolds, cylinder heads, crankcases, transmission housings) and EV parts. Accounted for 63% of H1 FY27 sales and about 52% of the INR1,180 crore order book; management said margin contribution was about 40% of H1 profit.

segments.name: Non-automotive / Engineering
segments.commentary: Covers power and energy distribution, agriculture, defence, healthcare and heavy engineering. Revenue of INR53 crores in H1 FY27 (25% of sales) and about 48% of the order book; contributed about 60% of H1 margins per management. Energy is the largest non-auto sector, followed by agriculture and healthcare.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 50% over FY26 (INR294 crores base), as reiterated on the call.
Revenue CAGR of 30-35% for FY28-FY30, with a target of INR1,000 crores annual turnover by FY30.
Order book execution path: about INR630-640 crores next year, INR800-820 crores the year after, and about INR1,000 crores by 2030 (management's framing).
Long-term mix target of 50:50 auto to non-auto within 2-3 years, and a longer-term 33:33:33 split across auto, EV and engineering.

Management expects all fixed costs of Unit 3 to be absorbed, so future margins should be driven by variable costs; it also said debt would be fully repaid by Q2 FY28, with finance cost minimal thereafter.
Aerospace (HAL / Indian Air Force) business expected to reach production in at least four years; defence to be served from Unit 3.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR1,180 crore order book split across H2 FY27, FY28 and FY29, and what does it include?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the book is about 52% auto and 48% non-auto, with execution of INR630-640 crore next year, INR800-820 crore the year after, and about INR1,000 crore by 2030, implying 30-35% CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: How much casting capacity will be installed this year and next, and what utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Machines are booked and expected by September 2027, with about 20% of the new capacity used this year and full installation next year; utilisation to ramp through 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Is aerospace business serviced from current or new capacity, and what is its timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: HAL approved the company for prototype parts and the Indian Air Force cleared its audit; production expected in at least four years, with aerospace moving to a separate Unit 4 and defence served from Unit 3.

qa_highlights.question: How is aluminium price movement handled in COGS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts with customers pass through metal price changes, so there is no net impact on performance; a later analyst question also got confirmation of full pass-through with a time lag.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital normalise, and is the inventory build a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is about INR60 crore versus last month's sales of INR42 crore (about 45 days), including INR20 crore of die stock with a 6-9 month cycle; management said dies will remain at 7-8% of sales and the normal cycle should stay near one month.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin split between auto and non-auto, and how will it evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: In H1 FY27 non-auto contributed about 60% of margins and auto about 40%; management declined to quantify margin by sub-sector, citing product-mix changes over the next 6-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for the INR1,000 crore FY30 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a RFQ pipeline above INR2,000 crore a year, an 8-10% strike rate, INR160-180 crore of new business added annually, and five demand drivers (China+1, Make in India, lightweighting, EV, aluminium substitution).

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth target and PAT margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 50% growth in FY27, 30-35% CAGR in FY28-30; debt to be fully repaid by Q2 FY28, with PAT margins expected to rise as fixed costs are absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offloading charge in other expenses (around 10% of revenue)?
qa_highlights.answer: Simple components are machined outside, while critical machining and processes such as powder coating, surface treatment and tooling are offloaded to optimise in-house capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix of GDC, LPDC and HPDC, and the alloy sourcing split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 70% GDC and 25% LPDC with 5% HPDC (later corrected); about 40% of alloy is bought as primary and converted, and 60% is bought as ready alloys from validated customer-linked sources.

544847|2026-06.headline: Manipal Health Q1 FY27 revenue rose over 38% YoY to INR3,091 crores, with network EBITDA of INR749 crores (up over 26%), volume-led.
544847|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's first earnings call after listing. Revenue was INR3,091 crores (up over 38% YoY) and network EBITDA INR749 crores (up over 26%; over 30% excluding a one-off gain in Q1 FY26). Growth was volume-led: IP volumes up about 39% and OP up 26%, with occupancy at 65% and ALOS at 2.7 days. Sahyadri (acquired, about 6-7 months in) grew revenue 13% to INR332 crores with EBITDA margin near 17.5%, while ex-Sahyadri margin was 25% versus 26.5% a year earlier, which management attributed to greenfield ramp-up and one-offs. Management also announced the Kinder Hospital (Whitefield, Bangalore, 100 beds) acquisition and reiterated bed additions and capex.

segments.name: Centres of Excellence (6 high-acuity specialties)
segments.commentary: Cardiac Sciences, Oncology, Neurology, Gastroenterology, Orthopaedics and Renal Sciences rose to about 65% of Q1 revenue, with IP revenue in these specialties up 45%. Oncology share grew from 10.8% to 12.2% at network level.

segments.name: Sahyadri Hospitals (9 hospitals, Pune)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR332 crores (up over 13%), EBITDA INR58 crores (up about 19%), margin about 17-17.5%. Integration is planned over 16-18 months; full rebranding to Manipal expected in about 14-16 months from integration.

segments.name: East region (AMRI, Medica, Columbia Asia)
segments.commentary: Top line grew 17% in the quarter, with cash and TPA business up 22% while government business was flat. AMRI grew 17% and Medica 15%.

segments.name: Greenfield hospitals
segments.commentary: Kanakapura broke even at EBITDA in month 5 and Yelahanka in month 2. Two older Bangalore greenfields are at about 13% margin in Q1, ahead of plan.

guidance_outlook: No specific numeric guidance; management said Q1 trends are secular tailwinds, not one-offs, but declined to guide to a core growth number.
Sahyadri margin expected to move closer to the portfolio over the next few quarters; management declined to give a target number or timeline.

Bed additions: Electronic City (about 300 beds) in Q2 FY27; Raipur in Q4 FY27; Nashik added 103 beds in Q1; Kinder (100 beds) possibly accelerated into FY27 as additional beds; Ahilya Nagar about 80 beds in FY28.
Capex: about INR2,000 crores in FY27, with about INR900 crores already spent in Q1; about INR4,000 crores over the next 3-4 years for about 3,000 beds.
Leverage comfort range of 1.5-2x net debt to EBITDA; debt repayment planned in Q2 FY27 from IPO proceeds.
capex_capacity: Bed count over 13,000; 50th hospital (Electronic City, Bangalore, about 300 beds) launched in July 2026, taking Bangalore to about 3,000 licensed beds across 13 facilities.
Nashik brownfield added 103 beds, taking licensed capacity to 307 beds; linear accelerator and PET-CT installed.

Kinder Hospital (Whitefield, Bangalore) acquisition of 100 beds including land and building; expected transfer within about 60 days after CPs; to be closed for 6-7 months for remodelling into multispecialty.
Raipur greenfield due Q4 FY27; Juhu (Mumbai) next; Wakad (Pune) greenfield started; Sahyadri expansions at Deccan Gymkhana (new tower), Hadapsar and Nashik oncology capacity (100-plus beds).
New equipment: AI-assisted neuro biplane cath lab at Mukundapur (Kolkata); OCT at MHB Old Airport Road and two other Bangalore sites; Dhakuria (Kolkata) extra beds due next quarter.
demand_pricing: Volume-led growth: IP volumes up about 39% and OP volumes up 26% YoY; management stressed volume over price-led ARPOB growth.
Ex-Sahyadri ARPOB INR77,200/day (up about 9%); Sahyadri ARPOB about INR45,000/day (up 15%).

Scheme collections (government schemes) were slow in Q1, which management said is a sector-wide issue; government mix in East is shifting as a national scheme replaces current schemes, with the authority discussion expected to conclude shortly.
International patients grew about 55% YoY but remain about 3% of revenue; government payers about 14% of institutional mix.
CONGO-R mix about 65% for the network and growing about 45%; complexity mix at Sahyadri is similar to Manipal network.

qa_highlights.question: How will Sahyadri's margin close the gap to corporate average and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sahyadri reached about 17.5% EBITDA margin in Q1 on volume and clinical enhancement, with integration over 16-18 months. No numeric target or timeline was given for reaching network margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ex-Sahyadri margin outlook and the greenfield drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-Sahyadri margin was 25% vs 26.5% last year; management cited about 0.6pp from a one-off Q1 FY26 reversal of INR15 crores, about 0.5pp from fully staffed greenfield doctor costs, and slower scheme collections. Greenfields are expected to ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: Is core standalone growth sustainable beyond Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 trends are not one-offs and called them secular tailwinds from volume growth, high-acuity specialties, and greenfield ramp-up, without guiding to a specific core growth figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kinder acquisition's margin and rationale given its small size?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Kinder revenue is about INR3-4 crores per month (about INR22 crores run-rate); management said the current EBITDA is irrelevant as the asset will be remodelled into multispecialty, with radiation oncology and transplants excluded. Rationale is adding capacity in the Whitefield micro-market.

qa_highlights.question: What capex and leverage should be assumed for the next few years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR2,000 crores (INR900 crores spent in Q1); about INR4,000 crores over 3-4 years for 3,000 beds. Net debt/EBITDA about 2.8x now, falling to about 0.9x after Q2 debt repayment; comfort range 1.5-2x.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to move medical colleges into the listed entity?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the listed company will remain a specialty tertiary and quaternary hospital provider and will not dilute that focus.

544851|2026-06.headline: MV Electrosystems expects propulsion output to ramp from 10 units in September to about 40 per month by January, against an order book of 564 propulsion systems worth about INR989 crores.
544851|2026-06.overview: This was the first investor call after the company's listing, with no reported financials in the transcript. Management said deliveries have been limited to 2 or 3 small batches so far, with none in the prior two months, and that IPO proceeds (working capital) now fund a scale-up. Management targets about INR400 crore of revenue this year and roughly 10% PAT once run-rate is reached, though it conceded margins are negative or constrained during the initial ramp. Growth optionality was discussed across EMU/MEMU/Vande Bharat distributed propulsion, OHE auto fault locators (with PNC Technologies), and marine/electrical adjacencies.

financial_highlights.metric: Supply price per locomotive propulsion system
financial_highlights.value: INR1.67 crore (AMC roughly matches this figure over 3 years)

financial_highlights.metric: Working capital requirement at ~INR1,000 crore turnover

financial_highlights.value: 105 days stated in prospectus; last three cycles completed in 85 days

segments.name: Locomotive propulsion systems
segments.commentary: Order book of 564 units valued at about INR989 crore; ramp planned at 10 units in September, 25 in November, 40 per month by January. Capacity built for 55 per month, with 40 chosen as the stable target.

segments.name: EMU/MEMU/Vande Bharat distributed propulsion
segments.commentary: INR86 crore MCF EMU development order with 24-month supply window; design and development targeted in 8-10 months, then approval taking about 15-16 months in total. A 12-coach EMU is about INR16 crore and a 16-coach Vande Bharat about INR40 crore including electrics.

segments.name: Overhead electrification (OHE) / AFL
segments.commentary: Auto fault locator tied up with PNC Technologies (South Korea). Management pegged unit prices at INR12 lakh (sectioning/sub-sectioning) to INR36 lakh (substation transformer), roughly INR1 crore of revenue per transformer section, with installations expected over 5-7 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR400 crore, described as achievable definitively.
Monthly run-rate of about 40 propulsion systems from January, implying roughly INR70 crore a month and about 480 units a year.
PAT of 10%-plus expected once run-rate is reached; management expects profitability within 2-3 months and margins to improve month over month after stabilisation.
R&D spend to be 3%-4% of revenue over time; R&D team to be expanded with a new centre ready by Q3.
Approximately 15-16 months to EMU propulsion approval including development.
capex_capacity: Capacity built for 55 locomotive propulsion systems per month; company plans to run at 40 for consistency, with spare capacity earmarked for EMU propulsion.
Unit 2 already set up; box fabrication and assembly to start the following Monday after the call.
No further machinery capex planned; only test setups are required, with three more ordered and installations expected in 45-60 days.
Two additional shifts planned in the existing factory, cited as enabling about 4,500 systems.
demand_pricing: Management cited Indian Railways building about 1,600-1,700 locomotives a year, about 15,000 locomotives in service needing rehabilitation, and 300-500 EMUs tendered or to be tendered this year.

Locomotive tenders in pipeline: CLW tender for about 748 locomotives (expected around 31 August), followed by BLW and PLW tenders, expected over the next few weeks; more than 100 EMU propulsion tenders and 200 train-set electrical tenders published by ICF Chennai, not yet bid.

Company said it won about 25-26% of tendered locomotive propulsion quantity, with competitors including Siemens, Alstom, ABB, Medha and BHEL. In the last tender, 7 suppliers were awarded small quantities.
Management said margins were very thin across bidders; company was L2 in two tenders and L1 in one. Bulk purchasing (200-300 sets) was cited as offsetting electronics price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the PLW/CLW propulsion tender cancellation affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was unaware of any cancellation and noted an active CLW tender for 748 locomotives. Tender-to-order conversion typically takes 45 days, sometimes up to 90.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company meet the December 26 order deadline, and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply obligations extend to March and into next financial year. Output is planned at 10 units in September, 25 in November, and 40 in January; extensions are typically granted for capacity-constrained suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: What margins apply given rising electronics costs and no price-escalation clause?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 10%-plus PAT at full run-rate; early months will have constrained or negative margins. Bulk procurement of 200-300 sets is offsetting global price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement lead times range from 7 days to 6 months, averaging about 45 days. Payments were received within 15 days on all three dispatches. Working capital of about INR200 crore needed for roughly INR1,000 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation per propulsion system?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply price is INR1.67 crore per locomotive propulsion system; AMC over three years roughly matches that figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EMU/MCF approval process and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Three-month validation at the MCF commissioning depot, performance trials on Delhi-Ambala Road, then a four-month trial covering about 30,000 km before approval.

544867|2026-06.headline: Dhoot Transmission Q1 FY27: revenue up nearly 50% YoY, wiring harness revenue Rs 1,090 crore (+44.6%), EBITDA margin ~15%; FY27 growth guided at 25-30%.
544867|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong first quarter as its first post-listing call, with growth of nearly 50% YoY, wiring harness revenue up 44.6% and non-wiring harness up 67.7%. EV revenue grew 79% and rose to 27% of total revenue from 24% a year earlier. EBITDA margin improved 110 bps QoQ to about 15%, while raw-material (copper, brass) inflation continued and is being passed through to customers with a roughly three-month lag. Management guided to 15-16% full-year EBITDA margin and 25-30% growth for FY27, while flagging a soft comparison in the first half from last year's GST-driven demand.

financial_highlights.change: Ahead of domestic 2W volumes (>20%) and exports (>36%)
+67.7% YoY vs Rs 213 crore; ~3% of overall growth from Multilink (about 20 days consolidated)
Up from 24% a year ago; EV revenue +79% YoY
Expected to turn to net cash after August IPO proceeds; management indicated ~Rs 1,000 crore net cash around end-August

segments.name: Wiring harness
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,090 crore in Q1 FY27, up 44.6% YoY from Rs 753 crore. Management says localisation has cut imported components from 30-35% to 20-25% of the component base.

segments.name: Non-wiring harness (EV components, battery packs, controllers, sensors, switches)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 358 crore, up 67.7% YoY, with Multilink adding about 10-12 points of that growth. Battery packs are the major portion; a second top customer in the South started supply in the last month of the quarter.

segments.name: Multilink (acquired)
segments.commentary: Contributed ~3% to overall revenue growth for the ~20-day period in Q1. Management expects 25-30% growth and margins in line with the group; full integration in about 3-4 months, adding Hero as a customer plus fuel level sensors and relays.

IPO proceeds to fund expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur plants, adding ~15-20% capacity this year; IPO utilisation update promised next quarter.

Management said the Q1 margin was impacted by a hard commodity cycle, not by mix shift toward battery packs.
Wage-hike cost is recovered from customers through annual discussions, per management.
Management says it has not lost ICE market share, despite an analyst comparison suggesting it had.

qa_highlights.question: How much more margin expansion is possible, and when does copper pass-through normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Kalani said most copper inflation is passed through, but prices kept rising for 4-5 months, so there is some impact. Guidance is kept at 15-16% full-year EBITDA margin; Q2 recovery is unlikely and Q3 is the earliest, if prices are stable.

qa_highlights.question: Cash position and FCF at end-June?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was about Rs 220 crore at end-June, after the March Bain infusion and part Multilink impact. Post-IPO money (received in August) should turn the company to net cash, with ~Rs 1,000 crore indicated by end-August.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of non-wiring harness revenue and EBITDA margin expectations for Multilink?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakup by product is not disclosed due to single-customer concentration. Non-wiring harness grew 67.7%, with Multilink adding 10-12 points for its ~20-day contribution. Multilink margins are expected to be in line with group margins.

qa_highlights.question: Wiring harness revenue and prior-year split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: wiring harness Rs 1,090 crore and non-wiring harness Rs 358 crore. Q1 FY26: Rs 753 crore and Rs 213 crore, respectively.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity given 75-80% utilisation?

544867|2026-09.headline: Dhoot Transmission Q2 FY27: organic revenue growth ~60% YoY, EV share 31%, FY27 growth guidance raised to 40%-45% and capex to ~Rs 750 crore.

Pre-exceptional PAT was Rs 162 crore, up 30% YoY, and the IPO-linked debt was fully repaid with net cash, bank and FD balance at about Rs 900 crore. Capex guidance for FY27 was raised to about Rs 750 crore and revenue growth guidance to more than 40% (later stated as 40%-45%), citing customer demand well above earlier plans.

544868|2026-06.headline: Milky Mist Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR973.45 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9% and gross margin up about 270 bps to 34.2%.
544868|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR973.45 crore, up 44% YoY, led by paneer, cheese, curd, ice cream and yogurt. Gross profit was about INR333 crore (34.2% margin, up ~270 bps), EBITDA INR144.89 crore (14.9% margin vs 12.24% a year earlier) and PAT INR64.67 crore (6.6% margin). Management attributed margin gains to product mix, a ~10.5% price increase taken in Q4 FY26, and scale. The call was the company's first earnings call after listing; several figures were corrected on the call during the prepared remarks.

segments.name: Paneer
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at INR248.29 crore, up 34% in both volume and revenue; management linked this to zero GST on paneer from September 2025 and FSSAI/state bans on analogue paneer. Company claims ~20% share of the organised paneer market.

segments.name: Yogurt (incl. protein range)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR84.5 crore, up 153%; management calls it a key margin driver, with Greek yogurt and Skyr in the protein range.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Volume +45%, revenue +60% YoY, aided by extended summer; management expects demand to stay robust around the year in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

segments.name: Cheese
segments.commentary: Revenue +38% YoY; new natural cheddar plant commissioned in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day capacity. Company says cheese sales come from retail, modern trade and quick-commerce, not QSRs.

segments.name: Curd
segments.commentary: Revenue +27% YoY.

segments.name: Regional mix
segments.commentary: South ~69% of revenue, growing ~44% YoY; non-South ~31%, growing ~50% YoY. Management expects a drift toward 60:40 over time.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to add INR150-200 crore of incremental revenue versus H1 (as stated on the call).
Operating margin: management guided to about 0.5% leverage benefit from scale; asked whether 18% EBITDA margin is achievable in 3-4 years, CFO said 'you can expect that' but CEO declined to quantify.
Maharashtra plant: at drawing-board stage, about three years out; the company aims for 40% utilisation from day one at break-even.
Revenue potential from Perundurai at current MRP: 3x to 3.5x FY26 revenue (as stated on the call).
Plans to deploy more than 50,000 visi coolers, ice cream freezers and chocolate coolers over the next three fiscal years.
Whey protein concentrate plant expected to be operational in about 15-18 months from the call.
capex_capacity: Commissioned new natural cheddar cheese plant in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day installed capacity.

Capex in the RHP: about INR500 crore plus INR150 crore, about INR650-700 crore in total; another ~INR380 crore WIP carried from last year. CFO said capex is funded through IPO proceeds and bank funding, with no cash-flow pressure this year.
Planned expansion covers whey protein concentrate, lactose, natural cheese, processed cheese and yogurt capacity.
Capacity utilisation: CEO said more than 12 product categories have spare capacity; paneer utilisation is about 50%.

Milk procurement averaged 13.2 lakh litres per day in Q1 FY27, up 28% YoY. Third-party share is about 10-12% of volume, and the company is expanding direct procurement in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 10.5% taken in Q4 FY26 (stated as ~11% in one answer); management said this offset milk and input inflation and produced a 2.7% margin expansion net.
Trade spend: about 4.5-5% trade discount from MRP to billing and another 4.5-5% on marketing/promotion.
Milk costs are about 50-55% of input cost; landed cost is INR45/litre (farmer price INR41-42). Aavin raised farmgate prices by INR3 twice recently; management is still studying pass-through.
Pricing is set after a 2-3 month lag following input cost increases, per CFO.
Management said the company has no B2B or QSR sales other than whey powder from cheese and paneer making.

qa_highlights.question: Third-party milk procurement strategy and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party share is about 10-12% through a five-year exclusive contract with MilkLane (linked to a PE-owned entity). Management says payments go directly to farmers and that quality premiums are about 50 paise/litre, with no financial dilution.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin resilience amid milk price inflation and further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credits product mix (paneer +34%, cheese +38%, yogurt +150%, ice cream +60%) and pricing. Price hikes follow a 2-3 month lag after input costs. About 10.5% price increase taken last year.

qa_highlights.question: Freight and logistics model with a single plant serving distant cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-owned fleet of about 375 vehicles with return-load logistics saves ~18-20% on logistics cost. Shelf life of 30+ days (vs 24-48 hours for pouch milk) makes one plant viable.

qa_highlights.question: Low base in Q1 FY26 and seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 weakness was price-driven (GST and milk rationalisation), not volume-driven. Ice cream is strong in summer and robust year-round in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

qa_highlights.question: Whey protein plans and high-protein B2C products?
qa_highlights.answer: The company generates about 1 million litres of cheese whey daily and currently sells whey powder B2B. A whey protein concentrate plant is due in 15-18 months; high-protein RTD products are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Yield per animal and farmer support?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement volume is up 28% YoY. Initiatives include bank credit via Kisan Credit Cards, herd-size expansion, AI/breeding, feed and health camps.

risks_watch: Milk procurement cost inflation: Aavin raised farmgate prices by INR3 twice recently and a report cites Tamil Nadu procurement price hikes of around 15%; management is still studying pass-through and has not confirmed price action beyond the 10.5% taken in Q4 FY26.

Third-party milk share (~10-12%, via MilkLane under a five-year exclusive contract linked to a PE-owned entity): watch whether this share falls as direct procurement expands in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra, and any impact on quality costs.

Paneer growth dependence on zero GST from September 2025 and state/FSSAI analogue paneer bans; the price gap between organised and unorganised players is now near nil, so volume gains depend on enforcement continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Unit 3 capacity, commissioning timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 3 is targeted to commence in Q1 FY28; shed is under construction and most machinery is ordered. Exact capex not disclosed pending exchange filing; total FY27 capex target is about INR80 crore across IPO proceeds, internal accruals and solar.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence and aerospace opportunity and when will revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders have come from Bharat Dynamics, Nuclear Power Corporation of India and private suppliers; a small revenue stream has started in prototyping. Management expects good numbers from FY28, with no quantified mix target; approval cycles are long.

qa_highlights.question: Update on centrifugal casting and foundry expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 3 will be a foundry with vertical and horizontal centrifugal casting for ICDP and HSS rolls, targeted for production next year. Management also cited thermal power demand visibility to 2035 and a recent 22-23 ton single-piece casting.

qa_highlights.question: Do you have order book or inquiries for ICDP/HSS rolls, when does commercial production start, and what are the entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing customers buying static metal rolls would be the buyers for ICDP/HSS rolls and trial orders could come from day one; it cited scrap access, existing heat treatment and machining, and 21-country export reach as barriers. No quantified order book for these grades was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR80 crore FY27 capex has been spent in Q1, and what is the post-expansion high-value mix and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: INR5 crore was spent in Q1 and INR75 crore is planned over the next three quarters. High-value share is targeted at around 70% in the near future, and operating EBITDA margin (cited as around 25% in prior years) is expected to grow 20-25% over two to three years.

544871|2026-06.headline: Shiprocket Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% to INR592 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 9x to INR8.9 crore and emerging segment losses narrowing.

Core revenue rose 22% to INR412 crore at a 12.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, up 50 bps YoY. Emerging revenue rose 70% to INR180 crore, and its adjusted EBITDA margin improved from -38% to -24%. qa_highlights.question: What is the emerging EBITDA margin trajectory, and when could emerging reach break-even?

qa_highlights.question: Why did core CAC rise to about INR3,600 from INR3,100 a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CAC fluctuates with experiments across channels and reactivation, has held steady for years, and is not seasonal. It said the focus is break-even, with CAC of about INR3,000 recovering margin quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Are 3PLs moving into D2C and SMB, and does that threaten Shiprocket?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its model is to integrate with leading 3PLs and that the D2C segment, which makes up most of INR32,000 crore GMV, is its focus. It said data and integrated stack are its advantage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power ARPU rise about 25% while power merchant count fell slightly?

544871|2026-09.headline: Shiprocket Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% to INR670+ crore and adjusted EBITDA hit INR14.2 crore (2.1% margin), with PAT turning positive.
544871|2026-09.overview: Shiprocket reported Q2 FY27 revenue of about INR670 crore, up 35% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of INR14.2 crore versus INR4 crore a year ago. Core (shipping) revenue was about INR460 crore (up 25%) at a 12.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, while Emerging (MarTech, Omnichannel, Cross-border) revenue was about INR210 crore (up 61%) with its margin improving to -21.2% from -31.5%. PAT was about INR6 million against a loss of about INR20 crore a year ago; management attributed roughly 70% of the swing to operating improvement and the rest to lower ESOP cost and post-IPO other income. Management said the core contribution margin held at about 21.1%, and that growth was volume-led rather than price-led.
