segments.commentary: Revenue about INR460 crore (+25%), transactions +31%, contribution margin about INR97 crore at 21.1%, adjusted EBITDA about INR59 crore at 12.8% margin. Management says the gap between volume and revenue growth reflects courier mix, larger merchants and lower-yield hyper-local categories.

segments.name: Emerging (MarTech, Omnichannel, Cross-border)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR210 crore (+61%), adjusted EBITDA about -INR45 crore (-21.2% margin). MarTech (rebranded Fastrr) grew 102% and powers about US$1.3 billion (about INR11,200 crore) annualised GMV; Omnichannel grew 79%; Cross-border grew 9%.

segments.name: Platform KPIs
segments.commentary: TTM transactions 233 million, TTM GMV about INR37,400 crore, over 236,000 active merchants. Quarterly GMV +33%, transactions +34%, merchants about +8%, revenue per merchant +25%. Paying active merchants reached over 2.3 lakh this quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects core margins to stay largely stable in the short term and improve over the longer run as fixed costs are spread over a growing base; no quarterly timeline was given.
Core operating leverage expected to be greater at the EBITDA line than at contribution margin; overhead growth to be well below revenue growth at this scale.
Q3 is seasonally weak on volume, not margin, per management; YoY there is no damage.

Finance cost and other income benefits from IPO (third week of August) reflected only about half a quarter in Q2.
capex_capacity: Shiprocket is carrier-neutral with 42+ courier partners and 250+ ecosystem partners, and owns no fleet.

AI courier selection (RADAR) routes orders by pincode and lane, and flags stressed lanes; management cited an example where 20-30 of 379 Chandigarh pincodes were stressed but under 4% of volume moved through them.
Omnichannel is investing in its own network, which keeps Emerging margins slightly lower in the short term.
Core is investing in AI, experience centres and customer acquisition; management said CAC is worthwhile if it pays back in under one year.
Agentic Analytics assistant in beta with about 1,000 users.
demand_pricing: Core yield fell roughly 4-5% (volume +31% vs revenue +25%). Management attributed this to customer mix, courier mix and lower-yield hyper-local categories, and said fuel costs were passed through rather than absorbed.
Management said growth is volume-led and not price-led; contribution margin grew faster than revenue (+43% vs +35%).
Over 90% of the business is D2C. Management said it is not changing its offering in response to supplier strategy, after a 3PL partner signalled a D2C focus.
MarTech: fewer than 10% of merchants use it; about 20,000 merchants on checkout; management claims 10-20% better conversion than the market. Competition exists in checkout.
Omnichannel: serves D2C brands with slotted replenishment to quick commerce dark stores (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart), 97% SLA claimed, and is paid by brands rather than by quick commerce platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Are core margins (about 21.1% contribution, ~12.8% EBITDA) steady-state, and when will they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Saahil Goel said margins are stable in the short term and should improve over the long run as fixed people costs are spread over more customers and ARPU. He declined to give a timeline. Tanmay Kumar said core operating leverage is greater at EBITDA than at contribution margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core realisation fall about 4-5% while volume grew 31%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield is driven by customer-cohort mix, larger merchants and courier mix, and that fuel costs were passed through. It said the top-five-customer explanation was not what it meant and gave no exact walk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy in food delivery, and is Eternal a conflict as a shareholder?
qa_highlights.answer: Restaurants are a new category using Fastrr ads, checkout and hyper-local delivery integrations, not a marketplace play. Management said Eternal is a financial investor and sees no conflict.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3PL partner's D2C push a risk to Shiprocket?
qa_highlights.answer: Saahil Goel said more than 90% of the business is D2C, that the offering will not change based on supplier preferences, and that growth trends show no visible impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q3 seasonality a growth or margin issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 is lower volume only, because brands shift to marketplaces during festive periods, and margins are not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Emerging revenue growth sustainable, and will overhead keep falling as a share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Tanmay Kumar said MarTech growth should continue because the same decision-maker buys several products and only about 20,000 merchants use checkout. He said core overhead growth will be much lower than revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why are power merchants flat or declining, and what are the unit economics of Omnichannel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARPU is rising and power merchants will grow as newly acquired paying merchants mature. Omnichannel customers are merchants, not quick commerce platforms, and margins are similar to logistics-style businesses.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 55% YoY growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were approximately the same YoY, so growth came from product mix and customer relationships. No quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin, given EBITDA of about 14% in Q1 after 9.5% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins move quarter to quarter with product mix and that the company focuses on profit amount rather than percentage. It did not commit to a sustainable margin range.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: The company buys gold equal to what it sells on the same day at market price. Inventory is carried at a weighted-average cost that management says is below market, so no hedging is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion comes from product mix and how much from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix was one factor and gold-price gains add 1-3 percentage points YoY. Analysts disputed that Q1 had gold gains, and management gave no split.

qa_highlights.question: How is growth funded and what is the working-capital cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Profits are reinvested, and the bank lines are open. The IPO raised equity to about INR450 crore to fund working capital. Management said the business needs more working capital as it grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers moving karigar work in-house, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said handcrafted, co-created bridal designs and long-standing relationships protect the business. It gave no figures to show the moat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did job-worker count fall and employee cost drop QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers larger, organised contract manufacturers. Employee cost fell because Q4 included an ex-gratia payment to directors, which will not recur.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14% vs 9.5% in Q4 FY26; management gave no sustainable range and said margins move with product mix. Track next quarter's gross and EBITDA margin against this base.

Unquantified growth drivers: 55% revenue growth attributed to mix and relationships with volumes described only as 'approximately same'; volume split and gold-price contribution (management cited 1-3 pp YoY) were not quantified. Watch for the promised Q2/Q3 volume data.

Working capital and funding: trade receivables of INR126 crore (about 22-23 days), inventory turnover about 8x, and management saying working capital needs keep growing; IPO proceeds (INR38 crore working-capital portion) are a key use to track against bank line usage.

Customer in-housing and moat: analysts questioned whether large customers such as Kalyan and P.N. Gadgil moving to in-house karigars threatens the outsourced model; management gave no share or retention figures.

Gold-price hedging and inventory accounting: hedging relies on a same-day buy-to-sell policy and weighted-average inventory valued below market; management did not show the inventory gain component, which analysts disputed for Q1.

544885|2026-06.headline: Gaja AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR27.2 crores; total income up 26% to INR51.8 crores.

Performance income of INR29.7 crores (+17% YoY) drove most of the income, while management fee income of about INR16 crores grew 7%. Cost-to-income improved to 38.4% from 42.3%. 544886|2026-06.headline: Tempsens Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR118 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 25.3% on higher employee cost.

Management guided FY27 revenue growth in line with the three-year blended growth rate and said margins should recover in H2 FY27. Four capacity projects with aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores are slated to commission between Q4 FY27 and Q3 FY28.

Management said the core SPOT platform PAT rose to Rs.85 Crores from Rs.34 Crores a year earlier, with PAT margin at 0.65% versus 0.18%, while enterprise revenue fell 32% as the company shifted sourcing toward recycled scrap gold, which ties up working capital for about four days versus under two for imported bars. Consumer (Gold For All) revenue rose 47% YoY and accounted for 13% of revenue versus 7% in FY26. Management declined to give revenue, margin or volume guidance, and said the IPO primary proceeds (Rs.625 Crores net of expenses) were deployed into working capital.

544889|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR218 crores, while new-business opex drag of INR23 crores left consolidated EBITDA at INR45 crores.
544889|2026-06.overview: Symbiotec's first earnings call after its BSE/NSE listing reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR218 crores (+7% YoY), with API revenue of INR215 crores (+6% YoY, volume-led) and API EBITDA of INR66 crores (+9% YoY). Consolidated EBITDA was INR45 crores and net profit about INR14 crores, which management said understates underlying profitability because of INR23 crores of new-business opex and INR11 crores of depreciation that were previously capitalised as pre-operative expenses. No CDMO or injectable revenue was booked in the quarter, versus about INR33 crores of milestone revenue in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of roughly 20% revenue growth and 25% EBITDA growth, with a plus/minus 5% band, and pinned new-business revenue to milestones in H2 FY27 and commercial CDMO revenue to the next 6 to 12 months.

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR227 crore, up 16% YoY; H1 up 11%, driven mainly by volume and product/geography mix. Gross margin above 60%, EBITDA margin around 30%. Management guides high-single-digit growth with possible low-double-digit upside; about 70% of the business is regulated markets.

segments.name: Complex injectables (DCV platform)
segments.commentary: Long-term US agreement signed 30 Sep 2026 for 2 complex injectable products; INR53 crore milestone recognised in Q2 and balance to follow in later quarters. First ANDA filed Sep 2026, second planned in Q4 FY27; commercial product supply expected FY28, with profit share as a third revenue stream.

segments.name: Fermentation CDMO / biomanufacturing
segments.commentary: Ujjain site has 400 KL fermentation capacity. A 10-year take-or-pay contract with a US alt-protein company expects commercial batches in Q1 FY28. A new 10-year take-or-pay agreement with a European alt-protein company starts Phase 0 at the existing 100 KL scale, with Phase 1 (750 KL, up from 600 KL previously guided) taking 12-15 months to build.

segments.name: Biologics (insulin drug substance)
segments.commentary: Plant at 14 KL scale with capex just over INR100 crore; validation batches expected Q4 FY27, sales from mid FY28 after approvals, about 2 months later than earlier expectation. Around 50% of capacity committed to an Indian customer on a 5-year take-or-pay contract.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: approximately 20% revenue growth and around 25% EBITDA growth, with a plus or minus 5 percentage point range.
Milestone income from the DCV deal to continue across remaining FY27 quarters and at similar yearly intensity in FY28, though not linear quarter to quarter.

Fermentation: Phase 0 production at existing 100 KL from around end of FY27; Phase 1 commercial revenue mainly in FY29, with management saying FY29 would be the strongest year for toll fees of a few tens of millions of dollars.
Vegan vitamin D3: plant qualification by end FY27; sales to nutraceutical and veterinary markets from early FY28; pharma D3 may need another year. Pricing not yet decided.
Corporate capex to be kept at INR200-300 crore per year, with customers expected to fund a significant part of CDMO capex.
Management targets margins of at least 30% ROCE, 30-40% EBITDA margin and 70-80% gross margin across bio and pharma businesses.
capex_capacity: Ujjain fermentation site: 400 KL operational capacity today; 32 acres in possession plus about 40 acres recently acquired, for a 70-72 acre site.

European alt-protein deal: Phase 0 uses existing 100 KL, needing about 3 more months of fine-tuning; Phase 1 is 750 KL (up from 600 KL guided last quarter), with 12-15 months build; Phase 2 takes total to a few million litres. Estimated cost to reach Phase 2 about INR1,000 crore, largely customer-funded (undisclosed split).

Insulin drug substance plant (biologics, 14 KL): capex just over INR100 crore; validation batches in Q4 FY27; sales expected mid FY28 after regulatory approvals; about 50% of capacity committed to an Indian customer.
DCV: 20 million vial facility referenced by analyst; bag and syringe formats have proof of concept but no capex committed yet; capex decision expected in a quarter or two.
Vegan D3 plant under construction, qualification targeted by end FY27.
Over INR1,000 crore invested in the new business verticals to date.
demand_pricing: API price pressure continues across verticals; growth in Q2 attributed mainly to volume and product/geography mix. Management says steroid hormone growth remains high single digit.

Freight and solvent costs rose recently (Middle East conflict cited); management estimates a 2-3% hit to gross margin, seen as partly temporary, mitigated by backward integration and make-vs-buy choices.
Management says it has about 4 bio-manufacturing customers at advanced discussion stage, with traction also in the DCV space (3-4 more products in pipeline; talks with Europe and China partners).

Alt-protein CDMO: management cites the US customer's 10-year contract at about USD7-8 million per year, with inflation escalators; the European customer's toll fees are a few tens of millions of dollars at Phase 1.
Classical fermentation: 6-10 products in the pipeline, 2 commercialised for India; regulated-market entry 2-3 years away.
Premarin: API development done to FDA expectations; partner formulation in progress; launch likely years away with a generic already on market.

qa_highlights.question: Opportunity size of the European alt-protein deal and expected returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers. It is a 10-year take-or-pay with Phase 0 from 100 KL in FY27-end, Phase 1 (sub-million litres) in FY28 and Phase 2 above a million litres; toll fees start at a few tens of millions of dollars and could scale further. FY29 is expected to be the strongest year.

qa_highlights.question: Is DCV milestone income recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarter-on-quarter intensity may vary but year-on-year it should be similar; milestones are expected to continue even after product sales start. Milestones are not linear quarter to quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the API growth from volume or price, and is the mix sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth mainly came from volume plus mix. Price pressure persists across verticals. About 70% of the business is regulated markets with sticky customers. High-single-digit growth guided, with possible low double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the trade receivables rise from INR197 crore to INR268 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Milestone invoices were raised on 30 Sep 2026 and collection falls in the next quarter, so receivables should normalise in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the CDMO capacity rise from 600 KL to 750 KL, and what is the capex and customer share?
qa_highlights.answer: The customer chose 750 KL instead of 600 KL and the agreement was revised. Management would not disclose the customer share, but said a significant part of capex will come from customers. Corporate capex stays at INR200-300 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the insulin plant slipped and how much has been spent?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex just over INR100 crore. Revenue timing moved by a couple of months after a new biologics head changed plans for evolving regulatory standards. Only about 50% of capacity is committed to the Indian customer.

qa_highlights.question: DCV US approval timing?
qa_highlights.answer: ANDA accepted without refuse-to-receive (RTR); accelerated review granted; July goal date, but queries may delay approval. FDA inspection and ANDA approval are expected by late calendar 2027.

544890|2026-06.headline: Skyways Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores, with consolidated PAT margin at 2.2% versus 1.72%.
544890|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong Q1 FY27, with operating revenue up 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores and operating EBITDA up to INR50.12 crores from INR27.31 crores. Management attributed much of the revenue jump to per-unit freight cost increases driven by fuel indices, with volume growth of 23% in air cargo and 18% in ocean freight. Employee and other expenses fell as a share of revenue, lifting margins. The company also flagged a board-approved INR30 crore international office expansion and INR20 crore capital infusion into existing overseas subsidiaries, and repaid around INR140 crores of borrowings post-listing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state revenue run rate, given revenue has roughly doubled YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 23-25% of revenue growth came from volume and the rest from per-unit cost increases driven by fuel indices; it did not give a steady-state figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% volume growth sustainable, and is the realisation growth tied to fuel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of sustaining volume growth and aims to improve it; yield is market-driven and fuel is a pass-through. Focus is on higher-yield trade lanes.

qa_highlights.question: Gestation period and capex for new Asian offices?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical gestation is 2-4 years; management targets 2-3 years. About 15% of the INR30 crores is capex. Current footprint covers Hong Kong, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Bangladesh.

qa_highlights.question: Which markets get the INR20 crore subsidiary infusion?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Vietnam.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the digital booking platform?
qa_highlights.answer: Air, ocean and express are in pilot; trucking is in final development. Launch expected in 30-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the EOW matter in the prospectus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is sub judice and under investigation in final stages, and it sees no financial impact at present. No timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the post-listing debt repayment and capital raise drag ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said historical ROE is 14-15%, the September quarter will show the post-listing capital effect, and it targets around 15% over time. About INR140 crores of borrowings were repaid.

544891|2026-06.headline: Hy-Tech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR430 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 19.6% from 21.5%, which management blames on price-revision timing.
544891|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR430 million and PAT rose 11% to INR46 million, while EBITDA was flat at INR84 million and margin contracted about 190 bps. Management attributed the margin dip to input-cost increases from the Feb–April period whose OEM price revisions, effective 1 April, are expected to be recognised only in Q2, and a cut-off sales shift into the next quarter. This was the company's first earnings call after its 1 September listing on NSE and BSE. Management guided to ~20% revenue growth, 25–30% PAT growth and a 24–25% EBITDA margin for FY27, with capacity expansion and new-customer wins as the main drivers.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Around 25% of revenue from USA and 7–8% from Europe; total exports about 30%. Management said exports earn roughly 10% extra margin, and a weaker rupee adds to this.

segments.name: Domestic OEM
segments.commentary: OEMs are 70–80% of business. Management expects domestic business to grow 15–20%, and domestic sales are about INR120–130 crore at present.

segments.name: Domestic distributors
segments.commentary: About 10% of business through four distributors (Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Delhi, Pune); management sees 10–30% growth potential here.

Total addressable market cited as INR40,000 crore globally (USA INR20,000 crore, Europe INR10,000 crore, India INR2,000 crore, other INR8,000 crore). Management says it holds about 10% of India.
Sany (Chinese excavator maker) approached Hy-Tech to indigenise its fittings supply; management also expects tenders and government-linked OEMs to be added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue growth guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue to grow at least 20% YoY, with PAT growing 25–30% per year. Management said it has no formal order book, only annual schedules and contract prices from OEMs.

qa_highlights.answer: INR30 crore capex this year, to be implemented within one year. A 6.5-acre land purchase is planned for a future plant estimated at INR350–500 crore in 2–3 years; a US subsidiary is also being set up.

544891|2026-09.headline: Hy-Tech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22-32% YoY to INR60.9 crores with EBITDA of INR14.5 crores at a 23.8% margin.
544891|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR60.9 crores, up 22% YoY (management also cited 32% in its opening remarks) and up 41% QoQ. EBITDA rose 21% YoY to INR14.5 crores at a 23.8% margin, versus 19.6% in Q1, and PAT rose 23% YoY to INR8.5 crores. H1 FY27 revenue was INR103.9 crores (+18%), with EBITDA of INR22.9 crores (+14%) and PAT of INR13.1 crores (+19%). Management said a price revision agreed with customers after 7-8 years is being billed from H2, and guided FY27 PAT growth of about 18-25% (clarified as 20-22% this year and 24-25% in FY28).

financial_highlights.change: +22% YoY vs INR49.8 crores; +41% QoQ (management also cited 32% YoY in opening remarks)
vs 24% in Q2 FY26; vs 19.6% in Q1 FY27
+18% vs INR87.8 crores in H1 FY26
+19% vs INR11 crores; PAT margin 12.6%, stable

segments.name: Hydraulic fittings (core business)
segments.commentary: Management calls this the primary growth engine, with nearly 11,000 SKUs. Growth is coming from share-of-business gains at existing OEMs and new OEM onboarding. John Deere is about 12% of total turnover.

segments.name: Stainless steel double ferrule fittings (new)
segments.commentary: Development took about 2-2.5 years. Current business is INR8-10 crores, with margins about 5 percentage points higher than carbon steel. Railway and Engineers India registrations are done; results are expected in 1-2 years.

segments.name: US exports / aftermarket
segments.commentary: US business has been flat due to tariffs. A wholly-owned subsidiary and a warehouse in New Jersey were set up to supply John Deere, Caterpillar and Case New Holland. The US aftermarket is described as the bulk of demand.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 is expected to be stronger than H1. Management cited a historical split of about 45-46% of turnover in H1 and 53-55% in H2, and said H2 EBITDA margin will be about 24% or better.
Full-year FY27 PAT growth is guided at about 18-20% on the first call, clarified as 20-22% on this call. Management said FY27 revenue growth of 20% is achievable.
FY28 PAT growth is guided at about 24-25%, linked to the US tariff situation easing and new customer wins.
Management said revenue will double within 3 years and that the business could reach INR500 crores of turnover in 4-5 years using existing land and added machinery.

All price revisions are finalised and accepted by customers; the second half will be billed entirely at revised prices. About 25% of the earlier shortfall from the price change is still to be recovered.
capex_capacity: Current utilisation is about 70%, and management keeps about 20-30% free capacity for new customers as a policy.

Existing infrastructure (land and buildings) is sufficient for about INR500 crores of turnover; reaching that level requires more machinery. The new land parcel (6.5 acres at Shirwal) is for beyond INR500 crores, with a factory timeline of 2.5-3 years.
Investment is going into automated machinery, including rotary transfer machines.

INR30 crores from the IPO object is to be invested over about 1.5 years and is expected to support about INR100 crores of revenue. Management expects internally generated cash of about INR25-30 crores over 2 years to fund further capex.
demand_pricing: Order books are full: management said the company is 'completely booked' with schedules from all OEMs. Tractor demand is softening, offset by rising excavator demand.

Price revisions were agreed with customers after 7-8 years, partly due to the war situation. Management said the revision covered both raw material and conversion cost increases, and that only about 25% of the raw material pass-through had been recovered before this quarter.
Management said the company earns about a 10% price premium in the market and that MNCs such as Parker import and sell at about 2x Hy-Tech's prices.
Domestic market: the company has integrity clauses with OEMs not to sell their fittings in the domestic aftermarket. The US business is largely aftermarket through distributors.
India hydraulic fittings market: management estimated about INR2,000 crores of potential against current revenue of about INR190-200 crores. It described the market as growing about 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 growth continue, and will EBITDA margin expand? Is the 25-30% PAT growth target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 will be much better than H1, with EBITDA margin of about 24% guaranteed. H2 typically accounts for 53-55% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company recovered the Q1 revenue lost to the 1 April price revision?
qa_highlights.answer: Not fully. About 25% of the previous shortfall is still to be recovered, and management expects full recovery in the next half.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term growth outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PAT growth is about 20-22%, with FY28 at about 24-25%. The gap reflects flat US sales due to tariffs, which are expected to improve after the US midterm elections.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential of the current capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it runs at about 70% by policy and keeps 20% free capacity. It guided to about 25% annual growth, reaching INR500 crores in 4-5 years. The INR30 crores IPO spend is expected to support about INR100 crores of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price hike and pass-through lift gross margins back to 65%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the price revisions cover both raw material and conversion cost, so margins are being maintained. All revisions are finalised, and H2 will be billed at revised prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of John Deere and other OEM business, and what concentration risk exists?
qa_highlights.answer: About three John Deere plants are now supplying, and four have approved samples. John Deere is about 12% of turnover, with the ramp expected in FY28. Tata Hitachi and Sany are long-term, gradual contributors.

risks_watch: US tariff and midterm-election outcome: US growth has been flat, and management's FY28 growth guide depends on a recovery.
Customer concentration: John Deere is about 12% of turnover, and its ramp is still pending.
Recovery of the remaining ~25% of the Q1 price-revision shortfall, and whether H2 billing at revised prices lifts margins as expected.
Capacity and talent: growth beyond INR500 crores needs machinery, staff and a new factory 2.5-3 years away. Management cited people and structure as a constraint.
New product ramp: stainless steel double ferrule revenue is only INR8-10 crores so far, and defence, railway and oil and gas wins are still pending.
Management did not give specifics on the acquisition question and deferred it to the next quarter.
544891|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and H2 growth, but evasive on specifics: several questions were deflected or answered loosely, and the FY27/FY28 growth guidance was revised during the call. Management was cautious on US tariffs and new verticals, describing new-sector revenue as slow to build.
key_quotes: So 24% EBITDA down the line for the second half is guaranteed.
We are completely booked.
Hy-Tech is growing not for the new market but for the existing market.

Our integrated manufacturing capabilities, wide product portfolio of nearly 11,000 SKUs, and ability to deliver high-quality precision components have helped us establish ourselves as a trusted supplier to leading OEMs.

rows.label: John Deere ramp and US subsidiary
rows.why: About three John Deere plants are supplying and four have approved samples, with John Deere at about 12% of turnover; the ramp is expected in FY28 alongside a New Jersey warehouse.

rows.why: Management says the company is completely booked with schedules from all OEMs, while tractor demand softens and excavator demand rises.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 margin (about 24%) and full order books, but cautious on US tariffs and new verticals; analysts pressed on the revised FY27 and FY28 PAT guidance, the Q1 price-shortfall recovery and capacity beyond INR500 crore, and management answered loosely on several points.

544894|2026-09.headline: Lumino Q2 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR661 crores, with EBITDA margin at 12.8% and order book at INR2,885 crores.
544894|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR661 crores, up 30% YoY from INR509 crores, with EBITDA of INR84 crores (12.8% margin) and PAT of INR53 crores (7.9% margin). H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,183 crores (+25% YoY), EBITDA INR155 crores (13.1%), and operating cash flow INR56 crores after paying INR68 crores of trade acceptances from IPO proceeds. Order book stood at INR2,885 crores on 30 September, rising to INR3,093 crores by October, with a further INR555 crores of L1 tenders. Management guided to a 12-13.5% manufacturing EBITDA margin and 13-14% EPC margin, and said debt repayment from IPO proceeds should cut finance cost by INR20-25 crores annually.

544897|2026-09.headline: Paluck Technologies guides FY27 revenue of INR130-140 crores and PAT of INR17-18 crores, about 25% growth, with H1 PAT of about INR5 crores.

544898|2026-09.headline: ESDS H1 FY27 revenue rose 24.6% YoY to INR 2,719 million; Q2 revenue INR 1,383.4 million, up 3.5% QoQ, with AI factory (Sharon AI) go-live pending.
544898|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 1,383.4 million, up 3.5% QoQ from INR 1,336.6 million in Q1. Management said the main growth driver is the 8,200-GPU AI factory contracted with Sharon AI and sold to ESDS's customers, now in final testing with NVIDIA, with RFS targeted between early and 17 December. Management also flagged the CIO/CTO exits, a shrinking customer count, and that the 8,200 GPUs are priced at contracted rates and cannot be repriced upward.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a delay, and is there any funding issue at Sharon AI? What SLAs apply?

qa_highlights.question: Why did the CIO and CTO roles change?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sharon AI contract structure: five or seven years?
qa_highlights.answer: The ESDS commitment to Sharon AI is for 5 years, with pricing locked for 7 years. Renewal after 5 years would be at the lower locked rate; ESDS's customer pricing is flexible after 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the INR 670 crore non-current and INR 1,900 crore current liabilities on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said these reflect a USD 140 million advance paid to Sharon AI and a matching customer advance, both amortised on a mirrored schedule, so the liability and asset line up.

544901|2026-06.headline: Purple Style Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR119 crores (from INR106 crores), but EBITDA was negative INR11 crores vs negative INR4 crores a year earlier.
544901|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with the four large-format experience centres opened in FY26 (Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York). GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores and AOV rose to INR86,000 from INR66,000. Revenue from operations was INR119 crores, gross margin held at 36%, and EBITDA and PAT losses were wider than a year earlier on the higher fixed cost base of the new stores. Inventory and net working capital fell year on year, but borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end.

segments.name: Mumbai (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR50 crores from INR28 crores in the first three months of FY26. Mumbai was the largest market in FY26 GMV at INR205 crores.

segments.name: Delhi (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR39 crores from INR29 crores. Delhi FY26 GMV was INR166 crores.

segments.name: Hyderabad (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR16 crores from INR10 crores.

segments.name: USA (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR29 crores from INR20 crores. New York flagship opened in March 2026 and is the first US store; US was online-only before that.

guidance_outlook: No objective margin or profitability guidance given; management said it would refrain from it.
Q1 is the leanest quarter; management said the cost structure set in Q1 will carry into Q2 absent changes, and clearer trends are expected over the next two quarters.
No significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of the FY26 store investments is to be observed.

EBITDA break-even framing: on a P&L basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed for zero EBITDA, with lease-related costs of INR45 crores (lease interest plus ROU depreciation) included. On a cash basis, lease payments of INR29 crores imply a smaller gap.
Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.
capex_capacity: Four large-format experience centres opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi (operational since Q2 FY26), Linking Road Bandra (end-March 2026), and Madison Avenue New York (March 2026).
Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.
demand_pricing: AOV rose to INR86,000 in Q1 FY27, from INR76,000 in FY26 and INR46,000 in FY24. Store AOV is about 2.5x online AOV (India online about INR38,000 vs store about INR90,000 in FY26).
Active designer brands fell to 1,109 in FY26 from 1,910 in FY24. Top 100 designers were 67% of sales in FY24.
Average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24. Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of FY26 GMV of INR722 crores.
Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew to INR312 crores GMV in FY26 from INR187 crores in FY24. Women's wear below INR35,000 fell to INR86 crores from INR162 crores.
Gross margin percentage is said to be broadly flat across price points. Management argued that absolute gross profit per piece rises with higher ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow still negative and borrowings rising despite lower inventory and working capital? When does the business become self-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower inventory reflects better inventory management after the FY22-25 build-up, and higher customer advances (INR49 crores) helped working capital. Debt is funding interest costs, and Q1 is not operationally profitable. It asked investors to observe the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the higher-ticket strategy improve gross margin or only AOV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage gross margin is similar across categories. The benefit is in absolute gross profit per piece (e.g., at 40% margin a INR2 lakh piece yields INR80,000 vs INR8,000 for a INR20,000 piece), plus lower supply and customer complexity from the long tail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of outright purchase, consignment and backorder inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

544903|2026-09.headline: Deepa Jewellers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.24% on plain-gold mix and PAT rose 37% to INR 37 crore.
544903|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, with EBITDA of INR 45 crore (up 17% YoY, margin 7.24%) and PAT of INR 37 crore (up 37%, margin 5.96%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,057 crore, EBITDA rose 24% to INR 84 crore (7.95% margin) and PAT rose 32% to INR 64 crore. Management attributed the Q2 growth moderation to festive demand shifting into H2, and said lower gross margin came from a plain-gold-heavy sales mix, with PAT supported by other income and a lower tax rate. The company also commenced its in-house Hyderabad manufacturing facility in September 2026 and guided to 40-45% revenue CAGR for FY27-FY29.

segments.commentary: Volume of 491 kg in Q2 (broadly stable) and 783 kg in H1 (-5% YoY). Own-processing realisation fell to about INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g, attributed to lower gold prices, plain-gold mix and higher 18-karat sales.

segments.name: Studded vs plain gold mix
segments.commentary: Studded share was 57% of H1 FY27 sales, against 65% in FY26, with plain gold at 43%. Management targets studded share of 75% over the next three to four quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 40-45% guided for FY27, FY28 and FY29, with FY27 growth of 40-45% compared with FY26 (March 2026) base; the 40-45% figure was also described as a 40-50% revenue CAGR for two years at a constant 24-karat gold rate of INR 50,000.
EBITDA margin expected to expand 80-120 bps over the next 4-6 quarters, driven by the Hyderabad facility, Tier-2/3 expansion, studded mix and standalone store sales.
Gross margin pressure from plain-gold mix expected to normalise in upcoming quarters.
Hedging to rise from 94% toward close to 100% of gold holdings over the next two to three quarters.
Working capital cycle (inventory days plus receivable days) expected in the 55-65 day range; inventory and receivables expected to normalise from Q3.
Internal accruals, IPO proceeds and existing debt expected to fund growth through FY29.
Effective tax rate guided at the standard 25.168%; Q2 benefit came from deferred tax on IPO expenses, with the tax shield reversing in later years.
capex_capacity: In-house manufacturing facility in Hyderabad, about 6,700 sq ft, commenced operations in September 2026.
Facility capacity of about 1.5 tonnes a year on single shift and about 2.5 tonnes a year on double shift.
Facility processed 65 kg (13% of volume) in Q1 FY27 and 167 kg (21%) in Q2 FY27; management expects about 40% in Q3 and about 50% in Q4.
Second sales office in Chennai planned for December 2026; Bangalore office planned for April-May 2027, following Vijayawada office.
Long-run target mix of 65% in-house and 35% outsourced manufacturing; outsourced work to shift in-house from Q4 FY27.

Q2 growth moderated as festive demand shifted into H2; H1 typically contributes about 40% of annual revenue.
Retail customers shifting from cash purchases to old-gold exchange after a gold price spike, moving sales from invoice basis to job work; management said total volume shifted rather than fell.

Job work conversion margin is about 75% and invoice-basis about 8%, with a similar ROCE/ROE in both models; job work is priced at about 1% lower wastage (4% vs 5%) because it needs no working capital.
Gold price assumption for guidance: constant 24-karat rate of INR 50,000 per 10 g; average selling gold price rose from about INR 8,000/g in FY25 to INR 11,950/g in FY26.

Job work realisation fell to about INR 178 from INR 202 a year earlier (about 11%), attributed to the same SKU mix.

Management expects normalisation from Q3 and a combined inventory plus receivable cycle of 55-65 days.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 40-45% CAGR, the Hyderabad ramp and margin recovery, and described Q2 softness as mix and timing; analysts pressed on the margin direction, the basis for the CAGR, the low tax rate, and the inventory build.

544911|2026-06.headline: Kanohar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 103.5% YoY to INR137.1 crore, with EBITDA margin of 28.3% and order book of about INR2,026 crore.
544911|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR137.1 crore, up 103.5% YoY, with transformers at 84.9% and EPC at 14.81% of revenue. EBITDA rose 152.2% to INR38.8 crore (28.3% margin, up 550 bps) and PAT rose 140% to INR27.3 crore (19.9% margin). Consolidated order book stood at about INR2,026 crore on June 30, 2026, up 11% from March 31, 2026, after incremental orders of INR332.2 crore in Q1 and INR867.3 crore in Q2 to date. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR950 crore with EBITDA margin similar to FY26, with H2 as the main execution period.

financial_highlights.value: Q1: INR332.2 crore; Q2 to date: INR867.3 crore

segments.name: Power Transformers / 400 kV
segments.commentary: 400 kV transformers contributed 70.16% of Q1 revenue (52% in FY26, 10.3% in FY24). Management said 400 kV, Scott-connected and shunt reactor products carry similar gross margins; about 70% of order book is power transformers, mostly 400 kV.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: EPC contributed 14.81% of Q1 revenue. Management does not disclose EBITDA separately; directionally lower than transformer margins.

segments.name: By end-user
segments.commentary: Power Transmission 85.18%, Railways 11.53%, Renewable Energy 2.84%, Power Distribution 0.23% of Q1 revenue. Shunt reactors were about 13.1% of order book at June 30.

segments.name: Voltage mix (other)
segments.commentary: 132 kV to below 220 kV at 11.38%, 220 kV to below 400 kV at 3.19%, below 132 kV at 0.23% of Q1 revenue.

Brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol, targeted to be in place by end-FY28 / FY29; existing capacity seen sufficient through FY28.
Net working capital guided at 110-120 days.
Order book at end-FY27 may be adequate to cover FY28 and FY29 revenue, per management; no specific FY27 closing order book number given.
Shunt reactors expected to be about 10-15% of revenue on average over time.

demand_pricing: Management estimates India 400 kV transformer market at about 60,000-70,000 MVA last year, growing 10-15% industry-wide; analyst's INR4,000-6,000 crore 400 kV market size was confirmed as 'in that range'.
Railways envisages about 1,000 traction substations for high-speed rail over 5-10 years (about 2,000 transformers), implying about INR20,000 crore opportunity.
Most contracts have price variation clauses (IEEMA PVC), which management says offsets raw material swings; order book margins said to be similar to FY26.
Industry lead times are 18-24 months; tenders being bid are mainly for FY29-FY30 execution.
Revenue per MVA about INR6.1 lakh last year; may have risen slightly due to raw material costs.
Management said there were no new entrants in the last 3-6 months that it is aware of, but expects new entrants over time.

qa_highlights.question: How were transformer margins protected in Q1 given input cost increases and fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts carry price variation linked to the IEEMA clause, which passes through raw material moves in both directions.

qa_highlights.question: Will GEC-III drive a multi-year order tailwind for 400 kV and 500 MVA transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a multi-decadal structural tailwind; intra-state transmission is mostly 400 kV, but no split of GEC-III capacity by voltage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can order book reach INR3,000 crore by FY27 end, and 40-45% YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to confirm; said Q2 execution will reduce the order book slightly, and end-FY27 book may cover FY28-FY29 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1H-weak, 2H-heavy revenue pattern a continuing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said H1 is typically softer and H2 heavier, an industry trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will new 400 kV capacity pressure margins beyond 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visibility for 3-4 years from current order book and tenders; beyond that, short-term supply-demand mismatch and margin pressure are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY24 a revenue decline and why is utilisation low; are exports planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY24 focus went to obtaining 400 kV and Scott certifications; ramp-up takes time. Exports are not the current focus; a re-look may come in 3-4 years.

Order book lumpiness toward power transformers, with large CPSU orders (INR250 crore+) in Q2.

544911|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and qualifications, with a clear long-term structural narrative. Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to confirm order book targets, FY28 growth, bid pipeline, and solar savings, and deferred several answers to later follow-up.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, qualifications and the long-term GEC-III and railway narrative, but cautious and evasive on order book targets, FY28 growth, bid pipeline and solar savings; analysts pushed on the 3,000 crore order book goal, 40-45% growth and margin pressure from new entrants.

544911|2026-09.headline: Kanohar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 112% YoY to INR208.6 crore with 35% EBITDA margin; FY27 revenue guidance of about INR950 crore reiterated.
544911|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 112% YoY to INR208.6 crore, with EBITDA of INR73.1 crore (35% margin) and PAT of INR53.9 crore (25.8% margin). H1 FY27 revenue rose 109% to INR345.7 crore at a 32.3% EBITDA margin. Order book stood at INR2,711.2 crore at 30 September 2026, up 34% QoQ, with Q2 inflows of INR867.3 crore. Management kept full-year EBITDA margin guidance at roughly FY26 levels (about 28%) and reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of about INR950 crore, while declining to quantify FY28 growth beyond "similar" YoY growth.

financial_highlights.change: built up ahead of H2 execution

segments.commentary: About 56% of H1 FY27 revenue, up 88% YoY; about 78% of order book. 400 kV is the largest product segment.

segments.name: Shunt reactors
segments.commentary: About 22% of H1 FY27 revenue versus negligible last year; about one-third of Q2 revenue; about 10% of order book. Mostly 245 kV with some 420 kV.

segments.name: Scott-connected transformers (railways)
segments.commentary: About 9% of H1 FY27 revenue (8.8% per Q&A); 220 kV and 132 kV only.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: 10.5% of Q2 revenue; EPC order book executable over the next 12 to 24 months.

segments.commentary: 400 kV 46.6%, 220 kV 34%, 132 kV 7%, below 132 kV 1.9%. Products rated 220 kV and above were about 78% of H1 revenue versus about 53% in H1 FY26.

segments.commentary: Power transmission 57.1%, renewable energy 34%, railways 7%, power distribution 1.9%.

In-house manufacturing of tanks, radiators, control panels and insulation components; management said these cover most requirements.

Shunt reactor market roughly 30,000 MVAR; typical ratings 50, 63, 80 and 125 MVAR.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin (35%) well above the FY26 guidance and is the 400 kV vs 220 kV margin gap large?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premium 400 kV power transformers, shunt reactors and Scott transformers have broadly similar margin profiles; the order book carries a similar margin profile. A quantified 400 kV vs 220 kV margin gap was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 margin guidance (about 28%) below the H1 run rate of 32%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited quarter-to-quarter and order-to-order margin variation and full-year operating expenses; it said there was no one-off in H1 and no direct reason for guiding lower.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR950 crore revenue guidance conservative given H1 of INR345.7 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 is typically softer; FY26 H1 was about INR175 crore against a full year of INR650 crore, so the same split is not expected. INR950 crore guidance stands. A post-Q3 upgrade was left open.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capacity utilisation low and why expand capacity now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10.5% figure divided annualised capacity by one quarter's output; on an annualised basis Q2 utilisation was about 41%. It said ramp-up is gradual to protect quality, so new capacity is needed in FY29 and lead time is required.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter 765 kV and what are the steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Technology and plants are ready; the company is seeking first orders and a track record. It expects 3 to 4 years before eligibility for regular tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Does shunt reactor volume in Q2 count in MVA sold?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; MVA and MVAR are combined into one MVA figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: In-house tanks, radiators, control panels and insulation components; no plans for new components beyond these. In-house supply covers most needs.

544912|2026-06.headline: Prasol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.7% YoY to INR433.6 crores and EBITDA to INR90.3 crores, helped by one-off inventory gains of about INR25 crores.
544912|2026-06.overview: First earnings call after the 16 September 2026 listing. Revenue from operations was INR433.6 crores (up 35.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 20.8% and PAT of INR61 crores (14.1% margin). Management attributed about INR25 crores of gross profit to a sharp rise in selling prices from West Asia-linked supply disruptions and inventory bought at lower prices, which it called partly non-structural. FY27 guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores revenue and INR240-250 crores adjusted EBITDA excludes these gains, and management described a 15-16% year-end EBITDA margin. A Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores for existing products (about 60,000 tpa of added capacity) was outlined.

segments.name: Acetone-based specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: About 40% of Q1 FY27 revenue; about 43% of FY26 revenue per management.

segments.name: Phosphorus-based specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: About 40% of Q1 FY27 revenue; described as the fastest-growing category, about 38% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Other specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Balance about 20% of Q1 revenue; customised products built around specific customer needs.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 27% of Q1 FY27 revenue, stated as stable or growing despite West Asia disruption to Dubai and Africa shipments.

segments.name: Mahad plant
segments.commentary: About 19,900 tpa capacity; utilisation rose from about 13% in FY24 to 44% in FY26, and management says it was EBITDA and PBT positive in Q1 (about 60% utilisation cited).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores and adjusted EBITDA of INR240-250 crores, excluding price fluctuation from geopolitical supply issues and forex gains/losses.
Year-end FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 15-16%.
Normalised gross margin expected at about 30-32%, supported by mix, debottlenecking and captive intermediate consumption.
Management expects pricing to normalise from Q1 elevated levels, with margins moving toward a more sustainable range.
Five-year aspiration of INR2,800-3,000 crores revenue.

Phase 1 adds about 60,000 tpa; 10-14 projects to come over the next 12-18 months, with the antibacterial product due in about 6 months and lubricant volume expansion before March.
Phase 2 of INR250-300 crores for new R&D products with better margins; site, product and regulatory work still in progress.
INR25 crores floating-roof acetone storage tank planned, plus more than INR25 crores in the next year for adjoining Khopoli land.
Application testing lab and additional 4,000 sq ft R&D space being built, with investments of about INR15-20 crores for application lab.
demand_pricing: Management says volume grew in the mid-single-digit range in Q1, with demand strong across sectors.
Q1 realisations were lifted by a sharp rise in acetone and petrochemical prices after the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption; the company says it does not speculate on raw materials.
Largest customer is about INR55-60 crores of revenue, against the FY27 revenue target; top 10% of customers are about 24-25% of turnover; more than 1,600 customers.
Management says export volumes to Europe were rising to offset weaker shipments to Africa and the Middle East, and that the West Asia war cost up to about 10% of potential export growth.
Antibacterial product: new technology cuts steps from 10 to 3-3.5; management expects more than 100 tons a month once samples are approved (NDA signed with MNC).
REACH registration for six or seven products; mining chemicals approved in US, with commercial volumes expected in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Phase 1 capacity additions (about 60,000 tpa) mainly extensions of existing products, and is the approach application-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said it builds new streams once existing capacity reaches 75-85% utilisation and customer visibility is 3-4 years; it has 10 streams for one client and five hydrogenation reactors.

qa_highlights.question: Will the acetone sourcing diversification need storage or logistics investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR25 crores is set aside for a floating-roof storage tank and more than INR25 crores will go into adjoining Khopoli land over the next year, with barge-based shipping expected to cut transport costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EBITDA guidance (INR240-250 crores) only modestly above the Q1 run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance excludes about INR25 crores of inventory and forex gains, and it is deliberately conservative given geopolitical uncertainty; it expects Q2 to be near complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Mahad outlook and how much EBITDA did it contribute in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahad is PBT and EBITDA positive; the exact EBITDA number was not given and will be revert-back. Utilisation is about 60%-plus, targeted at 70%-plus by year-end; the extra 20 acres will share overheads.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory higher at quarter-end and how is it managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stock is built from January-February for the April season, with raw materials bought at pre-war prices, and that it does not speculate on raw material prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for additional capex for the R&D pipeline, and on what land?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15-20% of about 40 pipeline products typically get commercialised; the newer chemistry will use the land already bought, and environmental clearance for one or two products is in an advanced stage (9-12 months typical).

rows.why: Antibacterial product with NDA signed with MNC targets more than 100 tons a month once samples are approved, and REACH registration covers six or seven products, though commercial timing depends on sample approval.

rows.label: Export diversification to Europe and US mining chemicals
rows.when: next 2-3 years for US mining volumes
rows.why: Exports are 27% of Q1 revenue and stable, with Europe volumes rising to offset Africa/Middle East weakness; mining chemicals approved in US with commercial volumes expected in 2-3 years.

544912|2026-09.headline: Prasol Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR413 crore (+38.6% YoY) and EBITDA INR58 crore (+86.1%), with FY27 guidance reiterated.
544912|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR413 crore, up 38.6% YoY, driven mainly by higher realisations with single-digit domestic volume growth. EBITDA rose 86.1% to INR58 crore and PAT rose 122.2% to INR38 crore. H1 FY27 EBITDA of INR148 crore included a one-time INR25 crore inventory gain and INR0.92 crore forex gain in Q1, and management said underlying full-year EBITDA should be INR240-250 crore. Working capital cycle lengthened from 63 to 76 days as the company added shorter-credit suppliers, and H1 operating cash flow was negative.

financial_highlights.change: +106% YoY; includes INR25 crore inventory gain and INR0.92 crore forex gain in Q1
up from 63 days at end Q1 FY27

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Q2 growth was driven by higher realisations, with single-digit volume growth in the domestic business.

segments.name: Agrochemicals
segments.commentary: Agro is about 15-16% of top line per analyst; October agro sales grew 150%. One molecule (7-8% of agro products) has only two Indian manufacturers. Management said no further agro investment is planned.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were about 25% of revenue, held back by freight (sea freight up 2.5-3x to US and 7-8x on some routes). Target is 30%+ of revenue. Gross contribution is 30-35%, with manufacturing around 35% and distribution around 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at INR1,550-1,650 crore; EBITDA INR240-250 crore, excluding geopolitical price gains and forex, implying about 70-75% EBITDA growth YoY.
Management said profit before tax for H1 has already exceeded last year's full-year PAT base; H1 EBITDA and PAT already exceed last year's H1 figures.
Working capital cycle expected to return to the normal 60-70 day range; management expects inventory to normalise by end Q3 FY27.
Long-term scale target of INR2,800-3,000 crore revenue in about 5 years. Management declined to share a 5-year EBITDA margin target.
FY28 guidance not given; management said it is too early to discuss.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 capex INR250-300 crore: about INR75 crore spent so far (H1 FY27 spend about INR75 crore); INR75-100 crore more planned before year-end.
Phase 1 adds about 60,000 tonnes, taking installed capacity to 150,000-160,000 tonnes over 12-24 months; about 25% of projects to go live by June-July 2027 and another 25% in H2 FY28.
Mechanical completion targeted by March 2027; about 3 months from mechanical completion to commercial production after sample approval.
Phase 2 capex INR250-300 crore for R&D-led products (mining chemicals, lubricants, pharma); propylene-based project needs about 2.5 years (CCOE and land approvals), the other about 1.5-2 years.
Additional domestic acetone capacity expected from January 2027; planned Khopoli storage facility for bulk procurement.
Antibacterial drug new process needs 3-6 months of requalification; lubricant additive capacity is a volume ramp-up, with the company sold out on current output.
demand_pricing: Management said demand from domestic and international customers remains healthy, the order book is strong, and the last month had the highest sales ever.
Raw material prices remain elevated; the company has added suppliers and customers across geographies. Shipping times for some inputs rose from 1-1.5 months to about 4 months.
Pricing pass-through: price increases pass to customers after 10-15 days; price cuts are passed on with a 15-30 day lag. Top 10 customers are on a formula-based supply arrangement.

Mining chemicals: a US lab approval was received; the company is now in mine-wise trials (South Africa and others), moving to bidding once mine approvals come. Management expects a breakthrough within about 2.5 years, possibly sooner.
Phosphorus-based products have about 2-2.5 months of visibility and are fully sold out.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY28 look for sales and EBITDA, and what new products and applications will come in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY28 numbers, citing the geopolitical situation. Expansions are in existing products already approved by end customers. Lubricant additives are in volume ramp-up and fully sold; antibacterial drug re-approval takes 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of inventory loss if crude corrects, and how is it mitigated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a formula-based pricing arrangement with its top 10 customers and books inventory only against order visibility. Price cuts are passed on with a 15-30 day lag, so the company is exposed when prices fall and benefits when they rise.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 operating cash flow negative, and what is the full-year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H1 cash flow is a snapshot and the working capital build reflects new suppliers, higher inventory cost and longer shipping times. Management expects inventory to normalise by end Q3 and expects to rebuild inventory in Q4 if demand holds.

qa_highlights.question: What are plant utilisation levels and which industries are targeted by expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined utilisation of both plants is about 65-75%. Expansions cover every non-agro product, with increases of 30-100%. Forward integration and identical plants for lubricant grades are planned.

qa_highlights.question: What share of Q2 growth came from volume?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth came from higher realisations, with single-digit volume growth in the domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of renewable power at Mahad?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is laying an own cable from the grid (INR2.5-3 crore, due in 1.5-2 months). Current Mahad power costs INR9-9.5 per unit, with expected savings of INR1.25-1.50 per unit subject to solar regulations.

risks_watch: Working capital cycle at 76 days versus the 60-70 day target; H1 operating cash flow was negative.
Inventory valuation risk if crude and derivative prices fall; the pass-through lag is 15-30 days.
Phase 1 commissioning in stages (June-July 2027 and H2 FY28); execution and cost overrun risk on capex.
Export share at about 25% versus 30%+ target, dependent on freight normalisation.
Dependence on a few manufacturers in key molecules; the H1 earnings base includes a one-time INR25 crore gain.
Long-term INR2,800-3,000 crore revenue target relies on Phase 2 and R&D products that take 1.5-2.5 years to build.
544912|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q2 results and reiterated FY27 guidance, with several claims of record performance. Cautious and deliberately vague on FY28 and the 5-year EBITDA margin, citing geopolitical uncertainty. Management repeatedly stressed that the Q1 INR25 crore inventory gain is excluded from underlying EBITDA.
key_quotes: I am very happy to announce that this has been one of our best Q2 of Prasol ever.
We are extremely well placed and we have seen every time in crisis, when crisis comes, we end up doing better generally.
So we are light on agro. Whatever we have invested is what we are going to reap. We are not investing any further into that.
We are not here to make a short-term gain on you.

tone.note: Management was confident on record Q2 results, reiterated FY27 guidance and the order book, and was cautious and vague on FY28 and the 5-year margin; analysts pressed on inventory risk if crude falls, negative H1 operating cash flow, and the sustainability of the one-time Q1 gain.

544913|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to Rs.107 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to Rs.23 crore, with margin at 21.3% and a Rs.982 crore order book.
544913|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs.107 crore, up 36% YoY, led by domestic facade (Rs.62 crore, +93%) and fenestration (Rs.6 crore, +127%), while international fell 12% to Rs.39 crore on delivery timing. EBITDA grew 9% to Rs.23 crore, and margin fell to 21.3% because of lower international contribution and a shift to DDP freight billing at cost. Management attributed about 1.5 points of the margin gap to freight pass-through and said the underlying margin is in line with FY26. PAT of Rs.17 crore grew more slowly than EBITDA due to lower other income (prior-year property sale gain) and higher depreciation from new capacity. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth, 23-25% EBITDA margin and 18-20% PAT margin, while flagging a weak first half and a heavier Q3 and Q4.

financial_highlights.change: Lower YoY; international margin cited at 36.3%
Grew slower than EBITDA; lower other income and higher depreciation

financial_highlights.metric: Freight cost included in revenue and cost
financial_highlights.change: Pass-through; adds about 1.5 pts to margin if excluded

segments.name: Domestic facade (turnkey, Grade A developers)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.62 crore, up 93% YoY; all order book is commercial real estate in Tier 1 cities. Historically about 49% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: International facade (B2B product supply, US and Australia)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.39 crore, down 12% YoY on delivery timing; management expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger with three projects. Historically about 45% of FY26 revenue; FY26 Australia revenue was Rs.24 crore.

segments.name: Fenestration (luxury doors and windows)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.6 crore, up 127% YoY on luxury residential demand. Historically about 6% of FY26 revenue. Higher margin, lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 25% YoY (management also cited a 20-25% CAGR ambition).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 23-25% and PAT margin of 18-20% on a consolidated basis, with freight pass-through expected to have limited impact.
Revenue mix for FY27 to stay similar to FY26 (about 49% domestic, 45% international, 6% fenestration).
Glass processing unit commissioning expected in about 8 months, with an estimated 1-1.5% EBITDA margin benefit.
Target of at least 2 years of order book visibility.
capex_capacity: Vile Bhagad (Mangaon) plant on a 1 lakh sq m owned MIDC plot; about 32,000 sq m built to date and about 30% of land used.
Current capacity about 130 panels a day across four production lines, with about 350 workers (about 120 on payroll).
Glass processing unit under construction; total project cost Rs.80 crore, funded by Rs.50 crore fresh issue and internal accruals; commissioning in about 8 months.
Management says infrastructure supports growth for the next couple of years without incremental capex.
In-house NABL-accredited test facility for air, water, seismic, structural and movement testing.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs.982 crore as on 31 July 2026, with no substantial new orders in the past three months; a few near-closure international jobs in the US, Canada and Israel.
Domestic facade market about Rs.9,000 crore, projected to reach about Rs.14,500 crore by FY30 (about 15.9% CAGR, per management).
Management estimates a 6-7% domestic market share, and says it is the second-largest domestic player by revenue.
Contracts include aluminium and glass pass-through across all verticals; freight now billed at cost under DDP terms.
Payment terms are milestone-based (about 10% advance, about 55-60% on material delivery, balance on installation); export invoicing is at dispatch with 60-day credit.
Management said US tariffs could slow US construction demand, but it views the impact on its business as small.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q1 order inflow, and will the freight change and any Q1 delays affect Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no substantial new order came in over the past three months. Freight of about Rs.5.5 crore is a pass-through, and adjusting for it plus the prior-year property gain, margin is in line with FY26. Export is back-ended, with three projects due in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin risen above pre-COVID levels on lower revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the export and fenestration verticals, a shift from residential to commercial projects with faster realisations, pass-through clauses on aluminium and glass, and consolidation from three factories to one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the glass processing unit timeline and benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is expected in about 8 months, with an estimated 1-1.5% bottom-line margin benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order-book and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to keep at least 2 years of visibility and grow revenue at 20-25% CAGR; a typical order cycle is 18-24 months (export about 12 months, domestic about 24).

qa_highlights.question: What are the market share and competitive position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates about 6-7% domestic share and says it is second-largest by revenue; its direct competitors are three or four players with revenue around Rs.200 crore.

risks_watch: Seasonality: management said the first two quarters are typically slow, so FY27 delivery depends on the heavier Q3 and Q4.
Order inflow: no substantial new orders in the three months to July, and the company is relying on near-closure international wins.
Freight and duty pass-through: under DDP terms the company bears freight and any tariff changes, and mitigation depends on clients accepting pass-through; management said margin % may dilute.
US demand: management said tariffs could slow US construction demand.
Glass processing unit commissioning in about 8 months; the margin benefit is estimated at 1-1.5%.
544913|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margin and FY27 guidance, which management reiterated despite the quarter's margin dip. Somewhat evasive on order inflow, export margin split and forward mix, and it repeatedly asked investors to judge on a yearly basis rather than quarterly.

544913|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 16% to Rs.239 crores and EBITDA rose 22% to Rs.60 crores at a 25.3% margin; FY27 guidance held.
544913|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.239 crores, up 16% YoY, with domestic up 33%, international down 14% on order-execution timing, and fenestration up 82%. EBITDA was Rs.60 crores (25.3% margin, up 138 bps), or 26.9% after stripping out Rs.14 crores of pass-through freight income and expense. Order book stood at Rs.957 crores at September 30, 2026, with management targeting Rs.500 crores-plus of new bookings in Q3-Q4 to hold about 18 months of visibility. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 20-22% and EBITDA margin of 23-25%, and said Q3-Q4 will be stronger.

financial_highlights.change: stated as in the same region as last year
added to both revenue and expenses

segments.name: Domestic (commercial, hospitality, residential, pan-India for Grade A developers)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.140 crores, up 33% YoY. Management says Tier 1 demand is strong and the domestic bid pipeline exceeds Rs.3,000 crores. One or two projects are running behind on the client side, which management does not consider material.

segments.name: International (US, Australia and others)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.76 crores, down 14% YoY on execution timing. Management says existing US jobs are funded and dispatching daily. New US awards are being held back by developers over tariffs, shipping costs and commodity prices, with a couple of awards expected in Q3-Q4. Israel is a new market, with a first job expected below Rs.50 crores.

segments.name: Fenestration / luxury residential
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.22 crores, up 82% YoY, which management said reflects project execution rather than a run-rate. Management expects substantial bookings in Q3-Q4 and says the segment carries higher margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-22%, unchanged from the previous call.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23-25% and PAT margin at 18-20%, both unchanged.
Q3-Q4 expected to be much stronger; an analyst extrapolation of over 30% H2 top-line growth was described as ballpark accurate by management.
Target of Rs.500 crores-plus of new order bookings in Q3-Q4 to end FY27 with about 18 months of visibility.
Glass processing unit commissioning expected July-August 2027, with an estimated 1-1.5% EBITDA margin benefit from Q3-Q4 FY28.
Working capital days guided at around 45 days, with anything below that described as a bonus.
capex_capacity: Glass processing unit project cost is about Rs.70-odd crores, funded from IPO proceeds held separately. Civil construction is expected to finish in 2-3 months, machinery arrival in 6-7 months, and commissioning in 2-3 months.
Other capex is expected to be no more than Rs.20 crores over the next 1.5-2 years, funded from internal accruals.

Current capacity utilisation is about 55-60%. Management says peak revenue of Rs.1,000-plus crores is achievable from the existing facility without material capex, and that this covers about 4 years of 22% growth.
The company has bought a couple of machines and is evaluating additional machinery for BIPV glass production, which is at R&D stage.
demand_pricing: Order book of Rs.957 crores at September 30, 2026, against Rs.846 crores at April 2026 and Rs.383 crores at the start of FY26. Management expects to execute about Rs.350 crores over the next two quarters and says the book will run for 18-24 months.

Average order size is now Rs.60-70 crores, with Rs.80-100 crores jobs described as normal. Bids include a Rs.400 crore Mumbai job, a Rs.450 crore Delhi fenestration quote, and a Rs.225 crore Raidurg bid.
Management says it is choosing jobs on client, terms, margin and execution period rather than chasing win ratio, and that it could win all Rs.3,000 crores of pipeline by cutting prices about 5%.

Q2 wins included a Mumbai hotel job of about Rs.90 crores and two South India data-centre jobs of about Rs.35-40 crores. Management expects data centres to be a few jobs only, with hospitality and commercial as stronger segments.

Pass-through clauses cover aluminium and glass. Claims are certified in 45-60 days, and management says this makes the company risk-free from commodity moves on current projects. Management says none of the jobs are cost-plus; all are re-measurable item-rate contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Are US customers cancelling existing orders, or is the Q3-Q4 strength tied to new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing orders are funded and dispatching daily, so none are being stopped. The slowdown relates to new US jobs, which developers are holding until prices normalise. Management expects a pent-up wave of awards after the US midterms or an end to the war.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp Q2 margin increase on flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to Rs.6 crores of escalation claims booked in Q2 for costs incurred in Q1, and to a richer mix from fenestration. It reiterated FY27 guidance of 23-25% EBITDA and 18-20% PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.500 crores order target for Q3-Q4 alone, and what is the split across segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is for Q3-Q4 only and said bookings will come from all three segments, without giving a split.

qa_highlights.question: How do aluminium and glass price changes flow through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through claims are raised after the client-side base rate is reconciled, and are paid 45-60 days after cost is incurred. It said the company carries no commodity risk on current projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-22% growth guidance net of freight, and what is the freight mechanism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is net of freight, which is a pass-through. The CFO said the company receives an advance against freight, so there is no new working-capital blockage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Israel and US new-client wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a first Israel order in Q3-Q4 FY27, initially below Rs.50 crores, with larger jobs possible within 1.5-2 years. It said the US bids cover both existing and new clients, with a couple of awards possible in the next quarter.

risks_watch: International revenue fell 14% in H1, and Q3-Q4 depends on US and Israel awards that management has not yet booked.
Q2 margin spike was partly due to escalation-claim timing; management itself said margins could move up and down.
H2 revenue depends on converting about Rs.500 crores of bookings in two quarters; no split was given.
Glass processing unit timeline is July-August 2027, and the margin benefit is estimated at 1-1.5%.
Some domestic projects are behind schedule on the client side.
Working capital is currently negative at -19 days, against a stated normalised level of about 45 days.
