544914|2026-06.headline: Steamhouse Q1 FY27 PAT rose 80.25% YoY to INR18.34 crore on 16.7% steam volume growth; EBITDA margin 24.05%.
544914|2026-06.overview: Steamhouse reported record quarterly steam volumes of about 3,05,816 tons, up 16.7% YoY and 11.52% QoQ, with revenue from operations up 13.35% to INR128.62 crore. EBITDA rose 60.08% to INR30.93 crore, lifting margin to 24.05% (up 702 bps), while PAT rose 80.25% to INR18.34 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher volumes, utilisation (41.40% vs 36.06% YoY) and operating leverage, and noted the exit from low-margin coal trading. Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore at FY26 end, with IPO proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and capacity expansion.

segments.name: Steam generation and distribution (own boilers)
segments.commentary: Own-generated steam was 73.7% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said it will be the source of future growth, with waste-to-energy boilers at Vapi supporting realisation.

segments.name: Steam trading (purchased and resold)
segments.commentary: Traded steam was 22.2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Coal trading has been discontinued as low-margin; two trading agreements (Dahej SEZ, Haldia) are signed and management declined to split margins between generation and trading.

segments.name: Industrial gases / nitrogen
segments.commentary: PSA-based nitrogen plant of 350 Nm3/hr commissioned at Ankleshwar. Management described it as currently small and plans air separation units for LIN/LOX and other gases.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to take utilisation to 60%-65%; newer boilers expected at about 50% in initial months after commissioning.
Steam volume growth of 5%-10% expected at existing locations; company-level 20%-25% volume growth described as 'very comfortably' achievable with new capacity and demand revival.

EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 expected to be maintained for next few quarters; Q2 seasonally weaker due to monsoon; full-year performance expected to be at par with or better than Q1 run-rate (management said 'we will try' to sustain growth).
Finance costs expected to moderate in FY27 as IPO proceeds repay high-cost borrowings.
Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business across quarters, and what explains the Q1 volume jump over Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no real consumption seasonality, but monsoon is challenging (wet fuel, flooded industrial clusters). Q1 volume growth was attributed to chemical and pharma demand recovering and repeat customers.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the 345 TPH capacity is contracted, and can customers terminate contracts early?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of the 345 TPH installed capacity is tied up under contracts. Tenure ranges 1 to 10 years with non-exit clauses, and management said customers rarely move to captive boilers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value proposition to win customers from competitors or in-house boilers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is generally no competitor in most geographies. Claimed cost saving versus captive furnace oil, LDO or natural gas is 25% to 35%, while coal-fired large textile users may be only at par.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed to reach 705 TPH and when will projects go live?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crore more for the four under-construction projects, targeted to go live in FY27. Another INR170 crore over 15-18 months for IPO-funded and Tarapur projects; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28, Dahej/Ankleshwar/Panoli by Q1 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is utilisation of 41% consistent with the planned ramp, and where does the company target it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 60%-65% utilisation; newer boilers are expected to run at about 50% in initial months after commissioning. Some capacity is held back for 2-3 years of new demand.

qa_highlights.question: What are receivable days and CFO to EBITDA ratio, and what are the related-party steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing?
qa_highlights.answer: Fortnightly billing with payments typically 7th to 15th day. Operating cash flow was about 1.2 times EBITDA last time, expected to hold or be slightly lower. Steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing for the Sachin location continue for at least the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected on the Una project and what is the revenue-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 8%-10% clear margin per ton, passed through to end consumers, with no capex. The 9% revenue share to Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd is to be recovered from steam customers. Agreement not yet signed.

qa_highlights.question: What is a sustainable volume growth rate and can company-level 20%-25% volume growth be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5%-10% growth at existing locations, with new capacity adding further. CFO said 20%-25% company-level volume growth is achievable 'very comfortably'.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR1,000 EBITDA per ton sustainable, and what about Q2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 is expected to hold for the next few quarters, with Q2 an exception due to monsoon. Structural changes cited: coal purchases moved from credit to cash, solar power installed, inventory optimisation. Full-year to be at par or better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there government interest in community boilers and are more such opportunities in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to Bulk Drug Park and PM MITRA Park schemes from 2021-22 and a March 2024 CPCB guideline pushing SMEs to common boilers. Gujarat Bulk Drug Park tender is live; PM MITRA and Textile Ministry discussions are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steam revenue rise 46% when volume rose 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation improved from better utilisation and asset leverage, plus higher waste-to-energy usage at Vapi. Growth also came from chemical and pharma recovery and new tyre and food processing (Haldia) customers.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital guidance and cash purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive. Coal was bought on credit until May 2026 and has since moved entirely to cash purchases, which management said lowers fuel cost.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split between own-generated and traded steam, and margin split by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Own-boiler steam was 73.7% of Q1 revenue and traded steam 22.2%. Management declined to split margins between generation and trading, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA CAGR guidance of 30%-35% going to be beaten?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to maintain the Q1 growth momentum for the full year on both EBITDA and revenue, but said 'We are not saying that we will maintain'.

risks_watch: Utilisation is still 41.40% versus a 60%-65% target; newer boilers ramp only to about 50% in initial months, so margin expansion depends on execution.
Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore; IPO proceeds are expected to reduce high-cost debt, but the timing and extent of finance-cost moderation need tracking.

544914|2026-09.headline: Steamhouse Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.4% to INR128 crore and EBITDA rose 73% YoY to INR24.68 crore, but both fell sequentially from Q1.
544914|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 steam sales were 3,01,642 tons, up 12.06% YoY but down about 1.36% QoQ, with monsoon conditions and one steam supplier's shutdown cited as drags. Revenue from operations was INR128 crore (up 2.4% YoY) and EBITDA was INR24.68 crore, with margin at 19.28% against 11.39% a year earlier. Sequentially, EBITDA fell from INR30.93 crore in Q1 and EBITDA per ton declined, which management attributed to monsoon-related fuel wetness, transmission losses and cost movements. H1 FY27 steam sales rose 14.35% YoY, and management reiterated 25% FY27 volume growth and 35% growth in FY28, with an EBITDA per ton target of INR1,100-1,200 for the next full year.

segments.name: Steam generation and distribution
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue from steam generation and distribution was INR96.97 crore; steam distribution contributed INR25.56 crore. Own generation was 2,31,775.59 tons and steam purchase/distribution was 69,866.67 tons in Q2.

segments.name: Nitrogen and other
segments.commentary: Balance of Q2 revenue (about INR5.5 crore) came from nitrogen and other items; nitrogen is billed per nm3 per hour, not per ton. A 750 nm3/hour PSA plant at Ankleshwar is expected by end-CY2026.

FY28 volume growth expected to be upwards of 35%, driven by new facilities and customers added in FY27.
Next full year EBITDA per ton guided at INR1,100-1,200, supported by waste-to-steam facilities; Q3 and Q4 expected to be significantly higher than Q2 as the dry season reduces fuel losses.
Quarterly interest cost guided to be a little below the approx INR6 crore run-rate in Q3, as IPO proceeds repaid part of the debt raised in Q1.
Jhagadia steam sales expected to start in November 2026; Nandesari and Vapi waste-to-steam plants expected in H2 FY27; a third waste-to-steam plant expected in the next calendar year.
capex_capacity: Jhagadia: about 14.8 tons per hour contracted out of 30 tons per hour planned; commissioning expected imminently.

Nandesari and Vapi expansions progressing; Vapi is about 7-8 km from existing facility and includes a roughly 1.5 km pipeline. Tarapur and Pirana under construction (Pirana targeting textile cluster in Ahmedabad).

Una (Himachal Pradesh) community boiler: 300 tons per hour, EPC mandate of about INR311 crore incl. GST plus long-term O&M; funded by Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Limited; pricing still under negotiation.
Waste-to-steam capex is about 1.5x-1.75x coal-fired projects on a like-for-like capacity basis, with opex about 50-55% lower; management cites a 2.5-3.5 year payback after stabilisation.
Capacity utilisation: 42.41% in Q2 FY27 vs 35.28% in Q2 FY26 and 41.40% in Q1 FY27; H1 FY27 at 41.91% vs 37.03%.
demand_pricing: Steam volumes grew 14.35% YoY in H1 FY27 to 6,07,459 tons (5,31,240 tons in H1 FY26); 99.48% of H1 FY27 revenue came from repeat customers.
Steam prices were raised about 17-18% from Q1 to Q2 and the pass-through of coal price changes is contractual, with a lag of around 15 days.
Fuel: imported Indonesian 4,200 GCV coal at about INR10,000-10,500 per ton as of the call, up from INR9,000-10,000 earlier and a temporary INR10,500-11,000 peak at end-September.
New sectors being added include food processing and adhesives, on top of the chemical, agrochemical and pharma base; Narol textile cluster targeted via Pirana.
Management said it is evaluating a large waste-based steam project in Sachin GIDC targeting the textile cluster, which is price sensitive.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected for H2 FY27 and FY28 based on current contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 25% volume growth over 10.66 lakh tons in FY26; FY28 volume growth is expected to be upwards of 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton fall from about INR1,000 to about INR818 QoQ, and what is coal cost and interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop to monsoon-related wet coal, higher transmission losses and cost movements; coal is a pass-through. Quarterly interest expected to be slightly below about INR6 crore in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA per ton is expected from the Himachal Pradesh (Una) EPC project given the 9% government revenue share and imported coal transport?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing and markup are still under negotiation; margins will be lower than the current model as no capex is on the books, though PBT is expected to be broadly in line.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% volume growth realistic given Q2 margin decline, and what EBITDA margin is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on track for both volume growth and EBITDA margin, and reiterated that Q2 is a seasonally soft quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How do trade payables and negative operating cash flow look going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade payables were largely cleared early using IPO money to earn cash discounts; payables are expected to remain in single digits, so operating cash flow should normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the penalty clauses for supply shortfalls?
qa_highlights.answer: Most agreements are supply-subject-to-availability with no penalty; some have quarterly minimum guarantees (for example 60% of contracted capacity), and no penalty has been paid historically.

risks_watch: Q3 and Q4 delivery of the guided EBITDA per ton ramp depends on waste-to-steam plant commissioning timelines (Jhagadia, Nandesari, Vapi and a further plant next calendar year).
Volume growth needs H2 FY27 to grow about 35% over H1; any further supplier shutdown or monsoon disruption would slow this.
Coal price pass-through lag (about 15 days) and an enlarged gap between steam revenue growth and volume growth can distort margins.

Himachal Pradesh project: offtake is not committed by the government and pricing is still under negotiation.

544916|2026-06.headline: MPi H1 FY27 revenue rose 40.3% to INR 849.4 crore and PAT 45.4% to INR 158.6 crore, while Q2 operational EBITDA margin fell to 30.5%.

Emerging businesses grew 92% in H1 and reached 34.5% of revenue, while core business grew 23%. Operational EBITDA rose 17.5% in Q2 to INR 131.3 crore, with margin at 30.5%, held back by forex, input costs and freight. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-35% and a 25% CAGR for FY27-29.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 EBITDA margin rise sequentially while emerging revenue fell QoQ, and what is the H2 pipeline for exports and metal cards?

qa_highlights.answer: PSU contracts are fixed for 2-3 years (sometimes 5) with force majeure renegotiation. Private banks, cooperative banks and fintechs can be renegotiated. Management said pricing factors in variances.

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight cost roughly double YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight is a direct cost tied to the integrated logistics business, which delivers cards end-to-end to customer beneficiaries. It rises with bundled service volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why has depreciation risen sharply, and will it normalise?

qa_highlights.question: What are the UK and US opportunities and timelines?

544921|2026-06.headline: Arcil Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 107% to INR143 crores on INR1,066 crores recoveries (up 151%), with acquisitions seasonally light at INR353 crores.

AUM was INR19,574 crores (up 16% YoY) and borrowings fell sequentially to INR1,100 crores, with management expecting to draw down more in the coming quarters. 544949|2026-09.headline: Swastika Infra H1 FY27 revenue INR207 crores (+5% YoY), Q2 revenue +42% to INR188 crores; unexecuted order book about INR1,420 crores.
544949|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's maiden analyst call after listing on NSE and BSE. Q2 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR188 crores, EBITDA 62% to INR27 crores and PAT 75% to INR16 crores, while H1 revenue grew only 5% after a weak Q1 that management attributed to component price volatility and supply uncertainty. Management said it went slow in Q1 as a prudent measure and has since geared up. Unexecuted order book is about INR1,420 crores (2.8x FY26 revenue), including a roughly INR600 crore Maharashtra order won in late Q2 with a two-year execution period. Management guided FY27 full-year growth in line with FY26, with H2 seasonally heavier.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: About 85% of the unexecuted order book, per management. Includes substation, underground cabling, RMU and related works bundled into single orders.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: About 8% of the unexecuted order book; a segment entered in roughly the last one and a half years. A BESS tender has also been quoted.

segments.name: Transmission
segments.commentary: About 6% of the unexecuted order book; a segment entered in roughly the last one and a half years. Management said transmission has longer site-readiness lags (RoW, component availability) than distribution.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year growth expected to be in line with FY26, per management qualitative guidance; H2 seasonally heavier.

Year-end FY27 order book targeted at about INR1,500-2,000 crores, dependent on wins in two to three new states, with bids of about INR1,000-1,500 crores planned and a historical success rate of about 30%.
EBITDA margin expected to normalise to around 14% on a full-year basis; no exact quantitative guidance given.
Expected closure of an INR325 crore order within about two months.
Management expects EBITDA growth of 1-2% going forward, with growth in turnover, EBITDA and PAT broadly maintained over the next five years.
capex_capacity: Operates across nine states: Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Maharashtra, Goa, West Bengal and Assam.
Plans to enter two to three more states, with bids expected in Q3 FY27.
Historically, the last quarter contributes about 40% of annual turnover; management said about INR200 crores was done in H1 and another INR200 crores is expected in the next quarter.
Company has said underground cabling is only about 20% complete nationally, with future growth expected in Tier B and C cities.
demand_pricing: Q2 margin improvement attributed to revenue mix: higher commissioning and erection work plus final milestone billings on completed orders.
Price escalation clauses with no ceiling are in tenders, with monthly back-to-back escalation from the funding agency, per management.
Major tenders are funded by World Bank, ADB, PFC or REC, which management said keeps receivable days lower than peers.
Management said there have been no project delays or liquidated damages historically.
Bill-to-order-book conversion historically about 70-80%+ (per management).

qa_highlights.question: How much order inflow was added in Q2 and what is the guidance for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR900-950 crores of new orders were added over the last six months, including a roughly INR600 crore Maharashtra order at end-Q2 (part of the INR1,420 crore book, two-year execution). Full-year growth expected in line with FY26, with execution visible mainly in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin increase and is 14% the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin was a function of revenue mix, with more commissioning and erection work and final milestone billings. Management expects margins to normalise to around 14% on a full-year basis, without exact quantitative guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 decline and what is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was weak due to peak component price volatility and supply uncertainty, so the company deliberately slowed work. Management said annual working capital needs should be roughly equal to H1 requirement, as working capital eases in H2 with government budget clearances.

qa_highlights.question: How will finance costs be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Near term, IPO proceeds should reduce debt over the next two to four quarters. Longer term, the company is rated BBB+ and aims for an A- upgrade, and a shift from bank guarantees to surety bonds is expected to lower funding costs and working capital needs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order-book breakup and do margins differ by vertical?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution about 85%, renewable about 8%, transmission about 6%. Orders are typically bundled across substations, cabling, instrumentation and RMUs, so margins were not split by vertical.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is executable in the next 6-12 months and are there delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the historical bill-to-order ratio of 70-80%+ as the guide. No delays or liquidated damages historically; distribution has shorter site-readiness lags than transmission.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin is at risk from cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply inputs are protected by contract price variation clauses; labour volatility is limited. It pointed to a track record of maintained margin discipline over four to five years.

qa_highlights.question: Are RDSS and other schemes driving the pipeline, and how is the company positioned for digital and DER work?
qa_highlights.answer: RDSS is currently active only in Rajasthan and Gujarat; the Maharashtra order is ADB-funded and Himachal and West Bengal are World Bank-funded. RDSS phase 2 is announced, with tenders expected soon. The company is not currently pursuing SCADA or AMI work, but has quoted a BESS tender.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 revenue declined YoY; H1 growth is only 5%, so FY27 full-year growth in line with FY26 depends on heavy H2 execution.
Order-book growth depends on winning new tenders in two to three new states, with a stated success rate of about 30%.

Working capital and receivables: management expects H2 to ease working capital, but H1 needs are large and retention is only marginally changing. Operating cash flow relies on subcontracting, which is still being explored.
Finance cost: debt remains high, and the path down depends on IPO debt reduction and a credit rating upgrade.
Margin sustainability: Q2 EBITDA margin benefited from milestone billings, and management expects normalisation to around 14%.
Concentration in distribution (about 85% of order book) and in government-funded programmes such as RDSS.

544953|2026-09.headline: Moneyview Q2 FY27 profit rose 16% QoQ to INR 201 crore; management guides FY27 PAT above INR 800 crore.
544953|2026-09.overview: First earnings call as a listed company covered Q2 and H1 FY27. Disbursals rose 7% QoQ to INR 7,701 crore and managed AUM closed near INR 23,900 crore. Total income grew 8% QoQ to INR 1,146 crore and PAT rose 16% to INR 201 crore, with pre-tax margin widening from 21% to 23% of total income. Management said asset quality was stable, with September collection efficiency at 98.64% and October similar, and reiterated a full-year top-line growth target of around 40%.

segments.name: Platform / partnership business (LSP model)
segments.commentary: About 75% of loan capital comes from lending partners; about 17 partnerships live, with no single partner above 13%-14% of platform capital and the largest at 10%-11%. Management said partner margins rose about 7%-8% YoY, supporting revenue growth faster than AUM.

segments.name: Own NBFC
segments.commentary: Provides about 25% of capital. INR 250 crore of IPO proceeds was downstreamed to the NBFC in October 2026. Management said cost of capital is falling and the NBFC is one of the largest partners on the platform.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT expected to exceed INR 800 crore (profit growth above 100% on a normalised basis versus FY26), per CEO and CFO.
Full-year top-line growth targeted at at least around 40%.
Opex to income expected to keep improving in H2 FY27 and beyond, driven by collections, CAC and tech/AI efficiencies.
Credit cost target to stay within 5% of average AUM near term; management expects it at about 4.9% and to keep improving over the long term.
Ongoing ROE expected around 30% once IPO equity is deployed; margin of about 23.5% to be maintained and improved.
Rating upgrade discussions with agencies underway; further cost-of-borrowing reduction expected over the next year as the rating benefits flow through.
capex_capacity: INR 250 crore of IPO proceeds downstreamed into the NBFC in October 2026; balance of the INR 750 crore IPO money held at the platform.
Management does not plan to use IPO proceeds to repay debt; intends to lever the added NBFC equity to raise more debt.
Credit rating was upgraded last year from BBB to A- with positive outlook; management is in talks with agencies on a further upgrade.
demand_pricing: Management said the festive season shows strong momentum in disbursals, collections and operating efficiency, and expects current growth rates to continue.

Digital personal loans are projected to grow 26%-27% a year through FY31; digital share of unsecured personal loans was about 15% in FY26. Personal loan market expected at INR 33-36 lakh crore by FY31 (industry estimate).

New customers: about 75% are sourced directly (roughly half organic, half paid marketing) and about 25% via embedded journeys with large consumer internet partners such as Airtel, Supermoney, PhonePe and CRED.
Partnerships contribute about 20%-25% of new business and about 10%-12% of total disbursals, per CFO.
About 65% of AUM comes from repeat customers; over 14-15 crore registered users, mostly tier 2 and tier 3 cities.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 shape up given H1 PAT of about INR 375 crore, and what are asset quality trends including bounce rates and 30+ DPD in Q2 and October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 PAT above INR 800 crore. September collection efficiency was 98.64%, October similar; Stage 1 at 94.6%, stable QoQ. Bounce rate and 30+ DPD numbers were not given in detail.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IPO capital be reflected in NBFC capitalisation and when will rating benefits show?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 250 crore downstreamed to the NBFC in October; balance held at platform. Management is in talks with rating agencies; incremental borrowing cost is down about 2 pp to 12.7%-12.8% in H1 FY27 versus 14.5%-14.8% last year.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the lower cost of borrowing, will IPO proceeds repay debt, and what is sustainable ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental borrowing is falling; average cost moved from 14.8% to 14%, expected to keep falling toward 12.5%-12.8%. IPO money will not repay debt but will support leverage. Normalised ROE rose from 29% to 31%; ongoing ROE expected near 30%.

qa_highlights.question: How are sourcing channels and partner concentration evolving, and does a rating upgrade help sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of new customers are direct and 25% from partners. Largest platform partner is 10%-11% (no partner above 13%-14%); about 17 partnerships live, adding 2-3 each year. Management said the rating upgrade helps influence partner cost of capital and sourcing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growing faster than AUM, and why did interest income lag AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue reflects higher margin share from partners, with partner margins up about 7%-8% YoY. AUM growth in the last month of the quarter was not yet reflected in interest income; management also cited better customer quality as the cause.

qa_highlights.question: What is CAC trend and credit cost guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CAC is 1.6% of disbursals versus 1.9%-2% earlier, with benefit from repeat and direct mix. Credit cost is targeted within 5% of average AUM; currently 4.9%, expected to hold near this level in the near term.

risks_watch: Credit cost at 4.9% annualised, up about 10 bps QoQ on annualisation; management targets staying under 5%.
Dependence on lending partners for about 75% of loan capital; diversification to add 2-3 partnerships a year needs to be tracked.
Rising competition for sourcing partners from mid-tier NBFCs, which may pressure partner margins.
Rating upgrade and cost of borrowing reduction timing remains uncertain; benefit flows to P&L gradually.
ROE optically diluted by IPO equity; normalised ROE to be watched as IPO capital is deployed.
Management did not disclose bounce rates or detailed 30+ DPD for Q1 and Q2; need to track in next quarter.

544959|2026-06.headline: Runwal Enterprises Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 3,400 million (from Rs 4,462 million) on occupation-certificate-based recognition, while pre-sales rose ~5% to Rs 4,835 million.

Pre-sales rose about 5% YoY to Rs 4,835 million and collections rose to Rs 5,754 million from Rs 4,993 million. Revenue from operations declined to about Rs 3,400 million, which management attributed to revenue being recognised only on occupation certificate and possession. Management said debt has been cut to about Rs 1,900 million external debt post-IPO and debt-to-equity has fallen from about 3 to about 1.5, with fuller benefits visible from Q3.

vs Rs 4,462 million in Q1 FY26 (decline)

segments.commentary: Sold about 0.35 million sq ft in Q1 at an average selling price of about Rs 14,200 per sq ft, up significantly YoY, which management linked to the luxury mix. Delivered about 1 million sq ft in the quarter against occupation-certificate towers.

segments.name: Annuity / commercial
segments.commentary: Runwal BKC (about 0.31 million sq ft GLA) and Nexus Runwal Garden City Mall (about 0.75 million sq ft GLA) expected to complete in about 2.5 years; mall rental could exceed Rs 100 crore in the first year after stabilisation. Annuity income is currently minimal.

Interest saving of about Rs 50-60 crore per year expected from debt reduction, visible mainly from Q3 FY27 results.
Launch pipeline active for the next 12-15 months; management aims to grow pre-sales about 25% YoY with corresponding launch volumes, subject to approvals.

Company will stay MMR-focused with no plans to expand beyond the region for now.

qa_highlights.question: Strategic priorities for the next 2-3 years and expected growth?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company issue stated guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna Kanodia said no specific guidance yet, but a general direction on growth (20-25% pre-sales) will be given while maintaining balance-sheet and margin health.

qa_highlights.question: Debt repayment plan and current debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said debt-to-equity fell from 3.1x to 1.5x and debt is now about Rs 1,900 crore external. Future borrowing will be limited and self-liquidating. qa_highlights.question: Where is the land for the data-centre monetisation and how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Shashi Bhushan said the land is in Dombivli (Gardens and My City, part of a 250-acre parcel); about 18 acres is being considered for sale. No transaction has been concluded.

qa_highlights.question: Lease income profile from BKC and Nexus mall?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said both projects should complete in about 2.5 years, with mall rentals possibly above Rs 100 crore in year one after stabilisation. BKC tenant is still being sought; a rental number is hard to give at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Launch pipeline and approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Shashi Bhushan said two or three projects await approval, including a Bandra redevelopment and a Marine Drive project, likely launched this year or early next year. Management declined to give launch guidance because approvals are third-party dependent.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the IPO size cut from Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said SEBI offered a one-time option to halve offer size for entities already approved, given weak markets; the offer was all primary (about 10-11% dilution), and bankers advised taking it.

guidance_outlook: Constant-currency revenue growth in the mid-to-high teens; management said mid-teens is a conservative baseline for FY27 and FY28. Currency gains would be over and above this.
EBITDA margin expansion of 150-200 bps per year in FY27, FY28 and FY29, taking margin to about 20% by FY29 from 14.1% in FY26.
Capex of about INR70 crore in FY27 and about INR70 crore in FY28 (INR44 crore spent in H1 FY27), covering vertical integration, automation, maintenance at the Sachin plant and some capacity addition.
Effective tax rate expected at 32-35% for the next two to three years, due to higher-tax geographies (Spain, Brazil, Germany) and loss-making subsidiaries without deferred tax assets.
Working capital days expected to fall by about 15 days over three years, to roughly 100-110 days from about 128 days; inventory is the main lever, receivable days already at 75.
Hydra Elevate already CDSCO-approved; Hydra next-generation valve and AVDC 1.5/TAVI 2.0 launch expected in FY27, possibly as early as Q3 and no later than Q4; PTCA catheters targeted for FY28.
EU MDR: Supraflex Cruz certified; Pipit NC and SC completed audits; Hydra and Cocoon technical files submitted, ahead of the end-2027 transition deadline.
capex_capacity: FY27 and FY28 capex guidance of about INR70 crore per year; INR44 crore spent in H1 FY27. Mix: vertical integration, automation, maintenance at Sachin legacy plant, and a small capacity component.

Management said current capacity suffices for at least 1.5 years, with capex unlikely to rise meaningfully above INR70 crore for the next two to three years. It declined to give peak revenue capacity guidance.

DES utilisation H1 FY27: 79% at Surat and 20% at Telangana (from 64% at Telangana per the analyst's reference). Balloon utilisation: 72% at Surat and 57% at Telangana. New drug-coated balloon line at Surat at 40%.
Surat PTCA utilisation fell to 72% from 97% YoY; management attributed this to inventory optimisation, as previously produced stock was converted to revenue faster than expected.
Gross fixed asset turnover was about 7x before the Telangana plant; management expects it to rise as Telangana ramps up.

Hyderabad (Telangana) technical sterilisation capacity of 9,000 for TAVI in the RHP was not shown in the deck, which shows 3,000 commercial capacity at 60% utilisation. Management said ramp-up of TAVI or occluder capacity is not capex-intensive.
demand_pricing: India: DGHS notification on single-use devices is a tailwind, mainly for PTCA catheters (Pipit SC/NC); implants (stents, TAVI, occluders) cannot be reused. Management does not expect it to lift the 9-10% industry growth to 15-20%.

Europe: TAVI market share about 1.5% (not yet 2%) in low single digits; management expects faster traction once Hydra valve and AVDC are launched. Europe is the largest addressable region for structural heart.
Pricing: broadly stable across all product segments, negotiated hospital by hospital in India, with competitive landscape, product merit and commercial team capability as drivers.

Trading (other products) is rising on IVUS demand after reimbursement in developed markets about two years ago; management said it is gross-margin-dilutive but EBITDA-accretive because SG&A is shared.

International: TAVI not yet approved in Brazil; Australia launched and Canada approved recently. Stents present in more than 70 countries; countries with commercial presence fell to 70 in H1 from 77 in FY26 due to distributor bulk-buying timing, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 capex plan and how much has been spent?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR70 crore guided for each of FY27 and FY28, with about INR44 crore spent in H1 FY27, split across vertical integration, automation, Sachin plant maintenance and small capacity additions.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin improve via backward integration, and what is steady-state EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No gross margin uplift quantified until processes are set up and cycles run; EBITDA margin guided up 150-200 bps a year, reaching about 20% by FY29, driven by European operating leverage with teams already in place.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate high?
qa_highlights.answer: ETR is around 35% because Spain, Brazil and Germany carry higher tax rates and some subsidiaries are loss-making without deferred tax assets; ETR expected at 32-35% for two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why do the RHP and deck show different TAVI capacity figures?
qa_highlights.answer: The RHP included Hyderabad technical sterilisation capacity, not yet commercialised, which the deck excludes; ramping TAVI or occluder capacity needs little capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the constant-currency growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-to-high teens, with mid-teens as the conservative baseline for both the current and next year; reported currency impact cannot be guided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital reduction outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 15 days of further improvement over three years, to about 100-110 days from about 128 days, mainly from inventory reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential on current capacity plus INR70 crore annual capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a peak revenue number, saying TAVI capacity at Hyderabad generates much more revenue per unit of capacity than stents and catheters, so no simple calculation is available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market share in Europe for TAVI, and how will Europe's structural heart business grow?
qa_highlights.answer: TAVI market share is about 1.5% in Europe; Europe is the largest structural heart market and growth is expected to hold or accelerate with the new Hydra valve and AVDC launch.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of trading/others revenue (IVUS, OCT, thrombectomy) and the impact of the Boston Scientific acquisition of thrombectomy business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give product-level breakdown, citing its no-product-guidance policy; trading growth was attributed to IVUS reimbursement tailwind.

risks_watch: Gross margin: H1 gross margin down about 170 bps to 74.3%, with trading mix and input and labour costs (quality investments) as drivers; vertical integration benefit not yet quantified.
Trading mix rising (about 25-26% of revenue per analyst) lowers gross margin; dependence on IVUS demand tailwind.
Product approvals and launch timing: EU MDR for Hydra and Cocoon pending ahead of end-2027; Hydra next-gen valve and AVDC launch expected FY27 but not yet confirmed.
Free cash flow slightly negative in H1 (-INR1.8 crore); working capital remains heavy at 128 days; inventory reduction is the key lever.
Currency: part of reported growth from European currency tailwind; constant-currency growth decelerated to about 16% in Q2 and 15% in H1.
Telangana plant utilisation is low (DES 20%), affecting fixed-asset turnover and the capital-light thesis.
Management disclosure: product-level guidance withheld; a number of key figures (e.g., peak capacity revenue, trading split) not given.
key_quotes: Quarter two FY 2027 was a record quarter for SMT, with the highest -ever revenue, EBITDA, and PAT.
On the current capacity that we have, it will be sufficient for at least a year and a half.
Unfortunately, since we are not giving product -level guidances, I will refrain from doing that.
Some of the other major products that are in the pipeline are a little bit further out, somewhere around the two to three years out.

545004|2026-09.headline: Jio Platforms Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.4% YoY to ₹40,475 Cr, EBITDA up 16.6% to ₹21,879 Cr at a 54.1% margin.
545004|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter reported after listing; management reported 542.4 million customers, 36 million YoY net adds and 9.1 million adds in the quarter, with 5G base at 300 million. Consolidated revenue of ₹40,475 Cr grew 11.4% YoY, EBITDA of ₹21,879 Cr grew 16.6% and margin expanded about 250 bps YoY, with management saying ~78% of incremental revenue flowed to EBITDA. PAT rose 13.7% YoY to ₹8,387 Cr, and EBITDA less capex was ₹15,449 Cr for the quarter (up 52.5% YoY) and ₹32,130 Cr for H1. Management framed growth around four pillars (grow, deepen, convert, build) and pushed a 'digital gateway' model, while explicitly not using tariff hikes as the main ARPU lever. Net leverage was 0.11x at 30 September; the call also covered the IPO (about ₹30,188 Cr of issue proceeds, 24.5x oversubscribed) and international partnership plans.

financial_highlights.change: Net debt positive after IPO proceeds

segments.name: Connectivity (Jio consolidated connectivity entity)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹35,307 Cr, up 10.8% YoY; EBITDA ₹20,505 Cr, up 14.7% YoY, margin 58.1%.

segments.name: Standalone JPL (digital services and other)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue up 23% YoY to ₹4,881 Cr, which management said captures the digital services monetisation not in the connectivity ARPU.

segments.name: Home broadband (FWA/UBR)
segments.commentary: Broadband homes reached 30 million, with ~7.3 million YoY net adds; roughly half of the base is fixed wireless access (FWA), and FWA drives most new additions.

segments.name: Mobility (5G)
segments.commentary: 5G customers reached 300 million (66 million YoY adds, 15 million QoQ); Jio holds 51% of wireless broadband subscribers and 60% of the 5G subscriber base.

guidance_outlook: Management said capex peak is behind it and capex for the next four to five years is not expected to exceed last year's level, so free cash flow should grow.
Dividends were not committed; management said growth is the priority and the first year as a listed company will be used to learn before deciding on payouts.
International: management targets 10 to 15 sizeable partners (not niche markets), using a managed-service, asset-light model rather than hardware or SaaS sales; no timing given.
Management said the Gemini offer's initial term is 18 months and it has not yet reached 12 months; no decision yet on charging after expiry.
Tariff increases: management said no decision yet and ARPU is not the only lever; timing will depend on market and macro conditions.
capex_capacity: 5G standalone investment is complete; management said capex for the next four to five years will not exceed FY27-level spend.
UBR (unlicensed broadband radio) home broadband stack has gone through four generations in about three years; management estimates a lead of at least 2.5 to 3 years over the nearest competitor.
Unlicensed UBR cost per user is about $3 against ARPU of about $6, per management, supporting the high-to-low ARPU market strategy.
Management said no incremental spectrum or capex is needed to convert the 4G base to 5G, per the call.
Radisys (already owned) is the existing channel for technology supply to operators, cited as the model for partnerships without direct competition.
demand_pricing: Management sees 340 million new mobility users (240 million from 2G users with other operators, ~100 million from demographic additions over five years).
Fixed broadband penetration is ~20% of ~330 million homes (~64 million connected); management targets ~46% by FY2031 and sees 150 million as a potential fixed broadband opportunity.
Digital economy target of $1.4 trillion cited; 80 million small merchants and 350,000 leased lines are cited as enterprise opportunities.
Digital services: Gemini voice AI usage rose from 2 minutes to over 7 minutes; home subscribers pay about 15% more for 13 OTT apps bundled, per management.
Competition: management said Jio's FWA base is 2x the nearest operator and it expects 5G adds to be driven by 4G-to-5G migration and share gains from other operators.

qa_highlights.question: Go-to-market for digital services, scale expected over 2-3 years, and international partnership timing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital revenue will come from enterprise, home and mobility; partnership talks are two-way, with equal engagement on UBR and full OSS/BSS stack; no timing was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why there is no converged single bill for connectivity and digital services.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is focusing on converged go-to-market and one bill, but said that story is still to play out.

qa_highlights.question: Free cash flow, dividends and capex intensity given the asset-light model.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said capex has peaked and will not exceed last year's level for four to five years; management said growth is the priority and dividends will be considered after the first listed year.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff hikes and ARPU, given about 2.5 years since last hike.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tariffs depend on several factors and it will decide at the right time; ARPU rose 3.5% YoY organically, and the focus is digital services realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Conflict of interest in international partnerships, given Jio's own connectivity business.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not give technology to domestic players, will avoid competing with partners, and the Radisys model is the reference for partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: AI monetisation (token charges) and Gemini pricing after free period.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Gemini deal runs 18 months, is not near expiry, and that AI will be offered via the telecom harness to the full base; no token charging decided.

qa_highlights.question: Starlink and satellite competition in India and the US.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said satellite direct-to-device capacity is far lower than terrestrial (about 20 kbps per sq km), that Jio covers 99% of India's homes, and that it plans its own LEO system as a complement.

qa_highlights.question: Financial metrics that management wants to hit over five to seven years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a single number and said it will track market share, deployment, and ARPU uplift; it cited FY26 EBITDA above $8 billion.

risks_watch: ARPU growth relies mainly on mix (+3.5% YoY); no tariff action has been taken in about 2.5 years, and timing is undecided.
Digital services revenue is still small (standalone revenue ₹4,881 Cr); the monetisation case depends on partner (3P) adoption and Gemini economics after the 18-month free term.
International strategy has zero customers and zero revenue; partnerships are not yet signed and no timing was given.
Competition from satellite (Starlink) and other FWA players; management claims a 2.5 to 3 year technology lead, which is not independently verified.
Watch next quarter for: any tariff move, first international partner announcement, converged billing rollout, and dividend policy.

545005|2026-09.headline: Paras Healthcare Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23% YoY to Rs 511 crore, with H1 PAT of Rs 90 crore against Rs 44 crore for full FY26.
545005|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was Rs 511 crore, up 23% YoY and 8.6% QoQ, with H1 revenue of Rs 981 crore (up 25%). Operating EBITDA (excluding other income) rose 47% YoY to Rs 120 crore in Q2, with margin gains attributed mainly to material cost efficiency, formulary compliance and case mix. Group occupancy rose to 76.3% in Q2 from 62.5%, and new hospitals (Srinagar and Ludhiana) moved to positive EBITDA. Working capital absorbed Rs 172 crore in H1, with receivables rising from Rs 350 crore in March to Rs 518 crore, and net debt stands at Rs 620 crore after IPO-funded repayments.

segments.name: Mature hospitals (Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula, Darbhanga)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 8.5% in Q2 and 9.1% in H1; Q2 operating EBITDA margin 29.6% (up 360 bps YoY), H1 margin 28.9%; H1 occupancy 76.5%.

segments.name: Emerging hospitals (Ranchi, Jaipur-area unit as named 'Adepur' in transcript)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 27.2% in Q2 and 43.2% in H1; H1 EBITDA margin 18.3% vs 12.4%; H1 occupancy 68.6% vs 49.1%. Ranchi reported 25.8% margin in Q2.

segments.name: New hospitals (Srinagar, Ludhiana as named 'Vlampur' in transcript)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 139% in Q2 and 147% in H1; operating EBITDA turned positive at Rs 15.8 crore in Q2 (vs negative Rs 13 crore in FY26); H1 margin 18.7%; H1 occupancy 68.4% vs 27.8%.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue guidance given; management said trends can be used for modelling.
Long-term steady-state blended operating margin targeted in the mid-20s range; management said this is a playbook, not guidance.
About 200-250 beds yet to open (Kanpur wings and Ranchi), taking operational beds from ~1,500 toward ~1,800; Kanpur and Ranchi additions expected by end of FY27.
Gurgaon adds ~300 beds (golf course extension) and Ludhiana ~500 beds over the next 12-18 months, per management.
Operating EBITDA margin (excl. other income) expected to stay in the 2.8-3x range... (AOL figure) management expects this trend to continue.
capex_capacity: Capex of about Rs 90 crore in H1 across various units, plus payments for a new Gurugram-area unit (transcript: 'Gulbagh 2').
Dandhi (Darbhanga) has 435 beds; roughly half opened, with two more wings pending.
Kanpur: more beds to be opened by end of FY27; impanelments under insurance and government schemes completed.
Robotic surgery programs running at Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula and newly launched at Ranchi; liver transplant extended from Gurgaon to Panchkula and Patna.
Management said expansion would be asset-light; acquisitions are low priority given current commitments, though not ruled out.
demand_pricing: Group occupancy 76.3% in Q2 FY27 vs 62.5% YoY; H1 occupancy 73% vs 59%.
Kanpur occupancy rose from 22.7% in H1 FY26 to 78.4% in H1 FY27.
Srinagar occupancy 60.4% in H1 FY27.
Revenue mix H1 FY27: cash/self-pay 32%, insurance 24%, government schemes and PSUs ~44% (as stated in transcript, partly garbled).
Rajasthan state government scheme temporarily suspended across multiple hospitals including Udaipur; company says it has recovered 30-40% of state scheme business there.
Management says payor-mix shift toward cash and insurance is a stated priority, with marketing and tertiary/quaternary programs to drive it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Udaipur soft in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rajasthan state government scheme was reviewed and temporarily suspended across multiple hospitals in the state; Udaipur overall business grew in absolute terms and about 30-40% of state scheme business has been recovered.

qa_highlights.question: How has Kanpur ramped up?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy rose from 22.7% in H1 FY26 to 78.4% in H1 FY27, driven by new empanelments, more clinicians and a specialty-focused mix; Kanpur insurance and government scheme empanelments are complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital absorb so much cash despite profit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Rs 172 crore outflow to DSO rising from ~79 to ~92 days, from the 25% business growth, faster growth at new hospitals, payor mix and lumpy payments from certain peer groups; it expects normalisation as mix improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 50 crore item in other financial assets?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a long-term fixed deposit made from the Rs 80 crore equity infusion in April 2025, reclassified as other financial assets because it is non-current.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable margin for mature hospitals and how new hospitals should evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a lifecycle: new hospitals start negative, reach mid-to-high teens, then emerging, then mature at mid-to-high 20s; the blended steady state should be in the mid-20s, though no formal guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the low AOL-type operating loss per bed continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the operating loss figure has consistently been in the 2.8-3 range and expects it to continue, helped by case mix (oncology, radiation, robotics, transplants) and occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Is there headroom to grow occupancy in mature hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Patna and Panchkula have further room; Gurgaon is constrained, which is why the golf course extension is planned. Darbhanga remains a feeder to Patna while adding tertiary programs.

qa_highlights.question: How long will emerging hospitals take to reach mature margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said emerging hospitals typically take 4 to 7 years to move to the mature bucket; Ranchi already delivers mid-20s margins and may be reclassified.

risks_watch: Receivables build-up (Rs 518 crore, DSO ~92 days) and its normalisation in H2.
Rajasthan government scheme suspension and its effect on Udaipur and other state-scheme-dependent revenue.
Execution of 200-250 bed openings in Kanpur and Ranchi and the Gurgaon and Ludhiana expansions over the next 12-18 months.
Payor mix: government and PSU share of revenue, and the pace of shift to cash and insurance.
Gross debt of Rs 979 crore and net debt of Rs 620 crore; pro forma debt Rs 143 crore post IPO repayments.

570004|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% to INR1,800 crore and EBITDA about 7%, but a March raw-material shock cost an estimated INR200-250 crore of sales.
570004|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 consolidated revenue was about INR1,800 crore versus about INR1,750 crore a year earlier, with Hi-Tech up about 8% and plastics down slightly. Consolidated EBITDA grew about 7% and margin rose to 13.2% from 12.8%, with Hi-Tech margin at 19.8% versus 17.5%. For FY26, revenue grew about 11% and Hi-Tech grew over 20%, while plastics grew only 2.4%. Reported PAT was negative at about INR40 crore due to one-time deferred tax unwinding, a Labour Code charge and non-cash NCD unwinding; management cited adjusted PAT of about INR133 crore. Management says debt repayments due in September and March FY27 are to be met from internal accruals and government receivables, with refinancing and equity as backups.

segments.name: Hi-Tech (drip irrigation, tissue culture, solar agri pumps)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 8% and EBITDA up about 22%, margin 19.8%. FY26 revenue grew more than 20%. Domestic business grew about 12% and retail about 13%, below the company's 15%-plus target because of March sales loss.

segments.name: Plastics (piping, plastic sheets)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue slightly down, EBITDA up 3.3%, margin 10.2% versus 9.7%. FY26 revenue grew only 2.4% and EBITDA declined. Overseas plastic sheet business is doing reasonably well.

segments.name: Agro Processing / Food
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew about 6% but EBITDA declined. FY26 revenue crossed INR2,000 crore, up 9%, with EBITDA up about 9%. UK food revenue rose from GBP 60 million to GBP 68 million, with cost headwinds. Beverage bottling lines (juice and CSD) started in Q4; about INR27-28 crore revenue was booked by end-March.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 to be better than FY26 on revenue, margins, cash flow and balance sheet, though it called FY27 an uncertain year.
Company plans to be PAT positive (reported) in FY27, with positive EPS targeted from next year.

Management expects standalone operating cash flow to rise from about INR350 crore to INR750-800 crore in FY27, with about INR450 crore of government receivables expected to come down and about INR150 crore of government benefits.
Management expects the second half of Q4 to be better than the first half and July onwards to be better than before, if there is no new price shock.
Management said it would not give numerical guidance because of uncertainty, but said FY28 onwards will be focused on growth funded by internal accruals.
Food business expected to improve in FY27 with the end of UK and US cost and market headwinds, duty-free onion imports under India-USDA rules, and beverage expansion.
capex_capacity: Two beverage bottling lines (one juice, one CSD) started in Q4; about INR140 crore invested over December and March quarters, with no incremental working capital needed per management.
Discussions ongoing for 3 additional beverage lines in FY27, with investment decision expected soon.
Tomato processing plant with a Japanese collaborator expected to start around January 2027, ahead of the tomato season.
Alwar plant near Delhi in Rajasthan is being expanded to grow in North India.
Land sale in Tamil Nadu under MoU, expected to close in the next one to two months, per management.
demand_pricing: Raw material shock: PVC and polyethylene prices rose sharply between 20 February and 25 March 2026, with polymer prices more than 50% higher at peak (polyethylene about 60%) within about 20 days.
By late April-early May, PVC had fallen to about 10% above February levels, while HDPE/LLDPE remained about 40% higher; PVC demand has returned.
Farmers postponed purchases in March and April due to price uncertainty and lower prices for farm produce as exports fell.
Management attributes an INR200-250 crore shortfall in Q4 revenue to the March pricing shock; standalone Q4 revenue was about INR1,000 crore versus a potential INR1,250 crore-plus.

Drip irrigation sales FY26: Maharashtra about INR700 crore, South about INR400 crore, West about INR250 crore, North about INR88 crore (up from INR75 crore), East about INR107 crore (up from INR60 crore).

570004|2026-06.headline: Jain Irrigation Q1 FY27 revenue fell ~2.5% to about Rs 1,500 crore, EBITDA margin dropped ~2 pts, and adjusted PAT was about Rs 3 crore versus Rs 30 crore a year ago.

EBITDA fell on lower standalone India fixed-cost absorption, weaker Hi-Tech volumes and negative forex, while plastics margin improved. Management said April was weak but May, June and July improved, and it expects a stronger second half. Rs 164 crore of EBITDA was converted to cash at about 78%, and net working capital days fell to 183 from 210 a year ago. Rs 680-690 crore of NCDs fall due in September (about Rs 230 crore) and March; management says these will be met from internal cash flow with refinancing and other options in progress.

590003|2026-03.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported record quarterly net profit of INR725 crores and full-year profit of INR2,500 crores (+29%), with full-year NIM of 3.97% above guidance. Total business grew 15% to INR2,14,420 crores, with advances up 17% to INR98,754 crores and deposits up 13% to INR1,15,666 crores, though advances growth moderated in Q4 by conscious choice. Management flagged a shift toward preserving relationships over margins: FY27 credit growth is guided at 1-2% above industry, NIM at 3.75-3.8%, and ROA at 1.7-1.8%. Asset quality stayed stable with GNPA at 0.75% and a one-time INR163 crore prudential provision taken against geopolitically exposed sectors.

financial_highlights.change: Highest quarterly profit in bank history
Includes INR163 crore one-time prudential provision

financial_highlights.value: INR187 crores (Q4); INR744 crores (FY26, 0.75% of loans)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 includes ~INR200 crore Q2 chunky slippages
Cost of deposits down 13 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.value: INR679 crores (FY26) excluding INR139 crore interest recovery

segments.name: Retail advances
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 25% YoY and 3% QoQ, driven by mortgages (+56% YoY) and jewel loans (+61% YoY). Housing loans grew only 2%, and BNPL book stands at INR798 crores after a partner management change.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri book grew 19% YoY (5% QoQ) per the call, with agri jewel loans at 91% of agri and LTV of 55.59%; management also cites 5% growth for the year, which is inconsistent with the 19% figure.

segments.name: Commercial and corporate
segments.commentary: Commercial book grew 11.56% YoY but was flat in Q4; corporate grew 12% YoY, or 20% including credit substitutes (incremental INR969 crores). Growth focused on CRE, capital markets and EPC contractors.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: CASA grew 12%, adding INR3,290 crores vs INR677 crores last year; savings deposits added INR2,505 crores. Bulk deposits grew 9% YoY vs 44% prior year, and CDs of INR1,773 crores were reduced in March.

guidance_outlook: FY27 credit growth guided at 1-2% above industry growth, versus 18% achieved in FY26 (RAM and corporate mix 18-20%, with ~5% flex).
FY27 NIM guided at 3.75-3.8% (management also cited 3.7-3.8% on the call), with exit-Q4 NIM above 4%; drop expected from retail term deposit repricing from April 2026 and lower advance yields.
FY27 ROA guided at 1.7-1.8%; credit cost guided at below 1%.
GNPA below 1.5%, net NPA below 1%, slippages below 1% of the asset book, cost-to-income below 50%, LCR maintained at 115-120%.

Branch expansion of 50 branches in FY27 (38 regular, 7 lite, 5 to be shortlisted), front-loaded into H1. Investment yield enhancement of 15-20 bps via HTM rebalancing; duration to be kept around 4-4.5 years over the medium term.

Management sees no need to raise capital in FY27; profit ploughback to fund growth. Dividend declared at 130%, subject to shareholder approval, with the payout on a larger base after the 1:5 bonus issued last year.
capex_capacity: Plan to open 50 branches in FY27: 38 regular, 7 lite, and 5 yet to be shortlisted; front-loading into H1 to capture benefit in Q2.
Management says capital is not a constraint: CRAR at 18.76% with Tier 1 dominant and RWA-to-total-assets at 55-58%, with room to take it up to around 65% over time.
Loan-against-mutual-fund IT integration is at final stage, expected launch in H1 FY27; premium credit cards planned in FY27.
Digital: 98% of transactions digital; DLite app rated 4.8 on Google Play and 4.6 on Apple App Store, with 2.5 million monthly active users.
demand_pricing: Retail term deposit rates raised in April 2026; new products at 7.2%, with blended incremental cost seen at 7.2-7.5% as senior citizen deposits are 27-30% of total deposits.

Competition on yields has intensified from private and public sector banks; management said concession pricing has moved ahead and it may have to cut rates to existing and new borrowers to retain accounts.
Corporate lending: management chose to lean into BBB-rated accounts with gating conditions, with the stated aim of lifting RWA density, while acknowledging fierce competition for AAA/AA names.
Gold loans: jewel loans are 30% of the book against an internal cap of 35%; agri gold yields are about 10.75-11%, and management plans to cut pricing toward 9.5-9% to limit growth.
Working capital utilisation fell 2-3% across sectors in Q4, as customers ran down lines amid geopolitical uncertainty; textile is flagged as the most exposed sector.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 NIM guidance versus the FY26 beat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 3.75-3.8% for FY27, citing sticky deposit costs, leakage of existing customers to competitors, and the need to concede yields to retain top line, accepting some NIM compromise.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the competitive pressure on yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said concession pricing has moved and the bank has held rates, but it now must cut to retain good accounts. Retaining accounts is a priority over margins; Q4 yield benefit of 16 bps came from repricing of 25-30% of the book.

qa_highlights.question: What sectors received the INR163 crore prudential provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Textiles, ceramics, fertilisers, chemicals, granite and quartz, plus other sectors with direct or indirect geopolitical exposure; provisioning was set on a portfolio basis after sector reviews.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ECL transition and steady-state credit cost be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still reviewing the final RBI ECL guidelines and will share clarity later; FY27 credit cost is guided below 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 credit growth guided lower than FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank chose a prudent, moderated approach in a benign-but-volatile environment to avoid credit cost offsetting yield gains, with capital not the binding constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan LTV and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold loans are capped at 75% LTV for retail and 80-85% for agri, with margin of 20-40%; loans above 75% LTV are under 1-1.5% of the portfolio.

risks_watch: NIM trajectory: FY27 guided at 3.75-3.8% vs 3.97% in FY26, with the retail deposit repricing impact to be seen in Q1 FY27.
Yield pressure from competition and existing-customer leakage in corporate, MSME and LAP segments.
Geopolitical exposure: INR163 crore prudential buffer on textiles, ceramics, chemicals and others; West Asia conflict impact on input costs and working capital demand.
Gold price risk: jewel loans at 30% of book; management says a 40% gold price fall would not breach LTV buffers.
ECL transition impact on steady-state credit cost is not yet quantified.
Wage revision provision from November 2026 (IBA committee not yet formed) is not yet provided.
Deposit franchise: term deposit renewals of 70-75% in retail; the flow of new deposits may be insufficient, which may push up cost of funds.

Answers on capital, ECL and the wage provision were non-committal, with several deferred to later updates.

Now stage may come, we may not be able to maintain. In that process, there can be an exodus of accounts in a particular geography.
We have achieved an ROA of 2.1% in this quarter and 1.93% for the full year.

590003|2026-06.headline: KVB Q1 FY27 net profit rose 45% YoY to INR756 crore, but NIM of 4.26% and sequentially lower write-off recoveries (INR103 crore vs INR216 crore) weigh on the outlook.
590003|2026-06.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported Q1 FY27 net profit of INR756 crore, up 4% QoQ and 45% YoY, with NIM of 4.26% and ROA of 2.11%. Total business grew 16% YoY to INR2,27,267 crore, with advances and deposits each up 6% QoQ. Sequentially, operating profit fell 12% to INR1,096 crore and non-interest income fell 28% to INR442 crore, mainly on lower write-off recoveries and one-offs. Management kept the full-year NIM guidance of 3.7% to 3.8% but said NIM should be above 4% next quarter, and it will review full-year guidance at end-September.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in INR; growth 32% YoY, 5% QoQ
financial_highlights.change: Highest growth in 5 years per management
+41 crore QoQ (about 6%), including AS 15 retiral cost up INR47 crore
+1 bp QoQ; 4.34% incl. 8 bp one-off interest recovery

Management expects 42.5% to 43% as a likely near-term level

segments.name: Retail (RAM, 86% of advances)

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri portfolio grew 5% QoQ; agri jewel loans are 92% of agri book. Gold LTV is 63.7% for agri and 56.83% for non-agri.

segments.name: Commercial banking / SBG & BBG (part of 14% corporate balance)
segments.commentary: Commercial segment grew 6% QoQ, with business banking disbursements up 45% QoQ. Management said Q4 FY26 flat growth was an aberration and expects ~18% growth for the year.

segments.name: Corporate and institutional (14% of advances)
segments.commentary: Grew 6% QoQ on CRE, capital market participants and EPC/infrastructure; disbursements are at a 5-quarter high. Credit substitutes rose INR171 crore.

segments.name: Deposits / CASA
segments.commentary: Deposits grew 6% QoQ; CASA grew 9% QoQ, with current accounts up INR1,753 crore (+19%) and savings up INR901 crore (+4%). Retail households are 72% of deposits.

guidance_outlook: Full-year NIM guidance of 3.7% to 3.8% kept; management expects NIM at 4%+ next quarter, with full-year guidance to be reviewed at end-September.
Credit growth guided at 1% to 2% above industry growth for the rest of the year; management said it would be 1% above industry in RAM if system grows, and more cautious in corporate.
GNPA expected below 1.5%, net NPA below 1%, and slippages below 1% of loan book for the year.
Credit cost guidance of about 1% is seen as conservative; management said it could be much lower. Yield on advances expected to fall 10 bp next quarter, and cost of deposits to rise 5 to 10 bp.
Yield on investments targeted at about 7% by exit of FY27 (6.83% in Q1). Write-off recovery target of INR500 to 600 crore per year, though quarterly recoveries will be lumpy.
Cost-to-income expected to rise to 42.5% to 43% (from 41.74%) as about 50 branches are opened in H1 FY27 (25 by end-Q1 per management). Opex impact estimated at 0.5% to 1%.
capex_capacity: Opened 2 branches in Q1 FY27; target of 50 branches in H1 FY27, with 25 to be completed by end-June and the rest by end of H1.
Mortgage-focused branches raised from 144 to 175 this year. Small business group relationship model extended to 77 branches from 75.
Staff strength rose from about 7,000 to 9,500 over the past year; management expects more manpower to be added this year.
Loan against mutual funds product to launch by end-Q2 FY27; credit card relaunched for existing customers, with new-to-bank rollout planned in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Competition and customer retention are compressing yields; management said some customers want up to 0.5% concession and that it may cede accounts or lower yields.
Housing: bank is slowing growth because public sector banks are pricing at 7.5% to 8.5%. It had INR160 crore of housing disbursements where yields were above 8.25% to 8.5%.
Fixed-rate book rose from 29% to 34% of advances; MCLR-linked book fell from 14% to 9%; EBLR-linked book stayed at 55%.
Gold loans: average blended yield is about 11% to 12%, with agri PSL benefit possibly taking it to 11.25%. Gold loans are about 30% of advances, against an internal ceiling of 30% to 35%.

Deposit pricing: time deposit rates were raised 40 bp during the quarter to fund front-loaded advances. FCNR(B) pricing is at about 7%, targeting tickets below USD1 million; base is about USD130 million.
Textiles are about 5% of the portfolio and seen as the main war-related risk. Working capital utilisation is steady at 77% to 80%. Management said the bank has not seen SMA build-up as a result.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth stay 100-200 bp above system if system growth has moved to around 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay about 1% above RAM system growth, but will be more cautious in corporate to avoid repeating the earlier mistake. Corporate is now 14% of advances, down from 45%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SME YoY growth slow to 12-13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 was flat because the bank avoided pricing competition and some weak accounts. Q1 growth recovered to 6% QoQ, with commercial disbursements up 45% YoY on NTB plus ETB. Management expects about 18% growth for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS disbursement and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: In commercial, 2,232 applications were received on JanSamarth. INR140 crore disbursed, with INR10 crore in Q1. In corporate, 54 applied and INR80 crore disbursed, with 176 units eligible, of which about 100 may qualify.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan blended yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a blended 11% to 12%, with agri PSL benefits possibly pushing it to 11.25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bank pushing a higher fixed-rate book if costs are rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed-rate loans at 11% to 15% insulate yields if rates fall later, and 20 to 30 bp of cost increase is manageable.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about full-year NIM given the Q2 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 NIM should be 4%+ but full-year guidance of 3.7% to 3.8% is not changed and will be reviewed at end-September. Downside is limited, though a fall to 3.6% to 3.5% would be a concern.

qa_highlights.question: How will the normalisation of write-off recoveries affect ROA over the next 2 to 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lower write-offs could cut ROA by about 25 bp, not 40-45 bp. Offsets: non-fund income (TPP and guarantees), and 10-15 bp from CASA cost and 10 bp from other income.

risks_watch: Write-off recoveries are lumpy and fell to INR103 crore; full-year target of INR500 to 600 crore is at risk if recoveries stay subdued.
Competition and retention pressure: yield on advances expected to fall 10 bp next quarter, and cost of deposits to rise 5 to 10 bp.
Credit cost and ECL transition: management said the ECL impact is premature to quantify; a normalised credit cost will be indicated in about 10 to 11 months.
SMA-30 rose from 0.17% to 0.22%; slippage ratio is guided below 1%. Textile (about 5% of book), ceramics, logistics and the El Nino/monsoon delay are the main sector watch items.
Gold price declines and El Nino could affect agri gold loans (92% of agri book); management said LTV is 63.7% for agri and 56.83% for non-agri.

So that way, if we are going to move to 3.6% and 3.5%, that's a cause of concern. But we are not on the trajectory, and we are trying our level best to manage the portfolio, product mix, all these things and all.
it will be premature at this stage to indicate any normalized credit cost under the new region.
YTD growth, this first quarter growth should not be considered as an indicator for the full year growth at the same tempo.
